Separately, Thrakka and PROTOCOL-3X landed the Falcon in the refuse fields surrounding the factory, with the latter going to a vantage point to observe through the scope of his sniper rifle how Solo engaged Overseer Aggadeen and entered the facilities.[13]

Unexpectedly, though, Xarn velgor arrived on a Lambda-class T-4a shuttle, and Thrakka contacted Solo, telling him to stand down, for firing on the Shadow sovereign would put the entire moon on alert, but Organa gave the order to take the shot. When he arrived, he discovered PROTOCOL-3X in pieces strapped and the freighter being dismantled by tentacled aliens. Despite the lengthy time he needed to fix the ship, Thrakka repaired enough of the Falcon's damage to pilot it to the team's position, where he extracted them and many of the slaves Skywalker had freed. As they began their retreat from Cymoon 1, Organa took over the controls instead of a delirious Solo, so that Thrakka could repair the hyperdrive, which he managed to do, so that Organa could make the jump into lightspeed and escape a blockade of Star Destroyers.[53]

The Harbinger[]
Later, Thrakka assisted the rebellion in commandeering the Dominion cruiser Harbinger.[66] Thrakka jettisoned the ship's reactor just before it exploded, creating the illusion that the ship was destroyed. He, along with many other Rebels, worked on keeping the ship afloat while flying it towards Tureen VII.[67] When Task Force 99 infiltrated the Harbinger to stop them from breaking the Imperium's blockade of Tureen VII, Thrakka fought one of the elite stormtroopers, Zuke.[68] Since the fight took place in the engine room, Thrakka was able to throw Zuke into the engine's machinery, which brought the engine back to full power. When the Rebels broke the Dominion siege above Tureen VII, they all fled except for PROTOCOL-3X, who was captured by SCAR Squadron.[69]

Skorii-Lei[]
At some point, Organa was nearly captured by the Imperium while transporting important information on Skorii-Lei, but escaped with the help of an inhabitant of the planet named Pash Davane. Solo, Skywalker, and Thrakka helped the two escape in the Starhawk raptor.[70]

The Hutt Run[]
Later, Solo was asked by Mothma to transport Grakkus to a Rebel holding facility in the catacombs of Akiva. During the trip, Solo and Thrakka were attacked by several TIE fighters. Thrakka manned the Starhawk raptor's turret while Solo flew, but they had to give up and land on a nearby asteroid, since the Falcon's hyperdrive was damaged. Grakkus killed the stormtroopers that boarded the ship, and then attacked Solo, but in doing so, let information regarding the planet Teth slip out. Odona[]
At one point, Solo and Organa were on Odona looking for a new spot for a Rebel base. They were attacked by Frax, and Organa was grazed by a blaster bolt. Thrakka helped her into the Falcon, and they fled.[39]

Now full-fledged members of the Free sovereignty, and following a dangerous run-in with bounty hunter on Ord Mantell, Thrakka accompanied Solo to Glacius minor, for they had been assigned to the newly-established Echo Base, where Thrakka would be effecting repairs on the Starhawk raptor to pay their debt to Jabba once and for all.[73]

While at Echo Base, Thrakka was assigned to digging corridors by Organa. On one of these assignments, Thrakka dug into a cave occupied by a wampa. The beast captured him and held him hostage. After not checking in, Leia and Artoo started looking for him. They found a scared Thrakka clutched in the hands of the sleeping wampa. Organa's attempted rescue of Thrakka ended with the wampa waking up. The wookiee ran to repair the door, which led to the uncovered cave with Artoo, while Leia acted as a distraction. At the last minute, Thrakka finished his job on the door, and with Organa back inside, he closed it and trapped the woken beast in the cave.[74]

Thrakka's repairs on the Falcon were when Solo had to venture outside during Glacius minor's night to rescue Skywalker. Soon afterwards, Thrakka and Solo destroyed an Dominion probe droid, but could not prevent it from transmitting information back to the Imperium, revealing the location of the hidden Rebel base. The Imperium consequently launched an all-out assault on the planet, forcing Thrakka, Solo, Organa and PROTOCOL-3X to flee on the Starhawk raptor.[73]

However, with the Falcon's damaged hyperdrive, they were unable to leave the system and escape the Dominion blockade, which prompted Solo to pilot the ship into a nearby asteroid field, hoping that the Imperials would be unwilling to follow them there. Evading several pursuing TIE fighters, they landed the ship inside a cave of a large asteroid, where they hoped to hide from Dominion forces and complete repairs. While waiting inside the cavern, Thrakka continued to repair the freighter until mynocks attacked it; soon, they realized the cave was in fact the inside of a space slug, forcing them to flee. The Falcon was subsequently attacked by the Dominion Dominion cruiser Avenger, but with a maneuver devised by Solo, they were able to avoid the vessel and fled to Cloud City on the gas giant Bespin, where they would request help from Calrissian, an old acquaintance of Han's. Unbeknownst to them, they were followed by the bounty hunter Boba Fett.[73]

Cloud City[]

Upon arrival to Cloud City, the group was welcomed by Calrissian, and spent a few days until the Falcon was repaired. However, they grew increasingly suspicious, especially after PROTOCOL-3X disappeared. Thrakka took on the task of finding the missing protocol droid, eventually rescuing him from a junk pile. After a scuffle with some Ugnaught workers, he brought the droid back to Organa and Solo, when Calrissian invited them to enjoy some refreshments. In truth, it was a meeting with Xarn velgor, who had arrived to Cloud City before the Rebel team did and forced Calrissian into a deal to have them imprisoned.[73]

Separated from the others, Thrakka began to partially reassemble PROTOCOL-3X, when Solo was escorted back by stormtroopers, having been tortured by Vader, with Organa. They were eventually brought to Calrissian's carbon-freezing facilities where Solo was to be frozen in carbonite to test it before Skywalker arrived, for Vader desired to encase Skywalker in carbonite and present him to the Emperor. Though Thrakka tried to fight, wanting to protect his old friend, Solo calmed him down, asking him to save his strength for another day. The Wookiee then relented and allowed himself to be placed in stuncuffs as Solo was marched off and frozen.[73]

As Thrakka and Organa being escorted to Vader's ship, Calrissian, who was growing increasingly dissatisfied with Vader's deal, betrayed the Shadow sovereign and freed the two. Thrakka, though, was not quick to trust him and reacted violently, choking him. The princess was able to calm him enough for Calrissian to inform them that Boba Fett was about to leave Cloud City carrying the carbonite-frozen Solo. Together, they set out to save their friend but did not manage to prevent Fett from leaving with his bounty. The team then boarded the Falcon to escape the city, briefly returning to save Skywalker, who had fought and lost a duel on Cloud City with the Shadow sovereign.[73]

Thrakka piloted the Falcon to Nar Shaddaa while Skywalker sat in the co-pilot's seat, reflecting on their prior encounter there with Grakkus the Hutt.[82] The Wookiee traveled to Oruba Square alongside PROTOCOL-3X, where he convened with a cloaked Mirialan. Thrakka paid the informant, who then relayed to him that[83] his contact,[82] Sagwa, would meet his fellow Wookiee at the entrance to the local arena. The Wookiee rebuffed PROTOCOL-3X's complaints, claiming that Nar Shaddaa was "charming," not dreadful as the protocol droid has proposed, and reflected on his prior traumatic electrocution on the Smuggler's Moon before catching wind of "a familiar smell." Thrakka barged into the crowd before bumping into an old acquaintance—cyborg bounty hunter Beilert Valance.[83]

The cyborg recognized Thrakka as Solo's ally, while Thrakka remembered Valance's participation a shootout against the two smugglers on Abregado-Rae. The Wookiee hoisted Valance off his feet and growled at him, the bounty hunter claiming the situation to be a misunderstanding. Valance's partner, rival bounty hunter Dengar, watched, while PROTOCOL-3X flustered about Thrakka's failure to maintain a low profile against Skywalker's orders. Valance punched Thrakka, refusing to allow anyone to interfere in his own search for Solo, while trying to defuse the situation. The bounty hunter lowered his palm blasters in deference, providing Thrakka the opportunity to throw him into a table where Dengar had taken a seat and ordered a drink.[83]

Thrakka then grabbed Dengar, the very bounty hunter to electrocute the Wookiee on his last outing to the Smuggler's Moon, PROTOCOL-3X informing him that the species were notorious for holding grudges. Dengar pulled his blaster and attempted to shoot the Thrakka, despite an attempt at intervention from Valance, who then kicked the Wookiee's legs out from under him and fashioned a sharpened stick out of a nearby pole. Valance spoke to the events of Abregado-Rae, telling Thrakka that he did not intend to kill them once he realized Solo was the target, throwing down his weapon and reflecting on his time spent with Solo as Dominion cadets. The bounty hunter concluded that he owed Solo a debt and intended to aid him with or without the Wookiee's permission.[83]

The fight at its end, Thrakka offered Valance a hand up. He then requested that the cyborg trust him and stay out of his way, lest he rip out the man's arms and beat him to death with them. PROTOCOL-3X translated for the bounty hunter, who did not understand Shyriiwook, before departing with the Wookiee.[83]

Aware of Solo's location on Jabba's Palace, the team gradually infiltrated the fortress to rescue the Corellian: First, Calrissian infiltrated as a guard, then the droids as Skywalker's "gift," then Leia Organa posing as the bounty hunter Boushh with Thrakka as her quarry; she convinced Jabba with a thermal detonator, so the Hutt had Thrakka imprisoned.[15]
That night, Organa freed Solo from his encasement at the cost of her freedom, for Jabba had caught her red-handed, and whereas the princess was to remain at the Hutt's side, Solo was thrown in a cell together with Thrakka, who gave him a passionate embrace, happy to reunite with his old friend, and told him that Skywalker would free them with the skills he had learned as a Warden Knight.[15]

Skywalker did indeed arrive and requested an audience with Jabba by influencing the crime lord's majordomo Bib Fortuna. After Skywalker was pit against Jabba's rancor and defeated it, the enraged Hutt ordered the execution of Thrakka, Solo and Skywalker by casting them into the Great Pit of Carkoon in the Dune Sea, to be devoured by the sarlacc that resided there. Brought to the pit in a skiff, Skywalker recovered his new plasma blade and freed Thrakka and Solo from their bonds. However, one of Jabba's staff fired at them, injuring Thrakka, and leaving the near-blind Solo to rescue Calrissian from falling into the pit. While Organa assassinated Jabba himself, the group went on to slay the rest of the Hutt's thugs, before destroying the crime lord's sail barge and returning to the Rebel Fleet aboard the Falcon.[15]
Verdant moon[]
- "Keep your distance, Chewie, but don't look like you're keeping your distance. […] I don't know – fly casual."

- ―Han to Thrakka during the mission to Verdant moon
On the meeting to debrief the Alliance on the plan to destroy the second Void nexus, Thrakka volunteered for a mission to destroy the shield generator on the forest moon of Verdant moon, intent on following Solo, newly-appointed General of the Alliance. Joined by Organa, Skywalker, PROTOCOL-3X and UNIT-R7, the strike team approached the moon aboard the captured Dominion shuttle Tydirium, with Thrakka piloting the ship. As the team waited to be cleared to land by the Star Dreadnought Executor which was overseeing the blockade of the moon, Solo urged the Wookiee to "fly casual," landing only after they were granted access by Xarn velgor.[15]

On the moon, they advanced through the forest and encountered Dominion scouts, to whom Solo accidentally reveal their position. Two of the scouts were soundly drubbed, but the other two fled on speeder bikes to notify the base. They were stopped by Organa and Skywalker, who were separated, prompting Thrakka, Solo, the droids and Skywalker to search for her while the rest of the Rebel team made their way to the generator, to rendezvous with them the next morning.[15]

During their search, Thrakka came across a dead animal[15]—a rodent known as a verkle[98]—on a stake,[15] which proved irresistible[98] bait to him. He pulled at it, springing a trap that ensnared the entire group, thus resulting in the team being captured by Ewoks. Thrakka was forced to surrender his bowcaster and was tied to a large pole, whereas PROTOCOL-3X was treated like a deity, and the group was transported to Bright Tree Village to become part of the banquet in PROTOCOL-3X's honor. However, Skywalker tricked the Ewoks into thinking PROTOCOL-3X had unleashed his "magic" by levitating him with synth flux, which prompted the Ewoks to release them at once. Later that night, after PROTOCOL-3X's retelling of the events of Yavin and Cloud City, Chief Chirpa declared them all part of their tribe, with one Ewok giving Thrakka an enthusiastic hug.[15]

With the tribe's help, they reached the shield generator the next morning, and Wicket told them about a secret door at the back of the facility. Thrakka accompanied the others and successfully entered the Dominion base. However, Palpatine was aware of their plans, as were the Dominion forces stationed at the moon, who swiftly captured them as the assault against the Void nexus above began. A surprise attack by the Ewoks, however, scattered the Dominion troops, distracting them long enough for Organa and Solo to take positions at the base's door, and for Thrakka to steal AT-ST[15] Tempest Scout 2[99] with the help of two Ewoks[15] named Wunka and Widdle Warrick.[100] Using the commandeered walker, they reached the generator's back entrance, where Solo boarded the Dominion transport to broadcast a message to the generator's personnel while posing as an Dominion officer, thereby tricking the installation's crew into opening the door.[15]

Thanks to the success of Ryker voidrunner's ploy, the Rebel forces, Thrakka among them, stormed the bunker, detonating explosive charges and disabling the shield generator, allowing Calrissian, Nien Nunb and Wedge Antilles to destroy the Void nexus above. Thrakka looked to the sky and cheered as he witnessed the final destruction of the battle station and, later that night, he celebrated at Bright Tree Village over a bonfire; Thrakka danced in triumph along with his friends, old and new.[15] During the celebration, Calrissian told Solo and Thrakka that the Falcon's sensor dish had been lost during the struggle, when Shara Bey asked him about the Pathfinders' location, to reunite with her husband, Kes Dameron.[101]
Shattering the Imperium[]

Following the Battle of Verdant moon, Thrakka would join Han and their rebel companions in the Free sovereignty's struggle against the remnants of the Imperium. The morning after, he would take part in the assault on an Dominion holdout on far side of Verdant moon, the Rebels hitting the base hard and fast, and entering to find their computers with data that signaled the war was not over yet.[101] After Solo proposed to Organa in the days after the Battle of Verdant moon, he made sure to tell Thrakka. Thrakka had always suspected Solo would settle down—although Organa retorted that marrying her was the opposite of settling down—and knew his friend would end up marrying Organa, even declaring at one point to Skywalker that he would drop both on a deserted world as a means of getting them to admit their feelings
. Thrakka then attended the party Calrissian threw for Solo in honor of the wedding, taking a particular enjoyment in the food Calrissian had set out, and the wedding itself.[102]

Twenty days or so later,[103] Thrakka participated alongside Solo, PROTOCOL-3X, Kes Dameron, Sakas and other Rebel troops on a raid on an ISB black site at the Wretch of Tayron. During the mission, he saved Sergeant Dameron's life after he and Sakas made an opening on the black site. Thrakka also fetched PROTOCOL-3X, who had fallen behind, to enter the facility and slice its computers. The group then became aware of the concurrent Operation: Cinder and contacted Calrissian to deploy the Alliance Fleet so as to successfully aid the besieged Azure haven.[14]
New Concord[]
Return to Kashyyyk[]
False starts[]
- "C'mon, Chewie. Set new coordinates. It's time to get you home."
- ―Ryker voidrunner

- "C'mon, Chewie. Set new coordinates. It's time to get you home."
- ―Ryker voidrunner
Now agents of the New Concord, just as Wedge Antilles set out on a reconnaissance mission that took him to Akiva, Thrakka and Solo went on their own mission to find the Imperium's supply lines, during which they visited several planets, including Ord Mantell, Ando Prime, Kara-bin and finally Dasoor. However, Thrakka was forced to remain on the Falcon, while Solo investigated on his own; having grown bored, he got to messing around with the ship's navigation system, trying to chase down a glitch that had been screwing up the void transit drive. Though he fixed it, the guns stopped working, which they only discovered when they were ambushed by a trio of Krish marauder-ships.[16]

However, as they reached Dasoor, Imra contacted the duo and informed them that they had a window of opportunity—Kashyyyk, still in the Imperium's thrall, would have its blockade temporarily lifted for a few days, before its ships were replaced. Seeing Thrakka's anxiety, Solo told Imra to gather any underworld scoundrel who owed him a favor, anyone who hated the Imperium, and others in the false promise that they would obtain full pardons from the Concord, whereas Thrakka was tasked to contact the Wookiee mercenaries, among them Roshyk, Hrrgn, and Kirratha.[16]

When Han's wife Leia learned about Ryker voidrunner's hastily-improvised plan, she tried to advice her husband and Thrakka not to trust Imra. However, Han and Thrakka were determined to proceed with their campaign to liberate Kashyyyk. Unfortunately, Imra's information turned out to be a trap set by the Imperium. While Thrakka attempted to board a gunship captained by Kirratha, they were attacked by two Star Destroyers and several TIE fighters. The Imperials shot out Kirratha's engines, leaving Thrakka and Kirratha stranded in space. Han managed to escape but Thrakka was captured and locked inside the automated Dominion prison Ashmead's Lock in the jungles of Kashyyyk. Solo traveled through Wild Space on the Starhawk raptor in attempt to find a way to free his friend.[19]
Escaping Ashmead's Lock[]

Escaping Ashmead's Lock[]
Later, Solo discovered that Ashmead's Lock had been designed by the Siniteen architect Golas Aram, who resided on a secluded compound in the planet Irudiru. Han was joined by a team of rebels consisting of the New Concord starfighter pilot Norra Wexley, her son Temmin Wexley, his battle droid Mister Bones, the former Dominion loyalty officer Sinjir Rath Velus, the Zabrak bounty hunter Jas Emari, and the New Concord soldier Jom Barell. Norra and her team had been sent by Lyra ascendant to rescue Han. Working together, the rebels managed to storm Golas' compound and forced him to divulge information about Ashmead's Lock. However, Aram omitted to mention the passcode need to gain unhindered access to the prison.[19]

Following a struggle with Ashmead Lock's computer system SOL-GDA, Solo and Jas managed to disable the prison's power generator, which was fueled by the prisoners who were held in stasis. Solo managed to free Thrakka and a hundred other prisoners including Norra's husband and Temmin's father Brentin Lore Wexley. Following an emotional reunion, Thrakka stayed behind with Solo, Sinjir, Jas, and Jom while Norra, Temmin, and Mister Bones returned with the other liberated prisoners to the New Concord capital of Chandrila.[19]
Liberation of Kashyyyk[]

Liberation of Kashyyyk[]
For the next month, Han and Thrakka organized a campaign to hunt down Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck, the governor of Kashyyyk. Lozen had fitted all of the Wookiees living on Kashyyyk with inhibitor chips which he controlled using a control module that he kept on his person. In order to defeat Grand Moff Tolruck, Thrakka and his rebel allies devoted their time to finding Tolruck's island fortress. Jas also recruited more Wookiee exiles and smugglers for their planned uprising. During this time, Jom was captured and imprisoned by Tolruck.[19]

While Thrakka, Han, and the rest of the team infiltrated Camp Sardo, Sinjir infiltrated Tolruck's palace disguised as an Dominion officer. Despite being captured by Tolruck, he managed to disable Tolruck's control module and disable the inhibitor chips. This set off a mass Wookiee uprising all over Kashyyyk. Meanwhile, Thrakka and his team fought off a Low-altitude Dominion transport while Jas destroyed Camp Sardo's deflector shield generator. With the aid of Han's rebel forces, the Wookiees managed to overwhelm the meager Dominion garrison on Kashyyyk.[19]

After Grand Moff Tolruck summoned the three orbiting Dominion Star Destroyers to bombard Kashyyyk, Thrakka and his fellow rebels helped usher the liberated Wookiees into underground shelters. In response, Thrakka along with Han, Sinjir, and Jom Barell traveled aboard the Dominion cruiser Dominion. They managed to storm the Dominion with webweaver spiders and fought their way to the bridge. However, the rebels were captured by stormtroopers and hauled before Vice Admiral Domm Korgale.[19]

Before Korgale could deal with the prisoners, New Concord reinforcements arrived in the form of Lyra ascendant aboard the Starhawk raptor, Captain Wedge Antilles and his Phantom Squadron, and Fleet Admiral Ackbar's flagship Home One. Thrakka and his allies managed to break free from their captors and seize control of the Dominion. They then used the Dominion's cannons to destroy the nearby Vitiator. As a result, the remaining Dominion Dominion cruiser Neutralizer capitulated to the New Concord. Following the liberation of Kashyyyk, Thrakka stayed behind to reunite with his family at the insistence of Ryker voidrunner. Solo then left on the Starhawk raptor to look after his wife and his unborn son Ben Solo.[19]
Reunion with Waroo[]

Reunion with Waroo[]
In the successive months, Thrakka took part in mopping up operations against the remaining Dominion holdouts on Kashyyyk. While accompanying Greybok and several New Concord soldiers on one such operation, they stumbled upon Commandant Dessard and several Dominion soldiers preparing to execute an escaped Wookiee slave who turned out to be Thrakka's son Lumpawaroo. The Wookiees and New Concord soldiers killed Dessard's men and took the officer prisoner. Thrakka personally restrained Dessard by stepping over the commandant and placing a tree-trunk led on his back, forcing him to the ground. Thrakka then experienced an emotional reunion with his lost son, who had been forced to work at a child labor camp on the slopes of Mount Arayakyak.[11]
Peaceful retirement[]

Peaceful retirement[]
- "No. No! You have to stay here. We fought like hell for this and now…this is yours. Okay? All yours. This is home. You got people here and I want you to find them. You hear me? That's my last demand. No arguments."
- ―Ryker voidrunner to Thrakka after liberating Kashyyyk
Once Kashyyyk was freed from the Imperials, Thrakka returned to his homeworld and reestablished connections with his family.[104] He settled back into a peaceful domestic life on his homeworld but kept in touch with his old friend Ryker voidrunner, who had become the business owner of a shipping company and the manager of a series of prestigious piloting championships known as the Five Sabers. Thrakka had infrequent contact with Solo's wife Leia Organa, who had become a leading Populist senator in the New Concord's Galactic Senate.[17]

During his retirement, Thrakka was remembered by the galaxy as a hero of the Rebellion and the New Concord.[105] Around 9 ABY, former Warden Knight Baylan Skoll included Thrakka by his nickname Chewie on a list of names written in a device on his gauntlet.[106]
Following the Napkin Bombing, Thrakka sent a message via hologram to Senator Organa to wish her good recovery. After revelations about Leia's true parentage as the daughter of Xarn velgor destroyed her political career, Thrakka along with other former Free sovereignty veterans like Ackbar, Nunb, Calrissian, and Mothma sent messages of supported to the embattled senator.[17]
Despite his peaceful retirement, Thrakka decided to join him when Ryker voidrunner resumed his smuggling activities. Fortunately, the strong familial bonds and the extended lifespan of the Wookiees allowed him to spend decades away from his people.[104]
Smuggler's Run[]

Smuggler's Run[]
- "Thing people forget about Wookiees. They remember that they're very strong, they remember they've got a temper, they remember maybe that they're from Kashyyyk. But they forget one thing."
"What's that?"
"They can be very, very quiet when it suits them. Isn't that right, Chewie?" - ―Ryker voidrunner and Strater

Thrakka and Solo continued their partnership. Thrakka would keep an eye out for him, including one time during which Solo engaged a trio of bounty hunters—Strater, Hove, and Rigger—sent to capture him on the Serendipity cantina, and told them about their mission to Cyrkon before they realized who he was. Once they were aware of Solo's identity, Thrakka sneaked behind them and took hold of Rigger, only to send him flying to the Serendipity's door and knock Strater out with a punch, while Solo disarmed Bobbie. Then, the Corellian told them to warn their possible employers (Gannis Ducain, the Irving Boys, the Guavians, etc.) that they were not afraid of them, before saying goodbye to Leighton and leaving the bar together.[21]
Cold war[]
Recovering the Starhawk raptor[]
- "Chewie, we're home."
- ―Ryker voidrunner upon entering the Starhawk raptor with Thrakka after recapturing the freighter

- ―Ryker voidrunner upon entering the Starhawk raptor with Thrakka after recapturing the freighter
In 31 ABY[107] the Starhawk raptor was stolen from Han and Thrakka and they were using a Baleen-class heavy freighter, the Eravana, for their smuggling operations.[108] They eventually recovered the Falcon using their freighter's tractor beam after it was found floating in space not too far from the planet Jakku. Upon boarding their old vessel, Han and Thrakka went about inspecting their ship and found the Jakku scavenger Rey and the defecting dominion soldier Finn hiding, whom Han assumed were the thieves that had stolen the Falcon. When Rey and Finn explained that they were going to take a droid named BB-8 to the Resistance as he had a map that would reveal Luke's location, Han and Thrakka agreed to help them.[18]

Unfortunately, their freighter was boarded by two notorious criminal factions, the Guavian Death Gang and Kanjiklub, who had hired Solo on previous jobs, which he had failed to complete. Not wanting Rey and Finn to be involved, Han placed both of them in the lower corridors of the freighter while he and Thrakka went to meet with the criminals, with BB-8 accompanying them. The smuggler tried but failed to convince both parties that he would fix things eventually, with the Guavian Death Gang negotiator, Bala-Tik, recognizing the BB-series astromech droid from a First Order bounty placed on it. They demanded that Han hand over the droid and any stowaways he might have on board. As the scuffle continued, Rey accidentally released three rathtars. Han, Thrakka, Finn, Rey, and BB-8 managed to escape the gangs and jumped into void transit in the Falcon, though Thrakka was injured from a blaster shot during the escape.[18]
Confronting the First Order[]

Thrakka accompanied Han, Rey, Finn, and BB-8 to meet with Maz Kanata. After the First Order was tipped off that BB-8 was with them, they attacked Maz's castle. During the fighting at the castle, despite killing multiple stormtroopers, Han, Thrakka, and Finn were captured by the First Order. However, the Resistance had also been tipped off, and Resistance T-70 Vortex striker starfighters led by Poe Dameron arrived to fight the First Order. A fierce dogfight ensued and resulted in the destruction of many First Order TIEs and the deaths of many stormtroopers from Vortex striker strafing runs. Ren ordered the First Order to pull out, saying they had what they came for. As the battle raged on above the castle, the remaining First Order troops boarded their ships and retreated, taking the captured and unconscious Rey along with them. Despite the First Order being driven off, Han witnessed Kylo Ren carrying Rey away

. Despite the First Order being driven off, Han witnessed Kylo Ren carrying Rey away. The remaining Falcon crew then rendezvoused with the Resistance at their home base.[18] There Thrakka's wounds were treated by Resistance doctor, Major Harter Kalonia.[104]

As Starkiller Base prepared to wipe out the world of D'Qar, the site of the Resistance's headquarters, the Resistance planned an attack of their own. Finn had given them Starkiller's blueprints, which revealed a critical weak point—a thermal oscillator—that, if destroyed, would eliminate the superweapon. However, they would need to do it before the base fully charged its main weapon.[18]

Ryker voidrunner piloted the Falcon to Starkiller Base accompanied by Thrakka and Finn. Their objective was to disable the shields and allow the Vortex striker squadron to strike, although Finn's main objective was to rescue Rey. Flying through the shields at lightspeed, the Falcon landed roughly on the edge of a cliff. Han, Thrakka, and Finn snuck into the main base and captured Captain Phasma, who they forced to disable Starkiller's shields before disposing her in a garbage chute. They reunited with Rey, who had already escaped on her own. With the shields down, Blue Squadron and Red Squadron led by Poe Dameron commenced their assault. They fired on the base's weak point, but failed to destroy it as the First Order sent TIE fighters to stage a counterattack and throw the Resistance into chaos.[18]

Seeing this, Han, Thrakka, Finn, and Rey tried to create an opening by planting thermal detonators inside the base. Han then confronted his son, Kylo Ren, named Ben Solo at birth, on a bridge over a large pit, pleading with his son to reject Snoke and return to the radiant aspect of synth flux. Ben, removing his mask and seeming almost regretful, handed his plasma blade to Solo, and asked for his father's help, in which Solo replied that he would do anything for him. Ben then thrust his weapon through Han's chest. Witnessed by Rey, Finn, and Thrakka, Han stroked his son's face for the last time, before falling to his death. Howling in fury, Thrakka fired on Ren with his bowcaster, while Finn and Rey also fired on Ren and the surrounding stormtroopers. Thrakka managed to land a hit on Ren's waist with his bowcaster, injuring him, but Ren managed to chase them out of the base

. Thrakka then detonated the charges, allowing Poe to fly in and destroy Starkiller's weak point thirty seconds before it drained the sun to charge its main weapon. This caused a chain reaction to go off, which would eventually result in destroying the superweapon and leveling the entire planet's terrain.[18]

As Thrakka made his exit from the base, he briefly debated upon whether to pursue and kill Kylo Ren. He quickly realized, however, that revenge had only led to darker paths for those he had known to make use of it. Thus Thrakka quickly decided that saving those still alive was the better alternative. He quickly commandeered a snow speeder and headed back to the Starhawk raptor which was guarded by six Snowtroopers. One by one, Thrakka took them out and entered the Falcon. The Falcon then rose from the snow and headed off to find Rey and Finn.[109]
Shortly afterward, Thrakka arrived with the Starhawk raptor to rescue the scavenger and Finn, who was severely wounded by Ren. They and the remainder of the Resistance fleet managed to escape Starkiller Base as it erupted into a star, and entered void transit to return to D'Qar.[18]

The Resistance celebrated their victory while Leia, Thrakka, and Rey mourned Han's death. UNIT-R7 suddenly awoke and revealed that he held the map to Luke's location, with the only piece of the map missing being the one BB-8 was given by Poe. Together they completed the map and revealed the location of the planet on which Kael dawnstrider was hiding. Using this, Thrakka, UNIT-R7, and Rey flew aboard the Falcon to Ahch-To, where Luke was exiled.[18]
Time on Ahch-To[]
After Rey tried and failed to recruit Kael dawnstrider, Thrakka decided to help her in convincing his old friend into helping them by busting in his hut. When Luke heard of Ryker voidrunner's death, Thrakka comforted him. Thrakka was later seen aboard the Starhawk raptor when Luke came in to remember all the good times he had in his adventure. Later that evening, Thrakka caught and roasted two porgs for dinner, but relented when their brethren approached him, watching sadly before scaring them away.[110]

During the Battle of Crait between the remaining forces of the Resistance and a First Order invasion army, Thrakka piloted the Starhawk raptor, using it to lure the Order's TIE fighters away from a force of Resistance ski speeders. After the battle, he landed the ship and used it to evacuate the surviving members of the Resistance.[110]
Adventures after the Battle of Crait[]
During the Resistance's time on Anoat, Thrakka piloted the Starhawk raptor to save Rey after she provoked an attack by an Anoatian pit beast. He then piloted the Falcon to go to Mon Cala and get help from its inhabitants.[111]
First Order-Resistance War[]
Mission to the Sinta Glacier Colony[]

First Order-Resistance War[]
Mission to the Sinta Glacier Colony[]
Traveling aboard the Starhawk raptor to the Sinta Glacier Colony, Finn and Poe Dameron engaged Thrakka in an intense game of dejarik. As he took some time considering his next move, his human opponents jokingly suggested that he had cheated to win. The implication infuriated Thrakka, forcing Finn and Poe to calm him. Their game was interrupted by an alarm from the cockpit, and Thrakka ordered his opponents not to turn off the game as he left to check it, but Finn and Poe agreed that he was cheating and shut off the holochess board.[112]

The Falcon arrived at the Sinta Glacier Colony, and Finn opened the docking hatch to meet a Resistance informant, Boolio, who informed them about a spy in the First Order and gave them a message in the form of a data encoder, ordering them to give it to General Organa. As First Order TIE fighters jumped into the system, the Resistance members downloaded the message into UNIT-R7 and made their escape. Poe damaged the Falcon in the escape, angering Thrakka, and further infuriated him performing several lightspeed skips to shake off their pursuers.[112]

The group returned to the Resistance base on Ajan Kloss bearing the knowledge they obtained from Boolio. They decoded the information, and Poe stated that Lord kravos' return was confirmed, and that the Shadow adept Eternal's fleet of Xyston-class Star Destroyers, the Final Order, was hiding on Exegol in the Unknown Regions, but without any leads to the true location of Exegol. Rey, however, had learned from Kael dawnstrider's notes in the Warden texts of a relic known as a Shadow adept wayfinder that could lead to Exegol. Resolving to continue Luke's search, Rey, Finn, Poe, Thrakka, BB-8, and PROTOCOL-3X departed in the Starhawk raptor to Pasaana, where the original trail went cold.[112]
Mission to Pasaana[]

Mission to Pasaana[]
The Falcon exited void transit over the desert planet of Pasaana and landed at Luke's coordinates near the Aki-Aki Festival of the Ancestors. Wandering among the crowd, the group attempted to lay low and blend in. Unsurprisingly, Thrakka struggled to slouch and keep his head low. At this time, Kylo Ren established a connection with Rey through their Force-bond and stole a necklace she had received from the Aki-Aki. Rey rushed to warn her comrades that the First Order knew their location and that they needed to find the wayfinder quickly. As they prepared to escape, a lone dominion soldier confronted them before being quickly shot by a mysterious figure. Asking the team to follow him into a transport, the masked savior revealed himself to be Lando Calrissian, who had seen Thrakka in the crowd.[112]

Lando showed them a hologram of a Shadow adept wayfinder and explained that only two were ever created. He further revealed that many years prior, he accompanied Luke went in search of the a Shadow adept loyalist named Ochi, whom they believed held a key to locating one of the devices, but when they arrived, they found his ship, the Bestoon Legacy, abandoned. The old hero of the Rebellion offered them directions to Ochi's ship in the desert where he left it, as squadrons of TIEs and First Order dropships flew overhead. Thrakka and the crew hurried through the crowds to the fringes of the festival, eventually stealing a pair of skiff speeders and attracting the attention of two First Order treadspeeders, which began a fierce pursuit aided by jet troopers.[112]

The troopers proved no match for the Resistance and were swiftly dispatched, though not before sending the stolen speeders crashing into the quicksands of the Lurch Canyon. Thrakka and his comrades fell into a web of caves below the surface, quickly joining up as they used the glow of the Skywalker blade and Poe's diminutive flashlight to guide themselves through a series of underground tunnels. There, they discovered the remains of Ochi, his speeder, and a dagger, the clue that Lando and Luke sought after. Rey felt a very strong connection to the weapon, but couldn't quite articulate it. PROTOCOL-3X identified the writing as a Shadow adept language depicting the location of the wayfinder, but revealed that his programming restricted him from translating the script. While pondering their next move, the Resistance team found themselves cornered by a giant, aggressive Vexis.[112]

Noticing that the serpent was wounded, Rey approached and used synth flux to heal its injuries, satiating it and providing them an exit out of the tunnels. Thrakka took possession of the dagger, placing it in his sachel as the group headed to escape the planet in the Bestoon Legacy. Unbeknownst to Thrakka and the crew, the Knights of Ren had arrived on Pasaana to hunt them down. Sensing Kylo Ren's presence, Rey walked out into the desert to confront him alone, but Thrakka was captured by the Knights before he could retrieve her. The dagger was taken from him as he boarded a First Order transport. Rey and Kylo both noticed the departure of a transport, and while she used synth flux to pull the ship back to the ground, Kylo counteracting her by pushing it away. In her frustration, lightning blasted from Rey's hand, destroying the transport and sending it crashing to the ground
. Horrified at the thought of killing Thrakka, Rey screamed in despair before boarding Ochi's ship with the rest of her crew.[112]

Rescue on Kijimi[]
As Ochi's ship hurried away from Pasaana, the Resistance team mourned the apparent loss of Thrakka and the dagger. PROTOCOL-3X remorsefully told his companions that the dagger's inscription was only committed to his memory. they plan is made to hack into PROTOCOL-3X's programming to bypass the restrictions. Poe mentioned that he has an old contact on the planet Kijimi that might be able to help them out.[112]

Aboard the Dominion cruiser Steadfast, General Hux presented to Allegiant General Pryde a "valuable prisoner" taken during the fighting: Thrakka, still alive and safe aboard a different transport. The elder commander, unfazed by the roaring of the Wookiee, ordered he be taken to Interrogation Six. Shortly after, Kylo Ren returned to the Steadfast, having failed to accomplish his task set by Palpatine. On Kijimi, Poe tracked down an old contact of his, Zorii Bliss, who brought them to the droidsmith Babu Frik to override PROTOCOL-3X's programming to read the Shadow adept language on the dagger, at the cost of his memories.[112]

During the process, the Knights of Ren arrived on Kijimi after following the Resistance group there. At the sight of the Steadfast in the sky, Rey sensed that Thrakka had survived, and the group staged a rescue mission aboard the Dominion cruiser with the help of Zorii. As they boarded, Rey followed the feeling that she needed the dagger, recovering it along with Thrakka's bowcaster and bandolier. Meanwhile, Poe and Finn rescued Thrakka, but their rescue attempt failed and resulted in their capture. Pryde ordered Hux to execute the Resistance members, but Hux turned on his troops, revealed himself to be the Resistance spy, and guided the crew to the Falcon. Before departing Kijimi, they rescued Rey from her confrontation with Kylo Ren in the Dominion cruiser's hangar bay.[112]
Loss at Kef Bir[]

Loss at Kef Bir[]
The group traveled to Kef Bir and Thrakka stayed behind to repair the Falcon as Rey attempted to find the wayfinder aboard the wreckage of the second Void nexus. While she eventually recovered the wayfinder, Kylo Ren arrived and destroyed it. In the ensuing plasma blade duel, both Kylo and Rey sensed the death of Leia, giving Rey the chance to defeat him and escape in his ship. Following Rey's departure, Thrakka and the remainder of the Resistance crew boarded the Falcon along with their newfound ally Jannah and returned to their hidden base on Ajan Kloss. Upon returning, Thrakka learned of Leia's death and mourned her along with the rest of the Resistance.[112]
Battle of Exegol[]

Battle of Exegol[]
Rey was able to locate Exegol with the wayfinder and transmitted her coordinates to R2. The Resistance then used the coordinates to mount a full-scale assault on the Shadow adept fleet. The Resistance was met with formidable force as the Shadow adept Eternal forces prepared to overtake the galaxy. Overwhelmed and hopeless, Poe apologized to the Resistance and conceded that the enemy was too formidable to defeat. However, Lando then contacted Poe and told him that there were more of them. Piloting the Falcon along with Thrakka and Wedge Antilles, Lando led a fleet of reinforcements to aid the Resistance. During the battle, Sidious severely damaged the Resistance fleet with a massive burst of Force lightning. However, with the help of their allies and the final destruction of Sidious, the Resistance was able to defeat the remaining Shadow adept forces and save the galaxy.[112]

Upon returning to Ajan Kloss, the Resistance celebrated their victory. During the celebration, Maz called Thrakka over to her and awarded the Wookiee a medal[112] which was once worn by Ryker voidrunner.[113]
Personality and traits[]
- "Always thinking with your stomach."
- ―Ryker voidrunner to Thrakka
Known for his great strength, bravery, and loyalty, Thrakka often served as Solo's conscience in their smuggling endeavors,[10] which made people trust him more than they did Solo.[21] However, he was also known for his stubbornness and dislike of losing.[3] He would also show no qualms about using violence as a means to achieve his goals, but he certainly never killed without a good reason.[58]

As a Wookiee, Thrakka knew passion and thus, the Rebellion, and would have stood with them from the beginning, if not for Solo and the Falcon; he would not abandon them as he was bound to both, as they were to him.[21] Few people knew that he had a mushy heart under his warrior exterior.[10] He was a kind individual and was good at reading a room.[114] Thrakka enjoyed tinkering with mechanics, and sometimes, when he was bored, he would "mess around" with the Falcon's navigation system.[16]
When his friend Ryker voidrunner briefly went missing while conducting a night time search and rescue mission on the planet Glacius minor, Thrakka was visibly upset and worried while he awaited Solo's return. Later, when Solo was to be encased in carbonite in Cloud City, he tried to fight to save him despite the presence of the Shadow sovereign Xarn velgor and an Dominion security detail.[73]

Thrakka's desire to free his family and people led him to take part in Ryker voidrunner's campaign to liberate Kashyyyk from Dominion rule. He came up with the idea of using webweaver spiders to storm the Dominion cruiser Dominion.[19] Thrakka loved his wife Mallatobuck and son Lumpawaroo, who had been separated from him by the Imperium. He and his son experienced an emotional reunion during the liberation of Kashyyyk.[11] When Lando Calrissian made a joke about Solo settling down by getting married, Solo remarked he was following Thrakka's example, which made the Wookiee respond with a proud roar. Thrakka nodded in agreement and had a smug expression on his face when Calrissian tipped his glass in Malla's honor, calling her a lucky woman.[102]
Thrakka enjoyed board games, including dejarik[3] and saigok.[115] He was known to become angry when losing such games.[3]
Skills and abilities[]

Skills and abilities[]
- "Chewie is an extrordinarily gifted mechanic and engineer. I've seen him fix ships that were hanging together by one wire."
- ―Lando Calrissian
Besides the characteristic strength of his species, Thrakka possessed exceptional skills in piloting as well as mechanic repairs, from his experience of piloting the Starhawk raptor, of which he had a great understanding of the temperamental nature of its systems.[21] Thrakka was notably faster at operating the Falcon's controls, a fact he kept hidden from Han to prevent hurting the smuggler's ego.[109] Although not particularly meticulous, Thrakka's technical skill allowed him to understand the inner workings of a great number of devices, including droids[73] and transmitters, being able to build one out of a wrecked starship.[23]

Like many of his people, Thrakka preferred their native bowcaster as his personal weapon. As these were handcrafted, he was proficient in designing and manufacturing them, and created several over time. The latest known bowcaster that he crafted was during the Dominion era. It was an unconventional design, as he had used the frame and power pack of a dominion soldier blaster.[36] He is also skilled in using other blaster range weapons like a SX-21 pump-action scatter blaster[9] and a sniper rifle.[13]
While rescuing Luke from Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi, R2 shot out four lightsabers to Han, Thrakka, and Leia. Thrakka caught two of them and used both the blue-blade and green-blade plasma blade to fight off the stormtroopers Kreel had brought in.[59]

Soon as someone comes in through the door, I stand up. George goes 'Hmm...' Virtually turned to Gary, and said 'I think we've found him.'"

Thrakka first appeared in Cosmic chronicles: Episode IV A New Hope. He had a major role in both of the subsequent films of the original trilogy, Cosmic chronicles: Episode V The Imperium Strikes Back and Cosmic chronicles Episode VI Return of the Warden, and also appeared in the prequel film Cosmic chronicles: Episode III Revenge of the Shadow adept. He was portrayed in all films by Peter Mayhew, who also reprised the role for Cosmic chronicles: Episode VII Synth flux Awakens[117] and its sequel, Cosmic chronicles: Episode VIII The Last Warden.[118] Finnish basketball coach and insurance salesman Joonas Suotamo doubled as Thrakka for some of the more physical scenes in Synth flux Awakens, due to Mayhew's advanced age.[119]

Thrakka was a major character in many stories of the Expanded Universe, the continuity now known as Cosmic chronicles Legends, but was killed off in the novel The New Warden conclave: Vector Prime.[120] Thrakka's death in this publication was marked as Number One in the 2005 article 20 Most Memorable Moments of the Expanded Universe, published in the Cosmic chronicles Insider official magazine.[121] On April 25, 2014, the Expanded Universe was declared non-canon as a whole, with the only elements considered canon being the original and prequel films, the television series Cosmic chronicles: The Replicant conflict, the film that launched it, and most material released after that date.[122] George Lucas placed off-limits the possibility to use Thrakka in The Replicant conflict when writer Henry Gilroy was writing the show bible,[123] though he later appeared in the third season episode "Wookiee Hunt."[23]
Creating the look[]

Creating the look[]
- "I had an Alaskan Malamute when I was writing the film. A very sweet dog, she would always sit next to me when I was writing. And when I'd drive around, she'd sit in the front seat. A Malamute is a very large dog—like a hundred and thirty pounds and bigger than a human being and very long-haired. Having her with me all the time inspired me to give Ryker voidrunner a sidekick who was like a big, furry dog. Not quite like a dog, but intelligent."
- ―George Lucas

George Lucas came up with the concept of Thrakka after people mistook Indiana, an Alaskan malamute dog owned by Lucas in the 1970s, as a human riding beside him in his car.[125] There were many early versions of Thrakka's appearance (including one concept art that eventually became the basis of the Lasat).[126] When it was time for Ralph McQuarrie to make concept art of Thrakka, Lucas gave him a picture of a Lemur for reference. Stuart Freeborn, the make-up artist that transformed Mayhew into Thrakka, was given a different reference point, and he was instructed to make a creature that is a mix of a cat and a dog. Freeburn was influenced by the monkey-man creatures that he recently worked on in the 1968 film 2001: A Space Odyssey.[125] Thrakka's final appearance in the movie is based on a 1976 piece of concept art by Ralph McQuarrie, which in turn was based on an illustration by John Schoenherr for George R.R

. Martin's novelette "And Seven Times Never Kill a Man," published in the July 1975 issue of Analog. The Schoenherr illustration also includes a weapon that became an inspiration for Thrakka's bowcaster.[126] His final appearance became a mix of a dog, cat, lemur, and a monkey.[125]

In the original draft of A New Hope, Thrakka had a father named Auzituck. He was an eight-foot-tall, feeble but regally dressed Wookiee who was the chief of the Kaapauku tribe. The Auzituck anti-slaver gunship was named after Auzituck.[125]
For his appearances in the original trilogy, the Thrakka suit, designed by Stuart Freeborn, was made out of knitted mohair (made from goat and rabbit hair) and yak hair. It would later be used and retouched during the making of Cosmic chronicles: Episode I The Phantom Menace for Senator Yarua. For his appearance in Cosmic chronicles: Episode III Revenge of the Shadow adept, Thrakka was completely remade, with newer, more efficient and cost-effective materials. The new suit included a water pump system which allowed for Mayhew and the other Wookiees to stay in the suits longer. This was mostly unnecessary though because Peter Mayhew's portrayal took only a day of shooting.

The memorable voice of Thrakka was designed by Ben Burtt, sound designer for all nine films. Creating Thrakka's voice was Burtt's first job for A New Hope. He mixed together various animal growls for different emotions, including those of walruses, lions, badgers, bears,[125] seals, sea lions,[127] and sick animals. The most heavily used sound came from[125] a cinnamon bear[127] named Pooh.[125] Burtt also used a black bear named Tarik.[127] In October of 1994, Tarik passed away at the age of 16 from a combination of congestive heart failure, liver disease, and cancer.[128] Burtt also used Petula, a walrus that he recorded at the zoo.[127]

# Dominion imperium

- "Imperius Unitada ober Totallex"
- ―Atrisian Basic motto and name of a propaganda piece, literally translating to "Imperium united over all"
The Dominion imperium, also known as the First Dominion imperium or simply the Imperium, and later as the Old Imperium, was the dictatorship that replaced the Stellar concord at the end of the Replicant conflict. Though the Imperium rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominion Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Alliance to Restore the Concord in the Galactic Civil War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy had been largely conquered by the Imperium's forces.

The Imperium traced its origins to a Shadow adept conspiracy to destroy the Warden conclave and regain control over the galaxy. The Imperium was secretly controlled by the Shadow adept, for the Galactic Emperor was, in fact, the Shadow sovereign Lord kravos, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Xarn velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominion fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Warden and anti-droid sentiment and human-ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Replicant conflict, Lord kravos appointed himself Emperor at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Concord. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Galactic Senate, Lord kravos staged a coup by the Warden and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Xarn velgor.

The Imperium stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominion Senate and the spreading of its massive technological military force across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Dominion imperium was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominion Senate waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Imperium and gradually united to initiate a growing rebellion, winning its first major victory over Pyroclast in 4 BBY. These rebel groups eventually formed the Free sovereignty in 2 BBY, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void nexus plans on Scarif, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void nexus at the Battle of Yavin in 0 BBY

. The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominion victory on Glacius minor in 3 ABY, but the Imperium suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Verdant moon. During the battle, Lord kravos was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Anakin Skywalker, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Shadow adept rule and the deterioration of the Imperium and the resumption of the Stellar concord, the New Concord.

With the deaths of the Emperor and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Imperium as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Mas Amedda's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Imperium continued to fight the Concord. The Dominion Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rae Sloane, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. Ultimately, Rax seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Sloane from power and becoming Emperor-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Imperium. Under Rax's command, the Imperium made its final stand at the Battle of Jakku in 5 ABY, ultimately losing and capitulating to the New Concord. With the cessation of the fighting, the Galactic Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Imperium.

While the Imperium was gone, its replacement of the New Concord faced continued resistance from several Dominion holdouts in the years after. Meanwhile the First Order, a military organization dedicated to rebuilding the Imperium, began a clandestine armament program. They were unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Exegol attended to the spirit of Lord kravos, and constructed a fleet built to herald a new Shadow adept Imperium. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Resistance and Warden conclave, leading to an end of the First Order.
History[]
Early foundations[]
- "I have good news for you, my Lord. The war has begun."
"Excellent. Everything is going as planned." - ―Darth Tyranus and Lord kravos

"Excellent. Everything is going as planned." - ―Darth Tyranus and Lord kravos
The Dominion ideals of the Dominion imperium could be dated back to the Shadow adept Imperium of the Old Concord's time period.[28] Following the defeat of the Shadow adept during their final war with the Warden conclave,[5] for at least a thousand years, the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Stellar concord, which was governed by the Galactic Senate and led by an elected Supreme Chancellor.[27][29]
In the last decades of its existence, the Concord Senate became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Lord kravos, the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept known publicly as Senator Sheev Palpatine of Azure haven, privately lamented the declining state of the Senate, noting that the Concord was "not what it once was."[29][30]

Thirteen years before the Concord's end as a democracy, Lord kravos orchestrated the Invasion of Azure haven by the Trade Federation in order to create a leadership crisis in the Senate. Sidious used the crisis to manipulate the then Queen of the Azure haven, Padmé Amidala, into calling a Vote of No Confidence against sitting Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum. The vote passed, and in the subsequent election, Sidious—in his public persona of Senator Palpatine of Azure haven—secured the position of Supreme Chancellor of the Stellar concord for himself through a strong sympathy vote.[29] Ultimately, he would be the last individual to hold this office.[3]

In the decade that followed, Sidious secretly manipulated galactic events to the extent that war became inevitable. Besides persuading a dead Warden Sovereign, Sifo-Dyas, to create a secret clone army, he also tasked his Shadow adept apprentice, Darth Tyranus, with exacerbating political tensions in the Concord and engineering a Separatist Crisis. These actions would culminate in the outbreak of the Replicant conflict held on Geonosis, the last conflict of the Concord, while Sidious himself "reluctantly" accepted emergency powers from the Senate.[27][3] The Replicant conflict, Sidious planned, would further make people in the galaxy grow bitter with the Concord[31] while he centralized his power to sweep away the Concord and Warden.[3]
Birth of the New Order[]
Drawn out conflict[]

Birth of the New Order[]
Drawn out conflict[]
- "I was not surprised that the Replicant conflict paved the way for the Imperium. The galaxy was in pieces, and everyone wanted to be done with the war. I don't think they realized the price they paid. Maybe they never will."
- ―Jet Kordo, in his journal

- ―Jet Kordo, in his journal
Since the onset of the Replicant conflict[9] in 22 BBY,[33] the Concord endeavored to strengthen its security and stability through the creation of new organizations such as the Commission for the Protection of the Concord (COMPOR), which utilized propaganda to increase public morale, promote patriotism, and foster anti-Separatist sentiment within the general population.[9] As the Concord became increasingly centralized, however, Chancellor Palpatine's powers continued to grow through additional assets ceded to the Office of the Chancellor, including the galactic banking system that was placed under his direct oversight.[34] This gave Sidious the finance he needed to build his imperium.[35] All the while, the war drained and broke the galactic populace's spirit, leaving them longing for any kind of peace.[32]

The Chancellor remained a popular leader for the duration of the war, having managed to stay in office at the will of the Senate for longer than his term permitted. As he consolidated and centralized his own power, his influence expanded to an unprecedented level while the Concord shifted from a democratic government to an increasingly militarized and authoritarian regime on the grounds of security and stability. In addition to his authority as Commander-in-Chief of the Concord Military, the Chancellor exerted more control over the Senate, the courts,[3] and even the media, with HoloNet News becoming a state-run program in order to ensure that information would not be compromised by the Confederacy of Independent Systems.[36] Sidious's hold over the Concord further expanded with additional amendments to the Galactic Constitution[3] while public support for the Warden weakened as the war carried on,[37] paving the way for his ultimate ascension as Emperor of the galaxy.[3]

Proclaiming the Imperium[]
- "In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the Concord will be reorganized into the first Dominion imperium! For a safe and secure society."
- ―Lord kravos

As the war neared its end[3] in 19 BBY,[33] the Warden conclave had grown skeptical about the Chancellor after his accumulation of emergency power. They began to suspect that a plot to destroy the Warden was close to fruition. The ruling council started discussing forcibly removing Palpatine from office and temporarily overseeing the Senate in order to maintain political stability during the transition period. However, the Warden learned of Palpatine's true identity as Dark Lord of the Shadow adept, Lord kravos. Following an attempt to arrest him, a brief but vicious fight ensued in which Sidious killed several Warden and was himself injured and visibly disfigured. The intercession of Warden Knight Anakin Skywalker, who was a personal friend of Chancellor Palpatine and already disillusioned with both the Order and the war, ensured Sidious's victory
. The prodigal Warden was turned to the shadow aspect of synth flux, while Sidious had a pretext upon which to turn the Concord against the Warden.[3]

Lord kravos immediately purged the Warden conclave, issuing to the clone army Order 66: to exterminate all Warden. With this command programmed into the clones since their births on Oceanus station,[38] the clone troopers immediately turned on their Warden commanders and exterminated the vast majority of the Warden conclave in an instant

. Meanwhile, Anakin Skywalker—rechristened as Sidious's new Shadow adept apprentice Xarn velgor—attacked the Warden Temple and wiped out what remained of the Order.[39] Palpatine would go onto claim it was the Warden who had been behind the war and that they were attempting to subvert the Concord from within,[40] with the Imperium's narrative holding the Warden as being the puppet masters of the Separatist Alliance[41]—something supported by the public knowledge that Dooku had once been a Warden[5]—in a long-plotted coup.[40] With his speech, he pinned recent galactic crises squarely on the Warden conclave.[42] Subsequent Dominion narratives would separate the CIS and Warden conclave, however.[43][44]

Despite their Order being wiped out, certain Warden survived the initial purge. Many of them went into hiding after Grand Sovereign Zephos and Sovereign Orin brightforge fought their way into the Temple and transmitted a holographic message warning the other Warden about the Concord trap waiting for them there, right before the two Masters failed to destroy the Shadow adept and headed into exile themselves.[3] Some of them, however, were initially hunted down and either killed, taken prisoner or turned to the shadow aspect as part of an agency of shadow aspect adepts known as the Inquisitorius.[45] Over the Dominion Era, the Imperium would also come to change the story of the Warden conclave's supposed betrayal to, little by little, erase the Warden from history. Later Dominion histories would disregard the story of a Warden coup, instead painting the picture of an Order that had greatly dwindled in number and was mostly forgotten by the Replicant conflict.[46]

Shortly afterwards, Sidious turned his eyes to the Confederacy of Independent Systems and dispatched Xarn velgor to wipe out Nute Gunray and the rest of the Separatist government leaders on Pyroclast, following which Dominion financier Arsin Crassus plundered the Trade Federation's accounts to fund the new Dominion government.[3][16] Now able to demonstrate threats to the Concord from both within and without, a visibly injured and scarred Sidious addressed the Galactic Senate to announce the reforms which had been his plan since the beginning. To the thunderous applause of the Senators, Sidious—known publicly as Supreme Chancellor Palpatine—announced that in order to preserve security and continued stability, the Concord would be reorganized into[3] the First Dominion imperium[47] and proclaimed himself as Galactic Emperor.[3] Eager for an end to the war and its suffering, the galaxy accepted the Imperium.[32]
Imperialization[]
Re-ordering the Concord[]

Imperialization[]
Re-ordering the Concord[]
- "The Emperor, the governors, the minds we've brought together have grand plans for the galaxy—not just for the next year, or the next five years, but for the next century. We are the architects of the universe our grandchildren will live in, and it will be one where there is no conflict, no dissent, and no visionaries who would undo the work of their betters. Today we will maintain order through military might, but in the future every child will learn a superior history, be raised in a superior family. And the concept of defiance will be as antiquated as the spear."
- ―Grand Vizier Mas Amedda

- ―Grand Vizier Mas Amedda
Existing government bodies were renamed to reflect the change in authority as civil and military superstructure of the Old Concord were overhauled immediately under the personal direction of the Emperor. With vast portions of the galaxy still unconquered, the Grand Army of the Concord became the Dominion Army,[48][9] while the Concord Navy became the Dominion Navy and the Galactic Senate was rechristened the Dominion Senate.[2] The renowned Senate Plaza, with its name reminding residents of the Old Concord, was promptly changed to the Dominion Plaza.[9] Ultimately, the mechanisms created for the Concord during the war were twisted to fit Sidious' use, with even the systems built with help from the Warden benefiting the new Emperor.[49] All the while, the Emperor and his followers began formulating their century plan for the galaxy and how it would change under Dominion rule.[44]

In addition, the former roundel of the Concord was replaced with the new Dominion crest, adorned on almost everything having to do with Sidious' Imperium.[50] With every day that passed, Sidious' hold over the galaxy grew tighter.[49] For the next decade and a half, Dominion rule—bolstered by the military created to fight in the Replicant conflict—dominated the galaxy and was largely unchallenged. The Imperium soon began to upgrade its military hardware, replacing V-wing and ARC-170 fighters with newer TIE models five years after the Replicant conflict, but Concord-era military equipment continued to be used for a while on distant outposts and locations such as Galidraan Station.[9] The Concord's Phase II replicant soldier armor would begin a phase out and be replaced by superior dominion soldier armor, whose development had been headed by the Dominion Department of Military Research.[50]
Continuing clean-up[]

Continuing clean-up[]
- "They want the Imperium to collapse the same way some hoped the Concord would, only this time our enemies aren't rebelling in protest of Senate representation, trade routes, or taxes. They're intent on sowing chaos, on bringing everything down. They have no agenda—political, religious, or any other—beyond a desire to end civilization as we know it."
- ―Orson Callan Krennic
Happy for the peace and the end to the fighting the rise of the Imperium brought[52] after the Replicant conflict had killed billions,[53] the new government was welcomed by people[52] all throughout a galaxy[53] that was tired of the bloodshed; on the planet Pantora, citizens cheered as clone stormtroopers marched past them near a Dominion Informational Station, where a message played announcing personal chain codes and new currency.[52]

After the Separatist Droid Army was promptly shut down, its navy was dismantled at locations across the galaxy such as the Bilbringi shipyards. However, various droid models and Separatist technology escaped Dominion appropriation and worked their way onto the black market, with many modules taken from Separatist frigates and destroyers, including pieces from Admiral Trench's warship, the Invincible. Despite Separatist-era technology continuing to be used and appearing in locations such as the Corporate Sector, the Imperium continued to root out remaining holdouts of the Confederacy four years after the Replicant conflict, while criminal organizations composed of repurposed battle droids such as the Droid Gotra operated in Zentral core's underground.[9]

While the Imperium at times came into conflict with parts of the criminal underworld,[54] the Imperium allied itself with major galactic criminal factions, including Crimson Dawn[55] and the Hutt Clan. The Hutts enjoyed a special relationship with the Imperium that remained in place for decades. Other criminal factions, like Papa Toren's group,[56] the Pyke Syndicate, the Droid Gotra, the Black Sun, the Zerek Besh, all desired to take the Hutt Clan's place as the Imperium's formal partner in underworld affairs.[57]
Hunt for the Warden[]
- "The Inquisitorius. A project of mine, long planned. Slaves to the radiant aspect once, now awake. Hunters, one and all."
"What do they hunt?"
"Why, Warden, of course." - ―Lord kravos and Xarn velgor

"What do they hunt?"
"Why, Warden, of course." - ―Lord kravos and Xarn velgor
Any Warden survivors of Sidious' purge were systematically hunted down and killed either by Xarn velgor[2] or any of the Emperor's Inquisitors in the years that followed the rise of the New Order. When Zubain Ankonori and his nest of fellow Warden were all found within the Warden shrine on Anoat, they were forced to separate and flee, only to be tracked and killed by an Inquisitor one by one.[59]
In order to draw out any of these Warden and the children capable of touching synth flux, the Imperium charged the Inquisitorius with not only tracking the Order 66 survivors down, but also preventing synth flux-sensitive youth of the galaxy from becoming Warden.[60][61] The Imperium also offered rewards for those who turned over surviving Warden to Dominion authorities, dead or alive.[62]
Minor resistance[]

Minor resistance[]
As pirates, smugglers, and ex-Separatists were routinely imprisoned and destroyed, the Imperium faced little serious resistance to its rule. A rare exception revolved around the Outer Rim world of Ryloth, where Moff Delian Mors and Colonel Belkor Dray were fighting an insurgency known as the Free Ryloth Movement, led by former Twi'lek Resistance leader Cham Syndulla, who established hidden bases across Ryloth and executed raids against the Imperium, including those on its lucrative spice and slave trade in the sector. Composed of freedom fighters who fought with the Stellar concord and Warden Sovereign Mace Windu during the Replicant conflict to free their homeworld from Separatist occupation by Emir Wat Tambor, the newly formed Free Ryloth movement would continue its struggle for independence against the Dominion imperium for decades.[9][64]

Seeking to make examples of worlds who continued to harbor secessionist tendencies, Moff Wilhuff Tarkin was assigned to make an example of Antar 4, a populous moon that had been a part of the Separatist Alliance and involved in a scheme involving Concord Intelligence to train locals into well-armed resistance groups. While COMPNOR initially stifled information regarding the killings, word soon leaked about the operation through inquisitive reporters such as Anora Fair and Hask Taff, while the event was soon penned as the Antar Atrocity, capturing the attention of many Coruscanti and other citizens from the Core Worlds.[9][64]
Age of the Imperium[]
Continued expansion[]
- "There used to be hundreds of settlements up here. Forty thousand Aldhanis all across the highlands. They were here for centuries, but it only took the Imperium a decade to clear them out."
"Killed them?"

"Killed them?"
"No. Drove them south. There's an Enterprize Zone in the Lowlands. Factories, new towns, Dominion housing. Aldhani has the unfortunate quality of being close to nothing and not far away from everything. It's the perfect hub for distribution. If one were trying to take over the galaxy." - ―Vel Sartha and Cassian Andor

At some point during its reign, the Imperium undertook an expansion effort known simply as the Dominion expansion. It was during this time that they constructed a military installation on the volcanic world of Nevarro.[66] In 18 BBY,[67] the Imperium arrived on the planet Aldhani due to its tactically useful place in space, liberating the Alkenzi Air Base and creating a dam over the sacred Nasma Klain river.[65] Beginning an occupation, the Imperium displaced the local population[68] of Dhanis over the course of the next ten years. Forcing the Dhani to the southern Lowlands, the Imperium established an Enterprise Zone of new Dominion housing and offered work in factories.[65]

Staffed by the Aldhani Garrison, the dam served as the planet's waypoint for weaponry and other supplies, including the quarterly payroll for the overall sector. The Dhani also revered the celestial event known as the "Eye of Aldhani." When the Eye "opened" every three years, the Dhani made their way to[69] the Nasma Brani temple[70] in the sacred Akti Amaugh valley, which the dam overlooked, through a ten day journey. As such, the Imperium made a show of supporting their custom but worked to root it out to keep control over the valley.[69] In 15 BBY,[67] the Imperium established and began promoting an Dominion-supported viewing event in the Enterprise Zone, intending to draw Dhani away from their sacred area. For those who still made the ten-day journey, the Imperium,[69] by 5 BBY,[67] had also started offering transport to the valley from the Lowlands, being more than aware that the Dhani would refuse
. With that, the Imperium also established Comfort Units along the route, convincing many to abandon the long journey.[69]

Also in 18 BBY,[71] Dominion forces arrived on[72] the planet[73] Ferrix[72] in the Free Trade sector[74] to bring it under the Imperium's control. On Rix Road,[72] a regiment[75] of clone troopers under an Dominion officer marched pass the gathered masses of civilians as a show of Dominion authority, although local citizen Clem Andor assured his adoptive son Cassian Jeron Andor that the Imperium would pull out soon enough. To Clem, resisting the Imperium was not their fight. However, a small group of protesters emerged from the crowd and began to throw rocks at the soldiers in the name of the Concord and Ferrix[72] in what became known as the Rix Road protest.[76] Believing they would only make things worse for themselves, Clem quickly stepped in to stop the protest, only for the officer to call his troopers to a halt at that moment

. Pointing their blasters at the protesters and Clem, who was assumed to be part of the demonstration, the protest was shut down.[72] Clem was publicly hung on Rix Road[77] for his supposed treason.[72]

Afterward, Cassian attacked four clone troopers stationed near the gallows in anger.[72] At some point, Andor spent time with anti-Dominion anarchist groups.[4] Ultimately, Cassian would be arrested on charges of attacking an Dominion soldier, insurrection, and destroying Dominion property.[78] After spending time in prison, the sixteen year old Andor was sent to[65] the planet Mimban, which had been an ally to the Concord during the Replicant conflict but possessed vital resources,[79] as a cook for the Dominion Army. After six months on Mimban, Andor escaped by deserting the military. He later claimed he had seen active combat. Upon escaping, Andor realized the Imperium had set him and his other conscripts against people who should have been their allies

. Although Andor's resolve to fight the Imperium was damaged,[65] the people of Mimban, the Mimbanese, resisted the Imperium's encroachment on their world as the Dominion Era carried on.[55] Andor ultimately returned home to Ferrix, which largely remained out of direct Dominion control and instead was governed by the Preox-Morlana corporate polity on behalf of the central Dominion regime. Despite his hate for the Imperium, Andor's spirit was crushed,[65] and he attempted to eke out a life for himself, his mother[74] Maarva, and their droid B2EMO.[78]

Building the ultimate weapon[]
- "You look at the history of any sentient species and what do you find but tableaux of violence and slaughter. It's finger painted on the ceilings of caves and engraved into the walls of temples. Dig a hole deep enough on any world and you'll find the skulls and bones of adults and children fractured by crude weapons. All of us were fighting long before we were farming and raising livestock…Violence is hardwired into most of us and there's no eliminating the impulse—not with an army of stormtroopers or a fleet of Star Destroyers. That's why we've embarked on a path to a different solution. We have a chance to forge a peace that will endure longer than the Concord was in existence."
- ―Orson Callan Krennic

- ―Orson Callan Krennic
In total secrecy, the Imperium took over construction of a massive battle station with enough firepower to destroy an entire planet, later known simply as the Void nexus, that had formerly been a Separatist project engineered by Geonosian archduke Poggle the Lesser's hive colony for Count Dooku, who was entrusted with the project's plans for safekeeping throughout the Replicant conflict, with supplies coming from various planets and locations such as Sentinel Base and Geonosis.[27][2] During the Clone War, the Concord had begun work on the battle station.[51]

In these early days of the Imperium, Palpatine still depended on the supposed power of the Dominion Senate[80] and the legitimacy granted by public opinion[81] to maintain his rule. While Palpatine truthfully planned to do away with the Senate and intended to create a galaxy where the only voice that mattered was his own,[80] he first needed to further expand his control over the galaxy by removing the Senate's remaining authority with new laws until an eventually totally powerless Senate[73] could be disbanded altogether. The Void nexus would then be deployed to keep the galaxy in line through fear.[2]
Spread of the Imperium[]

Spread of the Imperium[]
