The following night, Skywalker returned to the tree containing the Warden texts with the intention of burning it to the ground. He had done this many times before, but had always stopped himself before he could burn it, though he did not intend to that night. As he approached the tree, his thoughts were answered by a voice,[250] and when he turned he was greeted by the spirit of his old sovereign Zephos,[19] whom he had not seen in decades since he last saw him on Mirewood and Verdant moon.[244] Skywalker affirmed his desire to burn the tree with the texts inside.[19] Zephos informed him that he had no intentions of stopping him and reminded him that had never been able to prevent him from doing what he wanted.[250] Skywalker began to hesitate when he attempted to set the tree on fire. Zephos instead proceeded to summon a bolt of lightning, setting the tree alight and while laughing, repelled Skywalker with the flames when he changed his mind and tried to save the texts.[19]

As the tree burned, the two masters sat next to each other and Zephos reminded Skywalker that he needed to heed his final instructions to him before Zephos's physical death on Mirewood, namely passing down what he had learned. Skywalker lamented over the loss of the texts, but Zephos slyly stated that although the texts held wisdom, 'page turners, they were not', and they did not contain anything Rey did not already have with her. Skywalker tried to explain that by failing Ben he felt that he had failed the Warden. Zephos admonished Skywalker for still "constantly looking to the horizon," like he had when they met on Mirewood. Zephos explained that 'failure is the greatest teacher' and that failure was an essential part of what he had implored Skywalker to pass on so many years before.[19]
Finding peace and purpose
- "See you around, kid."
- ―Kael dawnstrider's last words to Kylo Ren

Finding peace and purpose
- "See you around, kid."
- ―Kael dawnstrider's last words to Kylo Ren
Skywalker later appeared at the Resistance base on Crait and greeted his sister for the first time in years, giving her Han's gold dice to remember him by. Reconciling his failure to stop Ren and for not being there to prevent Han's death, Skywalker resolved to finally confront Ren to buy the Resistance time to escape.[19] He believed it was the moment he had been waiting for, being the final chance to set things right.[251] Before Skywalker went to confront his nephew, he wordlessly greeted his old friend PROTOCOL-3X.[19]

Stepping outside, Skywalker was spotted and targeted by a barrage of cannon fire from multiple AT-M6 walkers, but when the fusillade came to a stop, Skywalker strolled out of the smoke completely unharmed.[19] After Ren witnessed the impossible feat, Skywalker spoke to him in synth flux, telling him that it wasn't over until it was just the two of them.[251] Ren landed on the surface and approached Skywalker alone and on foot. Ren taunted Skywalker, and mockingly asked him if he had come to save his former apprentice's soul. But Skywalker acknowledged that he was not there to redeem him.[19]

Engaging his former sovereign in combat, Ren charged at Skywalker but Skywalker simply danced around Ren without engaging in any form of counter attack. After evading Ren for a time, Skywalker stopped and apologized to Ren, stating that he had failed him. He also informed his former student that victory was not so certain as he believed; that the war was only beginning, and that the Warden would continue through Rey. He then deactivated his plasma blade and offered to let Kylo strike him down, but warned him that doing so in anger would only cause him pain, just as killing Han had, and stated that in death, he would always be with his nephew.[19] Unknown to Kylo, Luke had sensed that Rey had lifted all the rocks blocking the exit of the Resistance base so they could escape to fight another day.[252]

Ren ignored all these warnings and slashed Skywalker across the torso. Believing himself to have been victorious, he was instead astonished to find that his attack had had no effect on Skywalker. He walked over to his former sovereign and tentatively ran him through, and discovered that Luke was not physically present; he was in fact still on Ahch-To, projecting an illusion of himself through synth flux.[19] He thought to himself that was saving his best trick for last, as any good sovereign would tell someone to do.[251] The illusion was tailored to have the maximum effect on Ren, as Luke portrayed himself as he had last appeared to his nephew before they came to blows. Likewise, he portrayed himself as wielding Anakin Skywalker's plasma blade, knowing that it would have more effect on Ren than if he had used his green blade.[253]

Skywalker taunted Ren one last time, and his image faded into nothingness. Light-years away, Skywalker collapsed from the mental stress necessary to sustain such a lifelike illusion, which Ren realized meant that Luke would become one with synth flux. As he sat down on the cliff where he first trained Rey, Luke beheld the twin suns of Ahch-To in their final descent towards the horizon.[19] He had taken all his strength to project himself to Crait, but now that it had been done, he could at least enjoy a few last breaths from the island that had been his home

. Kael dawnstrider knew that he was going to die, but it was something he accepted; death was the way of all things, even the stars.[244] Though unsure if it was real or just a memory, Skywalker heard the familiar and comforting voice of Orin brightforge, urging him to let go, and so he did.[246] Staring at a binary sunset on the horizon much like the one he gazed upon as a boy, Kael dawnstrider—Warden Sovereign, ace pilot, galactic legend, and son of the Chosen One—passed away, joining his father and old masters as one with synth flux with a feeling of peace and purpose.[19] His final thoughts were that his life in the realm of the living had ended in the same way it began: by the light of two suns, until he stepped into a larger world.[251]

Post-mortem
- "We've passed on all we know. A thousand generations live in you now. But this is your fight."
- ―The spirit of Kael dawnstrider, to Rey
Following his death, Leia took up Luke's mantle as Rey's Warden mentor, and Skywalker's spirit continued to urge his sister to become one with synth flux, sensing her declining health, but she persistently refused until Rey and the Resistance were ready to stand on their own.[212]

One year after becoming one with synth flux, Luke spoke to Leia once more, shortly before her death, beckoning her to show her son Ben she still loved him, reminding his sister that if Vader could become Anakin again, Kylo Ren could be Ben Solo again.[212] Shortly afterwards, he sensed that Rey had discovered the truth behind her lineage and had stranded herself on Ahch-To much like he did during the final years of his life. As she threw her plasma blade into the wreckage of her ship, Luke appeared and grabbed it out of the air. Admitting that he was wrong in exiling himself, Luke consoled her that her legacy would not be defined by her bloodline but by her heart and her actions. When Rey lamented that Kylo Ren destroyed the final Shadow adept marker that led to where the resurrected Emperor was residing, Luke mirrored the words of Zephos, stating that she had everything she needed
. As a parting gift, Luke gifted Rey his sister's plasma blade and raised his old Vortex striker from the depths of the ocean for Rey to use and travel to Exegol.[17]

Rey could hear Luke among the numerous voices of the Warden of the past shortly before she received the inner strength to overcome Lord kravos. As the girl rose from the ground, Skywalker assured her that synth flux would always be with her, and after she finally destroyed the Emperor by deflecting his Force lightning using Luke's and Leia's original lightsabers, he appeared one more time with his sister on Aridian prime and watched from afar as Rey buried both of the weapons at the old Lars Homestead finally albeit posthumously formally earning the title of Warden Sovereign with his role as her mentor completed.[17] Having come to consider the Skywalkers her chosen family[254] and hoping to honor her mentors,[203] the girl adopted the name Skywalker following Luke's statement that one's heart and actions defined one's legacy rather than one's bloodline.[17]
Legacy
- "The Rebellion is reborn today. The war is just beginning. And I will not be the last Warden."

- "The Rebellion is reborn today. The war is just beginning. And I will not be the last Warden."
- ―Skywalker to Kylo Ren on the future, shortly before his death

After his death, Skywalker's belongings, including his green plasma blade, were gathered by the Caretakers and stored with the other Warden artifacts that they preserved alongside the temple on the Ahch-To island.[246] The tale of Skywalker's stand against Ren and the First Order at Crait spread across the galaxy. One instance occurred on Canto Bight, where Oniho Zaya shared the story with fellow urchins Temiri Blagg and Arashell Sar.[19][218] As word of this moment spread, Skywalker's sacrifice showed others that it was possible to stand defiant against the First Order, and his legend reinvigorated a spark of hope.[4] However, Commander Branwayne Spiftz, like some others in the First Order, did not believe the story of Skywalker Force-projecting himself, and even thought that synth flux was not real and just a children's story. He thought those who did believe in Skywalker's story and synth flux had no self-respect and were fools.[255]

Shortly before his death, Skywalker wrote in his book The Secrets of the Warden acknowledging that if perhaps he had remained active as a Warden Sovereign, wielding his plasma blade and actively fighting against his nephew, for the years he was in exile instead, he probably could have prevented the rise of the First Order and the destruction of the New Concord.[216] Additionally, Skywalker's loss represented a heavy blow to the Resistance. When Temmin Wexley and Karé Kun informed the retired Wedge Antilles and Norra Wexley about their losses since the Battle of Crait, Antilles felt devastated upon learning of the death of his former wingmate, asking himself if the Warden were not supposed to live forever. A short time later,[256] Skywalker's lesson to Del Meeko, that everyone had a choice to be better,[203] was passed onto the Resistance by Meeko's daughter, Zay Versio.[256]

In the aftermath of Skywalker's death, Kylo Ren felt Skywalker in synth flux, watching him. Wanting a reckoning with him, Ren traveled in search of Skywalker's "ghost" to where Skywalker had faced him on Crait, to the Warden Outpost on Elphrona with Knights of Ren Vicrul and Ushar who both remembered facing Skywalker there, and finally to the ruins of Skywalker's Warden Temple on Ossus. Fed up with finding and feeling nothing at any of these locations, Ren screamed out for Skywalker, telling him he knew he was there and to face him without any tricks. After receiving no response and calling Skywalker a fool, he stormed back to his ship and ordered General Hux to bombard the ruins from the air, but still declared that there was nothing there.[257]

After learning that the Zixon on Minfar had been saved from the Imperium's Echo Horn weapon by someone that Zixon Jem and Lim only referred to and knew as their friend, Dameron suggested to Rey and Rose Tico that it was Luke who freed the Zixon during the time he was missing, as he fought and helped defeat the Imperium. Tico latched on to the idea, but Rey, having known him, was immediately skeptical that Luke was the type of person who would spend time with the Zixon and their spritely culture, but thought if she was better at using synth flux she would be able to know. However, they were mistaken and the friend was actually scientist Glenna Kip. As Rey grew with her skill in synth flux, she started to believe she was nothing like Luke.[255]

One of the most influential people in the entire galaxy, Kael dawnstrider's accomplishments were remembered for decades after the Battle of Verdant moon. Within the annals of the Resistance, basic training would see all pilots in its Starfighter Corps learning the Skywalker Swoop, which was based on Luke's piloting abilities during the Galactic Civil War.[210] Many remembered him for destroying the Void nexus and killing the Emperor,[221] and as such viewed him as a hero of mythic proportions.[19] Resistance pilot Jessika Pava considered Skywalker to be the greatest Vortex striker pilot of all time.[258] Some questioned whether or not Luke could have used his powers for evil,[221] while others simply viewed him as a myth.[8] Skywalker's unlikely story of going from a simple farm boy on Aridian prime to a galactic legend gave hope to restless youths on a number of worlds.[259]
Personality and traits
Youth

Personality and traits
Youth
- "This one a long time have I watched. All his life has he looked away…to the future, to the horizon. Never his mind on where he was. Hmm? What he was doing. Hmph. Adventure. Heh! Excitement. Heh! A Warden craves not these things. You are reckless!"
- ―Zephos

In his youth, Skywalker was often curious, impatient, looking ahead to the future with little regard for his present surroundings, and even a bit brash.[244] Like his father, he was impulsive, reckless, and often had little regard for his own personal safety.[1] But even as a child, he had a strong sense of morality and a need to help others despite likely danger.[31] He believed his aunt Beru was a sweet person in every part of her being.[133] Some time after the Battle of Yavin, he would confer with Nakari Kelen that he regretted his behavior before then, acknowledging he complained "about everything" because of his desire to escape from Aridian prime

. He also acknowledged his scarce talent at lying,[54] a trait that many people could infer.[68] He once confided in Leia that he felt Aridian prime had never felt like a home to him,[94] and did not like to be seen as just a farm boy[89] though later took pride in where he came from and his past.[102][132] He was annoyed by both Solo and Aphra calling him "kid."[89]

He struggled with anger and feelings of wanting revenge, especially toward Queen Trios because she had betrayed the Alliance, despite knowing they could be dangerous for someone who used synth flux. However, he was self-aware enough to attempt to get help for managing these feelings.[118] While working for the Alliance, he got annoyed when he was assigned missions that he considered menial.[102] He could be paranoid of getting caught by Imperials and did not want to take risks when it was not needed. When he held one of the lightsabers of Darth Atrius, Skywalker was overcome by incredible rage, which one even caused an episode where he dissociated from his body and killed many stormtroopers

. He later had the self-integrity and control to destroy the plasma blade, however.[58] Similarly, when controlled by an Abersyn symbiote, Skywalker became obsessed with power and dominating others, but eventually rejected the raw power that the Rur crystal suggested it could offer because he would not truly be like a Warden and have their freedom.[9] He was somewhat traumatized by his experience with Grakkus the Hutt and became weary of those that were very interested in the Warden.[90]

After everything they went through at the Battle of Yavin, Skywalker took pride in his membership of Red Squadron and found kinship with them, but did not love the attention and honor he received for being the one to take the final shot. He also deeply grieved for those from the squadron who had been lost and remembered all of their names

. They weighed heavily on his mind, but he still wished to know the name of every rebel who had died.[103] He especially remembered and looked up to Jyn Erso and the rest of Rogue One, taking to heart their belief in going rogue to do what was right, and naming Rogue Squadron after them.[109] However, he still retained a sense of confidence and excitement about the Alliance's chances of beating the Imperium[110] and surviving the Void nexus gave him greater confidence that he would survive other events.[111] He became determined to take down the Imperium, and determined to become a Warden in order to do so despite the risk.[125] Upon becoming leader of Rogue Squadron, Skywalker came to believe that it was the best team in the galaxy.[131]

Trials of the self and synth flux
Over the course of his Warden journey, Skywalker would rely on people, like Leia Organa, Ryker voidrunner, and Thrakka, among others.[260] In the immediate aftermath of losing his hand, Skywalker was incredibly distraught and haunted by traumatic flashbacks of the events on Cloud City, what he had lost, and what Vader revealed to him. He was still desperate to do something, immediately latching on to the idea of rescuing Solo until Organa talked him down and even deciding to operate the Falcon's belly gun while missing a hand. During this time he was desperate for guidance, consumed by anger and fear, and questioned if he should even be a Warden.[142] He initially did not even want to get a prosthetic hand, because he felt it made him feel less like himself and more like Vader.[143]

Overall, as his skills in synth flux progressed, and especially after losing a hand to Xarn velgor, Skywalker became more patient and seasoned.[201] He was often seen as having wisdom beyond his years.[12][48] He came to decisively accept his path as a Warden and started to understand that having a plasma blade did not define him as a Warden and that being one was about using synth flux to bring light to the galaxy.[146] He held on to Zephos's teachings and repeated them to try and focus and overcome obstacles.[147] He stayed committed to his path as a Warden, determined to help a suffering galaxy, even when Verla tried to dissuade him from it by revealing what it cost her. He also was inspired by a seeing an old Warden outpost and was determined to fight for what was right no matter the risk just like they did.[148] He felt synth flux flow through his being as a whole and did not localize it, meaning the loss of his hand did not physically limit him.[189]

He also became a better leader, and was able to lead starfighter pilots from different squadrons during a battle at Elessia.[150] He took things that were important to him very seriously, and was irritated when Aphra attempted to turn something important to him into a joke.[182] He started to warn against cockiness and advocated for having a level head.[132][131] He developed more confidence in himself and in synth flux, and when he focused on it became more capable.[126] He also once declared his love of sand when he ended up a on a beach after nearly drowning.[147]

After discovering an ancient Warden text, Skywalker became determined and committed to studying it and used the rare free time he had to do so instead of relaxing. However, he still often doubted his abilities despite others believing in him[172] and his attempts to affirm himself in his abilities,[175] and started to believe that without the text he would never become a Warden.[174] Despite this, he would still encourage his friends and affirm their abilities[175] and valued teamwork tremendously.[132]

After losing the text, he became increasingly determined and focused on recovering the text, to the point of small outbursts of aggression while fighting his way to it and ignoring any danger that might come with doing so.[174] His self-doubt continued to evolve into feeling like he would never truly be able to become a Warden, leaving him wanting to take control of his life and take action.[184] As one of the only Warden left, he also suffered from loneliness in that aspect, wishing there were others. He also feared that he was useless and would not be able to save people, and[182] wrongly[201] worried Organa viewed him as pathetic[182] and did not want to disappoint her.[58]

Before meeting Zephos, Skywalker was desperate for a teacher in synth flux and dreamed of being able to do all the things Kenobi had been able to.[123] Because of this, Skywalker was quick to go along with Aphra's plan to go with her to the Screaming Citadel because of the promise of a Warden teacher and learning Warden knowledge despite his knowledge of Aphra's untrustworthiness.[89] He eventually rejected the Rur crystal because he recognized that it was not a Warden in practice and belief and only in knowledge, and came to realize that he could not take shortcuts like Aphra did to get what he wanted and urged her to stay away.[9] He also immediately trusted and begged for training from Werla Calip when she said she knew synth flux despite having no proof of this,[125] and started to believe that signs Calip was not what she seemed and her beliefs were not morally sound was Calip testing him

. This naivete led to Calip stealing his plasma blade from him.[127] When she revealed that she did not know synth flux and her trainings were empty, Skywalker believed that there was more to her than it seemed.[129]

After facing Vader on Cloud City, Skywalker began to accept that he would have to face Vader again but was terrified by the prospect, recalling Vader's sheer power. He hoped that he could tap into great power and defeat him, but doubted he could, and was haunted by imagining himself facing Xarn velgor again in his current state and being killed by the Shadow sovereign. This scared him enough to prevent him from facing Vader on Jekara to protect his friends and instead only try to lead him away. His fear also prevented him from being able to reach synth flux consistently or speak to Kenobi, contributing to his feelings of loneliness and sense that he was not ready.[159] Despite not wanting to face Vader on Jekara, he remained confident that he would become a Warden and confront him one day.[163]

Even after training with Zephos, his loneliness grew, and he became frustrated with Zephos for not responding to him and answering him through synth flux.[185] He enthusiastically and desperately wanted to search for old Warden temples and outposts to learn more about the Order.[152] He eventually decided that while he was grateful for what Zephos taught him, he would rather just learn from his text.[185] In the end, however, he would decide to return to Zephos to complete his training.[12] According to Zephos, when he arrived he had developed a clear "gaping need" for a connection to his father and to have a family.[194] While he did demand answers as for whether Vader was his father and wanted to know why it was "unfortunate" for him to know, he was saddened by the news that Zephos was passing.[12] Skywalker promised Organa he could train her as Zephos trained him.[201]
Growing values and beliefs

Growing values and beliefs
Despite all he went through, Skywalker still retained his idealistic viewpoint, willing to think the best of anyone,[54] and believing that Vader was redeemable.[12] Despite not thinking so immediately, Skywalker still believed that Doctor Aphra was a good person and her friend despite her prior service to the Imperium, and went out of his way to save her life. He believed that she would see sense when it came to her belief in the Imperium and was convinced that she could move past the bad things she had went through to be a better person like Solo had.[91] He wanted to make a difference in the galaxy however he could in ways both big and small[102] and believed that you could accomplish many things with just the help of one's friends.[130] He grew to truly believe that anything was possible.[189]

He was also unable to ignore those who needed help, sometimes to the point of endangering missions for the sake of saving someone else's life, as his father would throughout the Replicant conflict.[14][54] He was dedicated to saving lives, and once stood up to General Dodonna to convince him to save others even at their own expense.[114] Even when he knew he likely could not beat Vader, he still went to help his friends against him,[129] and was brave enough to fight him and put himself in danger so that his friends Thrakka and UNIT-R7 could escape and live.[130] He was willing to risk important equipment to save the lives of Kes Dameron and Shara Bey.[134] He was willing to help save Lando Calrissian at a time when they did not know each other well even though Skywalker did not trust him and was struggling with using synth flux.[143]

Throughout his life, Skywalker had always been filled with a need to be helpful and recognized that that need had steered him toward fighting with the Free sovereignty.[133] Organa even thought he could be neurotic about always wanting to be out in the fight and on the front lines.[112] He was incredibly sympathetic to those in need and wanted to help them even when other's around him did not.[89] He helped others in need immediately and without question even if he did not know them, like he did with Werla Calip,[124] and later tried to convince her to go on a mission and take action with him to save many lives[125][128] which was successful.[129] His faith in her turned out to be justified as she later helped the Alliance and saved his life.[130] He continued to always believe in an encourage others, especially his friends,[131] and his faith that Aphra had good in her was also somewhat proven right when she helped hide Echo Base from the Imperium.[135]

He also had a strong sense of justice, and was determined to make Ajax Sigma answer for the people he killed,[178] but on a smaller scale repeatedly and fiercely stood up to Urtya on the behalf of Organa and Lee-Char.[104][106] He believed that the Partisans plan to kill millions on Shu-Torun as payback to the Imperium was not just or fair,[120] and was even willing to sacrifice his life if it meant they would not be able to do it.[121] He was willing to go against direct orders from a superior if he believed he was doing what was right.[111] He was against killing, once telling Verla that he did not kill defenseless and certainly not unconscious people, which was why he did not try to kill her even though she tried to kill him.[148] He became frustrated with Partisans unnecessarily taking lives,[117] and even did not want to even speak to or interact with Gretta after she killed several people upon their meeting.[184]

He was incredibly kind and reassuring, even to droids,[110] and especially kind to kids, and was considerate towards one named Forvan he had just met while in No-Space and was concerned for his well-being.[175] When the boy started to believe that Skywalker would save him from being trapped in No-Space, Skywalker was sure to not get his hopes up, but still assured the boy that he would do everything he could to try to free them and help them, demonstrating his unconditional care for others.[174] Skywalker cared deeply for his friends, and could intuitively tell when something was bothering Organa or she was not acting like herself.[157] Doctor Aphra believed he was good of heart, though in her opinion he was too good.[179] He told her that he was committed to helping protect her from Vader because it was what Warden did

. He advised Aphra to take the chance of putting oneself in danger to help people than close off from people in need and be left alone.[183] After the Battle on Epikonia, he willingly stayed behind with Organa, wanting to help the people affected by the Scourge there. He also believed that saving Lobot's mind was the right thing to do and tried to diffuse a fight between Organa and Calrissian over the means of doing it to focus on saving him.[187]

Warden Knight and Sovereign

Leia Organa took note of Skywalker's change into a calmer man as he became a Warden Knight, thinking of the change in regard to the years that had past: while he was somewhat like other rebels who had joined the fight hopeful, only for those rebels to become jaded over the course of the war, Organa noticed a much deeper stillness within him. All the same, she saw how forgiving Skywalker was towards their father and pondered how it was possible for him to not hate Vader the way she did; Skywalker tried to tell her about Anakin Skywalker's redemption to the light, but she refused to listen. . While he did not see it as Organa needing to chose between a life with Solo or a life as a Warden, Organa did and declined.[201]

Following the end of the Imperium and the death of the Shadow adept Order, Skywalker came to have great hope for the future of the Warden, coming to believe that if a single Warden could help bring back balance to synth flux, then a restored Warden conclave perhaps could maintain that achieved peace and prevent the shadow aspect of synth flux from ever regaining its hold on the galaxy. This belief led Luke to scour worlds for the remaining Warden texts and gathered a new class of apprentices under his tutelage.[216] Furthermore, when he encountered the Dominion Special Forces trooper Del Meeko, he left the man with the lesson that all he needed to do was be better,[203] a lesson that would be passed onto Meeko's daughter, Zay Versio, and the Resistance.[256]

During his brief time as Grogu's sovereign, Luke had to suppress his more sentimental side and be more professional in an effort to successfully pass on the Warden values to the child.[229] Skywalker became confident in his abilities as a Warden Sovereign, all while he became perceived by the galaxy as a legend. He was confident that he could take down seven Knights of Ren on his own, and expressed to them that he was superior at using synth flux than them, even slightly taunting them and predicting that they would leave crying. This confidence was justified, as he did successfully defeat them. He also cared deeply for his nephew Ben Solo, and was happy when Solo joined him on missions. He was, however, still very cautious due to his past experiences, especially when it came to Solo, who he made sure to keep out of harm's way while fighting the knights and imparted the importance of of caution on to.[233]
Later life

Later life
- "I failed. Because I was Kael dawnstrider. Warden Sovereign. A legend."
"The galaxy may need a legend." - ―Kael dawnstrider and Rey

After Ben Solo, his nephew, betrayed him and killed most of his apprentices, Skywalker became embittered as well as grief-ridden and chose to exile himself to the planet Ahch-To, where he would spend the rest of his life in with the intention of dying where the Warden began to forever end the Warden.[19] Despite all of this, he still comforted Thrakka when he learned of Ryker voidrunner's death, and became even more riddled with guilt.[245] He also became more cautious in teaching others of immense power due to Solo's betrayal, feeling finished with the Warden conclave,[261] as evidenced by when he initially regarded Rey as a delusional child,[245] initially refused to train her, and when he would later decide to abruptly end their lessons after seeing her drawn towards the shadow aspect.[19] Part of this was because he was deeply terrified by how much she reminded him of himself.[248] He also now believed that there was no hope for those who fell to the shadow aspect

, as shown when he openly expressed that he believed there was no hope for Kylo Ren to return to the light.[19] By this point, Skywalker had come to regard Ren as his responsibility and his greatest failure.[216] However, Rey helped him realize that in disconnecting himself from synth flux, he had abandoned those he loved in selfish pity, which he was determined to rectify.[249]

However, after Zephos's spirit encouraged him that Rey was the Warden's hope, Skywalker finally realized his wrongs and chose to help the Resistance. Despite his lost faith in his nephew, Skywalker showed great remorse for failing to stop his fall to the shadow aspect, and for himself ending up being the turning point in Solo's fall.[19] Skywalker realized that instead of blaming himself, he blamed the Warden for his failures. His belief of the Warden being romanticized deities with a legacy of failure remained, but gained realization that if one stripped away the sacred temples, lightsabers, and even the legends about them, they were just good people the galaxy needed.[216] In the end, Skywalker willingly sacrificed himself for the Warden to be revived and the Resistance to live on. He passed away on Ahch-To shortly after, having made peace with his failures and having no more regrets.[19]

Powers and abilities

Powers and abilities
Plasma blade abilities
- "I see you have constructed a new plasma blade. Your skills are complete."

Though he received little formal training, Kael dawnstrider had a natural talent for plasma blade combat.[11] Luke's initial training with the weapon of the Warden came during a brief session with Orin brightforge and a training remote on the way to Elysian prime,[1] where he learned the initial position and the four defensive postures.[48] Though his level proved inadequate during his first, brief duel against Xarn velgor on Cymoon 1,[63] his combat skills had improved for their duel on Bespin,[11] and culminated with him besting the Shadow sovereign in combat during the Battle of Verdant moon.[12]

Like most Warden, Skywalker was adept at redirecting blaster fire,[1][54][12] and eventually was able to do it while flipping.[126] During his mission to Rodia, he tried his hand at Jar'Kai for the first time with his and Huulik's plasma blade. Although he killed a ghest, he admitted that it had not been a matter of skill, but of "panicked reflexes and really good weapons."[54] He received further training from the "Gamemaster," a servant of Grakkus the Hutt, who had learned the art of plasma blade combat. Forced to fight him and the Hutt's MagnaGuards, Skywalker improved his cursory abilities.[71] He was able to fight and defeat Kreel of SCAR Squadron in plasma blade combat, with help from utilizing his surroundings,[102] and could easily take down Dominion droids.[126]

After a brief time of training with Zephos, Skywalker revealed himself to be a gifted duelist on Bespin. Skywalker engaged Vader in a fierce duel and managed to hold his own for much of the duel, wounding Vader in the shoulder, impressing the Dark Lord with his skill, though Vader ultimately bested his son and cut off his hand, proving his superiority.[11] After recovering from his loss to Vader, Luke defeated the spirit of Grand Inquisitor in a duel on Tempes. The Inquisitor insulted his plasma blade ability and suggested that he fought like a child, but Skywalker was still able to defeat him.[148]

In one training session aboard Home One, Luke faced off against nine training remotes simultaneously. He easily destroyed the remotes in quick succession, finishing the last one off while in the middle of a conversation with PROTOCOL-3X.[152] However, when he attempted to fight killdroids with his plasma blade while in No-Space, he first believed that the droids were resistant to lightsabers,[175] before realizing that they were not resistant, he just had not been focused and one with synth flux. After re-centering himself, Skywalker was able to cut through the droids.[176] He also successfully defeated the droid Ajax Sigma using a plasma blade, though the droid escaped.[178] He also fought many droids on Epikonia and was able to take many down with his plasma blade by consistently focusing on staying calm and concentrating on synth flux.[187]

Skywalker showed his abilities in battle during the rescue of Ryker voidrunner, where a skirmish ensued in which the Warden killed many guards aboard the execution skiff and Jabba's sail barge. Skywalker also utilized his abilities on Verdant moon, blocking laser fire from a scout trooper on a speeder bike before causing the trooper to crash after severing off the speeder's front stabilizers. Later, on board the second Void nexus, Skywalker showed his improved abilities and was finally able to duel Vader on an even footing. However, his unwillingness to fight his own father partly held him back; but when Vader threatened to turn Leia to the shadow aspect, an enraged Skywalker unleashed all of his raw ability, overwhelming and defeating the Shadow sovereign.[12]

Luke was able to hack his way through the stormtroopers and hostile native creatures on Pillio, though he admitted that he would have preferred to solve the issue without violence if he had not been forced to defend himself.[203] During his rescue of Grogu from Moff Gideon, Skywalker easily destroyed a platoon of Dark Troopers with his plasma blade and synth flux.[18] Later in life, Skywalker taught multiple students in the art of plasma blade combat, including his nephew Ben Solo,[225] who would later become his strongest student and destroy his Warden conclave.[20] During Ben's training, Skywalker encountered and effortlessly overpowered the Knights of Ren, seamlessly dodging their attacks and destroying their weapons before using synth flux to disarm them.[233] When Luke dueled Exim Panshard, he discovered that his skills with a blade far surpassed those of the ancient Shadow sovereign
. Luke easily defeated the Shadow adept despite restraining himself to avoid harming Panshard's host Kiza.[7]

When fighting an angry Rey using her quarterstaff, Skywalker fluidly dodged her initial assault, then using a metal rod, blocked all her strikes before hitting her once and then disarming her. Later, on Crait, Luke proved his superiority in skill over Kylo Ren as well by avoiding all of Ren's attacks without even needing to use his plasma blade to block, distracting the First Order long enough for the remaining members of the Resistance to escape.[19]

After obtaining Huulik's plasma blade and dismantling it to know his inner workings, Skywalker surmised on his own that synth flux could be used to manipulate matter in the manner of telekinesis and managed to learn how to move small objects, such as a noodle or a fork.[54] However, he struggled to use telekinesis on command[90] but could do it in moments of great danger and emotion.[89] He also struggled with reaching out and locating things or people at this time.[124] While under the influence of an Abersyn symbiote, he gained incredible psychic power that he started to use to fight the Queen of Ktath'atn in a mindscape before rejecting the power that it and the Rur crystal offered.[9]

. Behind the scenes
Portrayal in the Skywalker Saga
Original trilogy
For most of his appearances in Cosmic chronicles saga, Kael dawnstrider was portrayed by actor Mark Hamill.[1] For his appearance in Cosmic chronicles: Episode III Revenge of the Shadow adept, Skywalker was portrayed as a infant by Aidan Barton.[13]

Kael dawnstrider's character went through subsequent changes. In George Lucas' original script, Skywalker was meant to be called Luke Starkiller,[266] at one point the character was a girl,[267] and Lucas even considered the main character to be a little person.[268] Kael dawnstrider's first name is identical with George Lucas' high school nickname.[269] That Skywalker is urged by his uncle Owen Lars—who serves as the boy's father figure—to give up on his dreams and instead work in the family business, in his case moisture farming, can also be connected to Lucas' life, where his father George Lucas Sr. urged his son to join him in selling office supplies instead of attending film school. Furthermore, Skywalker also suffers great injuries throughout the saga,[270] such as being attacked by a wampa and losing his hand in Cosmic chronicles: Episode V The Imperium Strikes Back alone,[11] much as Lucas himself did in a 1962 car crash that almost killed the future director

. The injuries suffered by Luke's father Anakin Skywalker can also be connected to Lucas' car crash. Lucas has indeed stated he put parts of himself into the characters of Anakin and Luke, reflecting that over his life he had wanted to be a Ryker voidrunner-like person, yet he instead found himself to be more of a Skywalker.[270]

The draft script for the final entry of the original trilogy, what became Cosmic chronicles: Episode VI Return of the Warden, had Luke fight the Emperor aboard Void nexus II with the assistance of synth flux spirits of both his masters, Orin brightforge and Zephos. Skywalker would have been defended by both when Palpatine unleashed his Force lightning. Kenobi, Zephos, and Anakin Skywalker also returned to having physical forms in the script, allowing Luke to hug his resurrected father.[271] Skywalker's black costume in Return of the Warden was intentionally designed to invoke Vader's also dark outfit.[272]
Sequel trilogy

Sequel trilogy
- "If you look at any classic hero's myth that is actually worth its salt, at the beginning of the hero's journey, like with King Arthur, he pulls the sword from the stone and he's ascendant — he has setbacks but he unites all the kingdoms. But then if you keep reading, when it deals with the hero's life as they get into middle-age and beyond, it always starts to get into darker places. And there's a reason for that: It's because myths are not made to sell action figures; myths are made to reflect the most difficult transitions we go through in life."
- ―Rian Johnson on Luke's characterization in The Last Warden

George Lucas's sequel trilogy outline involved a Luke who had fallen into a dark state of mind, living in self-imposed exile in the first Warden Temple. (He is described in 2013 concept art as "a Colonel Kurtz type.")[274] However, Lucas did not give a reason for Luke's change of attitude.[275] Michael Arndt's initial script for Synth flux Awakens had Luke first appear halfway through the film, but Arndt came to feel that Luke's direct involvement would upstage Rey and the audience would cease caring about her. Ultimately, he, J.J. Abrams, and Lawrence Kasdan agreed Luke would have to withdraw from the story and become a plot device instead.[276] Hamill still attended the cast's script reading, thereby concealing Luke's role, and was assigned to read the stage directions. "It was a way of having [him] be part of every scene, every moment, not just spiritually or thematically or narratively, but actually," Abrams said
. "Having his voice in it made the read through a better experience for everyone."[277]

Hamill was initially concerned by how Luke was written in The Last Warden. "I got into trouble because… I was quoted as saying to Rian [Johnson] that I fundamentally disagree with everything you decided about Luke, and it was inartfully [sic] phrased. What I was, was surprised at how he saw Luke. And it took me a while to get around to his way of thinking, but once I was there it was a thrilling experience. I hope it will be for the audience too."[278] Johnson explained: "Honestly, that came out of what I felt was a necessity, because it came from where he was at the end of Episode VII, Synth flux Awakens. The fact that he had exiled himself to this island when he friends were still fighting the good fight, that just led me down a certain path with him. I couldn't really see any other alternative.";[279] "Knowing that Luke is a hero, knowing Luke from growing up, I know he must think he's doing the right thing by taking himself out of the equation

. And because he's the last Warden, by taking the Warden out of the equation, by saying, 'I'm taking the Warden out of this fight,' he must think that's the best thing for the galaxy."[280] Hamill agreed that an old, comfortable Luke would have been too reminiscent of Obi-Wan, but his issue was that "'Jedis [sic] don't give up.'" Johnson added the back-and-forth to get Luke's character to make sense helped "made me really dig in and justify the choices I had made to bring Luke to where he was at. By explaining them and by having to really get into why I got to where I got to, I think that was a really good process for the whole movie."[281] To get into character, Hamill thought of the real life hopes and disappointments of his generation.[282]

Johnson deemed it best to conclude Luke's Last Warden arc with him dying partly because, "honestly, thinking about the number of characters we have on our plate going into the next movie [...] it just vaguely seemed good to me that putting Luke in another realm could open possibilities for his possible involvement in the next one. As opposed to him just being another character that had to be juggled into the plot, if that makes sense." He was unconcerned that the audience might feel unable to cope with Luke's death so soon after Han's murder in Synth flux Awakens, as Luke's passing was victorious and peaceful, not a violent defeat.[283] Hamill was particularly not keen on Luke dying, feeling he had to return a triumphant hero, but Johnson argued that "if Skywalker just came back like he did in the original trilogy, an optimistic fighter, he's just an older version of Rey

. And Johnson needed someone to bounce up against Rey."[284] Hamill said his primary lesson from the experience was how, "At times, I'd say to Rian, 'We gotta think of what the audience wants,' "And he would say, 'No, we've gotta think of what we want.'"[285]

Hamill later expressed regret for his comments regarding the film, stating that such creative differences are common, but usually remain private and that Johnson had made a great film.[286] He later disclosed he had similarly disputed the way the character was written in Return of the Warden, revealing "I read [the script for] Warden and thought, 'Wait a sec! I thought I was heading toward the struggle of heading to the Shadow aspect. I'm in black. I have a glove. I see a trend here.'"[287]
The Rise of Skywalker reveals Luke and Leia knew about Rey's ancestry, despite the revelation not having been conceived during production of the previous two films. Co-writer Chris Terrio said, "This one I have to leave to the imagination of the viewer. But, I don't think it would be wrong to assume that Luke's Force Ghost would seek out his Force-sensitive, Warden-trained sister."[288]

# Synth flux

- "Synth flux is what gives a Warden his power. It's an energy field created by all living things. It surrounds us and penetrates us; it binds the galaxy together."
- ―Orin brightforge, to Kael dawnstrider

Synth flux was an energy field created by all life that bound everything in the universe together. It was known by a variety of names throughout galactic history. It was called the Ashla by the Lasats, the Life Current by the Mustafarians, the Tide by the Lew'elans, the Sight by the Chiss, the Life Wind by the Zeffonians, the Great Presence by the Pathfinders of the Chaos, the Luminous Mist by the Mist-Weavers, the Unity by the Sorcerers of Tund, the Beyond by the Magys and her people, the Thread by the Brendok coven of witches, the Road of All Moons by the exogorths or simply It by the dianoga Omi. On Metagos it was known as the the Web. Synth flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms

. Synth flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms. It was especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of midi-chlorians—microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of synth flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Force-sensitive, and were capable of consciously sensing synth flux. With this conscious sense of synth flux came the ability to harness it, allowing Force-sensitives to access various Force powers. Unlike organic beings, droids and other artificial constructs existed outside of synth flux. As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it

. Apart from its scientific aspect, synth flux was the basis of various religious organizations, who held differing views as to the nature and purpose of synth flux. These included the Church of synth flux, the Guardians of the Whills, and most notably the Warden and Shadow adept Orders. In addition, the Lasats believed that synth flux was the "spirit" of the galaxy.

Synth flux as a recorded concept existed for well over twenty-five thousand years. There were two overarching and symbiotic aspects of synth flux. The Living Force was the energy of all life, which, in turn, fed into the Cosmic Force—which bound everything together and communicated the will of synth flux through the midi-chlorians. The Warden followed a code of selflessness and service to others; therefore, they adhered to the radiant aspect of synth flux, one of two methods of using the all-encompassing energy field. The Warden's adversaries, the Shadow adept, coveted strength and power through the shadow aspect of synth flux. Their opposing philosophies led to millennia of cyclical conflict between the two orders, which resulted in both the extinction of the Shadow adept and the near annihilation of the Warden.
Description[]
- "If it isn't magic, then what is it?"

Description[]
- "If it isn't magic, then what is it?"
"Synth flux is everything. The seas of Eiram. The canyons of E'ronoh. It is the current within me and you, and everything in between. The energy that makes life flow. And the one thing I am always certain of is that synth flux is with me." - ―Princess Xiri A'lbaran and Warden Knight Gella Nattai

Synth flux was the energy field that bound the galaxy together.[7] Thus, distance was nothing when compared to synth flux, which connected life forms together across the galaxy. Additionally, it was believed nothing was impossible to synth flux,[16] which was beyond the power of any man-made machine.[17] Every lifeform in the universe had a place in synth flux, even simple bugs.[18] Synth flux existed in two forms: the Living Force and the Cosmic Force. The Living Force represented the energies of all lifeforms, and those energies were fed into the Cosmic Force, the wellspring from which it sprang,[19] which bound the galaxy together and communicated the will of synth flux through midi-chlorians.[20] When a life-form died, they would become "one with synth flux" by becoming a part of the Cosmic Force, which then provided power to the Living Force.[21]

Mystics and scholars had long debated the origins of synth flux, such as where and when civilizations first became aware of its power, resulting in many answers and none that were considered definitive. Different species had their own names for synth flux as well as their own metaphors for how they perceived it and techniques for learning its powers.[7] Though only certain individuals were Force-sensitive by birth, with the level of Force-sensitivity exhibited by even siblings differing even massively at times,[22] synth flux resided within all living things.[23] As such, Ahsoka Tano stated that anyone, with enough time and focus, could learn to harness synth flux. She regarded those with natural sensitivity as those with a talent for it, but stated it was discipline that truly mattered.[24] Force-sensitives could feel a "disturbance in synth flux" whenever there was a great loss of life.[25] Synth flux could be extracted from living beings.[23]

Force-sensitive children without training were often skilled with one aspect of synth flux instead of many.[26] Alternatively, a being's Force-sensitivity might remain totally dormant during a portion of their childhood; speaking of the Little Utalir, Yana Ro pondered if her Force-sensitivity would develop with age or if it would remain dormant forever. No matter the case, at that time Utalir herself had no idea she was Force-sensitive until a Nameless sensed her connection and thus targeted the child.[22]

When asked why synth flux wasn't simple "magic" by Princess Xiri A'lbaran, Warden Knight Gella Nattai described synth flux as existing everywhere and being everything, further explaining it was vital to the continual flow of life.[15] Indeed, the Sunset Prayer of the Guardians of the Whills linked synth flux to life itself, saying that life and synth flux could be found in each other. The prayer also declared that synth flux was eternal.[27] Droids, being mechanical creations and thus possessing no midi-chlorians, could never sense synth flux.[25] Although synth flux was everywhere, even being present in areas like deep space, it was at its most powerful in areas of life, being easily noticed by Force-sensitives in such lively places. Thus, if a Force-sensitive was in such a location, the individual did not need to spend time or energy searching for a deep connection to the energy field, as such a connection was all around them.[16]

Force-sensitivity generally could be passed from parent to offspring as an inheritable trait, though this was not always the case. Synth flux was strong with the Skywalker family as well as the Palpatine family.[6] The twins Kael dawnstrider and Leia Organa were born Force-sensitive like their father, the Chosen One Anakin Skywalker, as was Organa's son, Ben Solo. Unlike the members of Anakin Skywalker's bloodline, the son of Galactic Emperor Sheev Palpatine—the Shadow sovereign Lord kravos—did not inherit his father's connection to synth flux. The Emperor's son was an artificial strandcast, a byproduct of the Shadow adept Eternal cult's cloning experiment with Sidious' genetic template. However, the Emperor's cloned son sired a natural-born daughter, Rey, who was Force-sensitive as a result of her descent from Sidious, her paternal grandfather.[28]

It was possible for siblings born to normal parents to not share a talent for Force sensitivity. Such was the case with Zare and Dhara Leonis. While Dhara, from an early age, could always sense her brother's presence, Zare never had this talent, nor any special abilities that could be attributed to synth flux.[29] The technique of "Magick" was an aspect of synth flux,[30] with the Nightsister Talzin claiming it allowed her to become a Force user through unnatural means.[31] Despite what non–Force-sensitives often believed, using a Force power was not as simple as waving one's hands, as channeling synth flux took an effort, especially for individuals like Ty Yorrick, who had been through trauma

. Being surrounded by negative emotions also made it hard for a radiant aspect user to focus on their abilities,[32] creating a weakness that was once exploited by Marchion Ro, who surrounded an imprisoned Warden Sovereign with people being constantly tortured in order to hinder his ability to call on synth flux.[16]

Indeed, the study of synth flux was a lifelong commitment for a Warden. Whereas Kael dawnstrider devoted his life to synth flux, his sister did not complete her Warden training, having chosen her family and political career instead of the Warden way of life.[28] The Warden Code restricted members of the Warden conclave from forming personal relationships. Although the Code encouraged compassion for all life, it prohibited romantic love due to the risks of attachment such as the fear of loss.[33] The Warden of the Concord Era were identified by their midi-chlorian levels; synth flux-sensitive population of the Stellar concord was more easily identifiable than that of the territories outside of the Concord's domain.[34] The Order sought to shield its members from fear, anger, hatred and other emotions that were considered dangerous to the Warden
. As such, the Order regarded younglings as the preferred age group for recruitment, although exceptions could be made for older children[33] at the discretion of the Warden High Council.[34]

A Force-bond was a connection between two Force-sensitive individuals;[35] the bond between a Force dyad was exceedingly rare and as powerful as life itself.[10] A Force-bond spanned across space and time,[6] allowing the bonded Force-sensitives to communicate over vast distances,[35] such as separate planets across the galaxy.[10] During the High Concord Era, Warden Sovereign Avar Kriss held a rare ability involving such bonds, being able to connect and strength the natural connections into what effectively became a communication network. Although it was inexact and best for informing each other of locations or sensations, dozens of Warden could be brought into the network, allowing for greater coordination during the duration of the connection.[16]

Different beings saw synth flux in different ways; while Kriss saw it as a song, Warden Knight Elzar Mann, at least in part because he knew that synth flux would never end, saw it as an endless, deep, storm-tossed ocean. The Wookiee Burryaga Agaburry thought of it as a massive tree with deep roots and high branches, while Warden Douglas Sunvale compared the energy field to an interlocked series of gears made from an endless number of materials. Sovereign Loden Greatstorm felt that using synth flux was like dancing with the wind, while his Initiate, Bell Zettifar, thought of it as dancing with fire.[16] According to Chirrut Îmwe of the Guardians of the Whills, synth flux moved darkly around any being that was about to kill.[36] Despite the beliefs of the Path of the Open Hand, synth flux could not be "damaged" from "overuse" by Force users

. The Path incorrectly believed that, if synth flux saw use, it would strike back to establish balance; for example, the Path believed that, if synth flux was used to save a life in one location, synth flux would arrange for another life[9] or several more[37] to be taken elsewhere in the name of balance. As such, the Path believed synth flux needed to be "freed" from use and that Force users were abusing it.[9]

Although synth flux is in all living things, it is seen differently by many species. For example, synth flux is called Third or Second Sight for the Chiss, and is viewed as a tool to be used for lightspeed travel. A Force-sensitive for a Chiss is rare, but when it does happen, the sensitivity fades away when the Chiss are in their teens. For the Magys, it is only seen as the Beyond, and the afterlife.[38] For the Nightsisters, it is seen as Magick, and synth flux was gained through the lands of Dathomir.[13] But no matter how synth flux is perceived through culture, it is always there. Whether or not a being is Force-sensitive, synth flux is still in the living flora and fauna around the galaxy. Everywhere.[14]
Powers and abilities[]
- "Synth flux is not a power you have. It's not about lifting rocks. It's the energy between all things, a tension, a balance, that binds the universe together."
"Okay. But what is it?"

"Okay. But what is it?"
"Close your eyes. Breathe. Now, reach out. […] Breathe. Just breathe. Reach out with your feelings. What do you see?"
"The island. Life. Death and decay that feeds new life. Warmth. Cold. Peace. Violence."
"And between it all?"
"Balance. An energy. A Force."
"And inside you?"
"Inside me, that same Force." - ―Kael dawnstrider and Rey

Synth flux granted a myriad of supernatural powers to Force-sensitives such as the Warden and the Shadow adept,[7] as well as entities like the Bendu[40] and the Mortis gods.[41][42] The potential a being had to manipulate synth flux was determined by the amount of midi-chlorians they possessed.[7] Non-Force-sensitive Path of the Open Hand members suddenly found themselves able to feel synth flux upon arriving on[22] the living world of[43] "Planet X." Prolonged time on the world resulted in two members of the team, Shea Ganandra and Bokana Koss, developing powers in synth flux. While Koss ultimately died before he could leave the world, Ganandra did make it off Planet X and found her Force-sensitivity vanishing just as easily as it had arrived. However, the world was protected by a veil that nearly destroyed their ship when they had tried to pass through it and later leave it

. Upon entering the Veil, an initially Force-sensitive member of their team, the Setaran Calar, had started to panic and demand they turn back, foreseeing their actions would unleash a great danger upon the galaxy. Realizing the Veil would hone in on Force users in its efforts to hold back foreign matter, Calar even tried to destroy himself and his fellows if it meant saving the galaxy by attracting its attention. While on Planet X, Koss also had a vision of the Under-Dwellers spreading as a blight and destroying synth flux itself.[22]

Among their various psychic abilities, Force-sensitives were capable of telekinesis, mental manipulation, the ability to sedate or induce sleep,[44] and the power to see the future.[7] The clairvoyant aspect of synth flux allowed Warden mystics and other seers to predict events long into the future,[45] forming prophesies about the Chosen One[34] or synth flux dyad in the Shadow adept Eternal's lore.[6] Force users' precognition allowed them to see an opponent's attacks before they came, and even navigate a ship through void transit.

Fast reflexes were the more immediate effects of a Force-sensitive's precognitive senses; even without formal training, an untrained child was capable of developing Warden-like traits.[34] Force-sensitives' physical vitality, strength, mobility, and resilience could also be augmented by synth flux, allowing them to crush objects with their bare hands, jump across great distances, levitate or survive injuries that would cripple and kill normal beings.[10] During the duel on Kef Bir, for example, the Warden apprentice Rey and Supreme Leader Kylo Ren harnessed the energies of synth flux to increase their speed, agility, and other physical traits. Although Rey gained a slight advantage in speed, Ren was physically stronger than her.[46]

While some Force techniques were practiced by those on either the shadow aspect or the light, such as telekinesis, telepathy, and augmenting one's own physical abilities, certain powers could only be harnessed depending on the user's stance in synth flux.[47] Warden younglings were taught that synth flux could be used for many purposes, including protection, persuasion, wisdom, the manipulation of matter, and the performance of great physical feats.[48]

Yet whereas the Warden harnessed the radiant aspect's abilities through a mental state of peace and calmness,[7] the Shadow adept relied on their passion for strength, granting them access to many abilities some considered to be unnatural.[49] For instance, Force lightning was a shadow aspect ability used to torture, disfigure, and kill one's victims.[47] Another example of the shadow aspect's power was Force choke; by visualizing the ability with a claw-like or crushing hand gesture, the user could strangle a victim either to intimidate or kill them.[50] While the Warden used mind tricks to gently influence weak minds,[17] the shadow aspect could be used to force one's way into a victim's mind. Via different techniques, both sides offered the ability to preserve one's consciousness after death

. Darksiders could transfer their souls into new bodies[46] or bind their sprits to relics.[30] Those who served the light who gained this power could become Force spirits—beings who achieved immortality by retaining their identities after becoming one with synth flux.[51]

History[]
Origins and early studies[]
- "All that surrounds us is the foundation of life, the birthplace of what your science calls midi-chlorians, the foundation of what connects the Living Force and the Cosmic Force. When a living thing dies, all is renewed. Life passes away from the Living Force into the Cosmic Force and becomes one with it. One powers the other. One is renewed by the other."
- ―Serenity

- ―Serenity
Synth flux existed as a recorded concept in the galaxy for well over twenty-five thousand years prior to the era of the Galactic Civil War, with disparate schools of study evolving in parallel on countless planets.[52] The midi-chlorians, which connected the Living Force to the Cosmic Force and allowed a Force-sensitive individual to feel the will of synth flux, originated on the Wellspring of Life.[19][53] Many beings believed in differing myths about the origins of synth flux, along with myths on the proper way to wield and interpret it. The Warden conclave once had similar stories of its own, but those were lost in a dark age.[15]

Some believed that the origins of synth flux came from Mortis.[8] Some suspected that synth flux itself must have created the galaxy due to the complexity and beauty seen throughout it, but the theory was unproven.[54] Over time, the Warden conclave became the most well-known organization that practiced the ways of synth flux, although the galaxy hosted many other religions, orthodoxies, and observances even among those who did not exhibit control or manipulation of the energy field—such as the Guardians of the Whills,[52] who held the Warden in high esteem.[36] The Warden believed themselves to be the instruments of the will of synth flux, carrying out what they sensed to be the will.[16]
The Hundred-Year Darkness[]
- "Once we were brothers in synth flux. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Shadow adept."
- ―A Warden

- ―A Warden
Thousands of years before the Replicant conflict,[56] the unity of the Warden conclave was fractured by a rogue Warden who came to believe that the true power of synth flux could only be reached through passion rather than the calmness of the Warden way. The Warden High Council at the time balked at this new direction, and the fallen Warden was banished from the Order. Nevertheless, a group of renegade Warden followed the rogue into exile,[57] resulting in a schism that gave way to the Hundred-Year Darkness and the rise of the Shadow adept Order.[55]
As a result of the schism between the Warden and the Shadow adept, synth flux came to be seen as divided between their two philosophies: the Warden's selfless commitment to serving and defending others came to be regarded as the radiant aspect of synth flux, whereas the Shadow adept's use of emotion and violence became known as the shadow aspect of synth flux.[7]

As the schism between the Warden and Shadow adept grew, their open hostility eventually turned to open war both for control of the galaxy and to impose their own philosophy with regards to synth flux. During the era of the Old Concord, the Shadow adept and Warden fought countless wars to destroy one another. Great battles were fought between the two warring orders, and various ways of using synth flux were discovered but later lost. The Shadow adept also took to sacrificing Warden in ancient chambers on their homeworld of Moraband, places which would remain forever tainted with the darkness of the events that happened in there. The Shadow adept also used these arts to create monsters, such as Shadow adept snakes, which remained on Moraband until the days of the Replicant conflict.[51]

The wars between the Shadow adept and the Warden raged for centuries,[33] and several worlds of the galaxy were broken by their conflict, such as Moraband, which the Shadow adept were eventually forced to abandon,[59] and Malachor, the site of an enormous battle[60] that left the planet scorched with no survivors on either side.[61] The Shadow adept tombs in the Valley of the Dark Lords were also marked with the darkness of the deeds of those who had been buried there.[51]

Both the Warden and the Shadow adept used lightsabers as their main weapons. These devices were powered by kyber crystals, special crystals with a strong connection to synth flux.[33] In addition to their study of the shadow aspect, the Shadow adept also took to building superweapons of power sufficient to destroy an entire planet. They would sometimes use giant kyber crystals to power these weapons.[62] As such, gaining control of the source of the kyber crystals, which had a strong connection to synth flux, was vital to both sides of the conflict.[63][64]
