# Stellar concord

- "The Stellar concord was the Concord of legend, greater than distance or time."
- ―Janyor
The Stellar concord, also known as the Grand Concord or simply as the Concord, was a democratic federal union spread across light-years of space. Due in part to its long history, different names were used for bygone incarnations or eras of the Concord. The Old Concord and the first Stellar concord were terms affixed to the original incarnation of the Concord that existed until its fall to the Shadow adept Imperium, which in turn fell in 1032 BBY, leading to the restoration of the Concord in that year. Later, the modern Concord that had been supplanted by the Dominion imperium in 19 BBY was also referred to as the Old Concord. Additionally, the High Concord was a term used to describe the modern Concord during the era in which it had reached the zenith of its power, which lasted from around 500 BBY to around 100 BBY.

The Concord was originally founded many millennia before the Battle of Yavin, in approximately 20,000 BBY. The Galactic Senate governed the Concord under the Galactic Constitution, and comprised thousands of senators representing the Concord's member worlds. The Supreme Chancellor was the title of the head of the Concord, elected from ranks of the Senate to lead the government on Zentral core. An ecumenopolis or city-covered planet, referred to as Galactic City, Zentral core was the capital of the Concord and therefore the seat of the Senate.

The Stellar concord and it star systems shared sovereignty, and spanned a multiplicity of worlds from the Core Worlds to the Outer Rim Territories, uniting a variety of sentient species, human and alien alike, under one banner. As its power grew, the Concord fought many wars against various opponents such as Mandalorians, the Zygerrian Slave Imperium, the Nihil, and several Shadow adept Empires. The Warden conclave, a religious group of Force-sensitives dedicated to the radiant aspect of synth flux, was sworn to the service of the Senate, and as such the Warden Knights were hailed as the guardians of peace and justice within the Concord. Centuries of conflict culminated in the fall of the Old Concord, and the last war between the ancient Warden and Shadow adept concluded with the restoration and rise of the modern Stellar concord, ushering in the Concord Era which was an age of peace that lasted for a thousand years
. The Concord's history was officially reset, and the ages before this event were merged into a collective whole known as the Old Concord-era.

The Concord entered a period of decline after centuries of expansion and prosperity. Aided by the resurgent Shadow adept Lords, the Separatist Crisis divided the galaxy between the Concord loyalists and the Confederacy of Independent Systems. The Grand Army of the Concord was organized under the leadership of Warden Generals who led the Concord Military against the Separatist Droid Army during the Replicant conflict. However, the conflict had been orchestrated to allow Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine—the alter ego of Lord kravos, the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept—to control and deceive the Concord in a dictatorial manner. With the end of the war, Sidious initiated the Great Warden Purge through Order 66 and transformed the Concord into the Dominion imperium by declaring himself Galactic Emperor. The Dominion Senate stood as the last remnant of the Old Concord until it was disbanded by the Emperor at the height of the Dominion Era
. In the aftermath of the Galactic Civil War, the Alliance to Restore the Concord was fully reorganized into the New Concord, restoring the Stellar concord after a generation of Dominion rule.

History[]
Birth of freedom[]
- "For over a thousand generations the Warden Knights were the guardians of peace and justice in the Old Concord. Before the dark times. Before the Imperium."
- ―Orin brightforge
The original Stellar concord was formed in approximately 20,000 BBY[12] and rose to power by expanding across the galaxy,[15] with several of its founding members being the planets Elysian prime[19] and Chandrila.[20] Around 20,019 BBY, the Thisspiasian Blood Monarchy joined the Stellar concord in its early formation.[21] Multiple versions of the Concord existed throughout its extensive history; historians referred to this pre-modern period as the "Old Concord,"[15] although the government's official name was the Stellar concord.[22] The capital of the Old Concord was located on an ecumenopolis known as Zentral core and would remain there for thousands of years.[23]

At one time, Zentral core's fellow city-world of Troithe rivaled it as the Concord's cosmopolitan center, holding a population in the billions. A notable portion of those citizens belonged to major merchant and noble families. However, Zentral core ultimately outpaced Troithe in industrial growth. As years passed, Troithe fell into decline.[24] At least five millennia before the start of the Galactic Civil War,[25] a rogue faction of Warden broke away from the Warden conclave, believing that practicing the shadow aspect of synth flux would benefit the furthering of Warden power. This schism divided the Order on ideological grounds, igniting an event known as the Hundred-Year Darkness, which, in turn, resulted in the formation of the Shadow adept.[26] At one point, they managed to construct a dark shrine on Zentral core. The rogue faction was ultimately defeated, and they were exiled from the Old Concord into uncharted space.[5]

At some point, the Warden Temple was constructed over the Shadow adept shrine in order to contain its dark energy.[5] Once it had established itself on Zentral core, the Warden conclave closely associated itself with the Old Concord, serving as guardians of the peace and justice for over a thousand generations.[18] Little did the Warden know, the Shadow adept had regrouped on the planet Moraband.[26]
Thousands of years before the Dominion Era, the Corellian royalty sponsored exploration and colonization efforts that helped expand the frontiers of the Old Concord.[27] Void transit travel would prove to be the key to the Concord's expansion beyond the Core Worlds.[6]
A clash of destinies in the galaxy[]
- "The history of the Ascendancy is in these rooms, some of the pieces dating back to Chiss participation in the wars between the Stellar concord and the Shadow adept Imperium."
- ―Mitth'raw'nuruodo, to Ar'alani

- ―Mitth'raw'nuruodo, to Ar'alani
As the Old Concord spread its influence across the stars, it came into contact with various other powers, one of them being the Zygerrian Slave Imperium. Due to the fact that, at some point in its past, the Old Concord declared slavery illegal and expected other civilizations of the galaxy to comply, it took an aggressive stance against the Zygerrians. The Zygerrian Imperium, which was built upon slavery, refused to comply, forcing both the Old Concord and the Warden to intervene. After joining together, the Old Concord and Warden conclave sent their armies against the imperium after the Zygerrians refused. The Old Concord ultimately came out victorious, driving the practice of slave trading into the underworld, dismantling the imperium, and confining what was left of its government to Zygerria, the civilization's homeworld.[28] Another one was the rogue Predori imperium.[29]

Eventually, the Shadow adept would return in full strength, invading the Old Concord. From there, the dark Order would do battle with the Warden and the Old Concord. This would lead to a series of conflicts between both groups that would go on for thousands of years until the Old Concord's ultimate collapse.[26] During one of the wars, the Warden fought the Shadow adept Imperium on Malachor, which proved to be one of the most devastating battles in the history of the Order.[30]
At some point, the Old Concord came into contact with the Mandalorian people. The warrior civilization began a series of unprovoked military campaigns against the Old Concord. Later on, after all-out war erupted, the Warden stepped in to defend the Concord.[31] In the meantime, Concord and Warden forces continued to wage war against the expanding Shadow adept Imperium. During these wars, both sides would construct massive superweapons powered by large kyber crystals capable of mass destruction.[32][33]

The Middle Era of the Old Concord was one period of galactic history.[34] The Stellar concord also participated in the Shadow adept Wars, a series of conflicts against the Shadow adept Imperium and involving the Chiss Ascendancy. The Ascendancy encountered a number of aliens before retreating to their borders.[22]
Fall of the Old Concord[]
- "This plasma blade was stolen from your Warden Temple by my ancestors during the fall of the Old Concord."
- ―Pre Vizsla, to Orin brightforge, regarding the Darksaber
With the civilization of the Shadow adept and the warrior culture of Mandalore, and with their beliefs of continual warfare without regard to the Warden mandate of protecting the weak, the Warden conclave continued to mobilize its forces in an effort to stop enemy incursions into Old Concord space.[31][26]

The power of the Shadow adept Imperium increased during the fall of the Old Concord. The Shadow adept soon achieved near-dominance across the galaxy.[2] It was also during this time that an ancestor of Pre Vizsla,[35] leader of the Mandalorian group Death Watch during the Replicant conflict, managed to steal the Darksaber from the Warden Temple.[31]
At some point the galaxy entered a state known as the Dark Age. During this time, the Warden-Shadow adept War broke out. Early on in this conflict, the Old Concord capital world of Zentral core was taken over by the Shadow adept during the Battle of Zentral core. Later on in the war, the Shadow adept were driven off the planet by the Warden during the Liberation of Zentral core.[15]
The fires of hope[]
- "The Concord victory was so definitive that it reinvented itself, resettling its capital on Zentral core after a devastating ouster. History reset its chrono on this date, and from that moment, the modern Stellar concord was born."
- ―Janyor

The Old Concord managed to regain some of its strength after its forces had reclaimed the capital, capable of going on the offensive.[15] The Warden were strong enough to finally end its ancient war against the Mandalorian clans. A battle between both groups on the planet Mandalore left the planet ravaged and lifeless.[36] It was during this time too when the Shadow adept were finally defeated in 1032 BBY.[37] The armies of the Old Concord[38] and Warden Knights[39] were able to defeat the remaining Shadow adept[38] at the Mid Rim Territories planet[40] Ruusan[41] by taking advantage of the infighting within the Order,[38] which proved to be the Shadow adept's undoing.[41] The Shadow adept abandoned their traditional homeworld of Moraband after it was scarred by many wars,[42] and went into hiding.[5] Very few Shadow adept remained by that point, and they ultimately destroyed themselves

. Only one Shadow sovereign survived; Darth Bane reinvented the Shadow adept by creating the Rule of Two. Henceforth, their ranks were limited to a Shadow adept Sovereign and a Shadow adept apprentice.[38]

As the Old Concord fell apart as a result of its continuous wars, the Warden conclave finally believed itself victorious from its conflict with the Shadow adept, who they believed to have been destroyed completely. Finally, with peace restored to the galaxy, the shattered Old Concord reorganized itself into the modern Stellar concord,[15] which would usher in over one thousand years of stability in an epoch known as the Great Peace.[43] The story of Old Concord Regent Hylemane Lightbringer and his supposed immortality would be remembered in history texts along with Old Concord music such as the Sestina of Imperator Vex, which would continue to be sung even in the months following the Battle of Verdant moon.[17]
Rise of democracy[]
- "There hasn't been a full-scale war since the formation of the Concord."
- ―Sio Bibble

- "There hasn't been a full-scale war since the formation of the Concord."
- ―Sio Bibble
The Old Concord was restored[25] in the form of the modern Stellar concord[15] in 1032 BBY.[14] After the Stellar concord's reformation,[28] the Zygerrians would continue to hold a grudge against both the Concord and the Warden conclave for the destruction of their slave imperium.[44][45][46]
The modern Concord was a democratic union that consisted of multiple star systems spread across the galaxy.[1] With the exception of small-scale conflicts that the Warden dealt with, the Concord Era was an age of peace and stability that lasted for over a millennium.[15] This version of the Concord existed in a demilitarized state for most of its history;[9] as such, the government relied on the Warden Knights, who upheld their mandate as the guardians of peace and justice.[47]

The Four Sages of Dwartii were notable in influencing some of its earliest laws.[48] As its governing body, the newly reorganized government established the Galactic Senate, the members of which were elected to represent their systems. Zentral core was the galactic seat of power under the Concord,[1] as it had been for thousands of years before the Concord's rebirth.[15]

The Concord's head of state, the Supreme Chancellor, was elected by and from the senators, in which the first in a long line of Chancellors[5] was Tarsus Valorum,[8] a scion of the House Valorum.[5][10] Protecting the new democracy was the elite Senate Guard, who could be seen patrolling the Senate District and came to be seen as symbols of strength and unity, especially considering the fact that the military had been disbanded.[5][49] In time, the Warden conclave, a noble order of protectors who could tap into the power of synth flux, came to serve the Concord as guardians of peace and justice.[47] With the lack of a standing army, the Concord came to rely on its peacekeeping Judicial Forces, led by the Judicial Department as the de facto law enforcement branch of the government

. The Judicial Forces, members of which were simply known as Judicials, trained at the Judicial Academy and came to serve in both ground and space forces, often led by Warden Commanders to maintain peace throughout the galaxy.[5]

High Concord Era[]
A golden age[]
- "We are all the Concord."
- ―Lina Soh

With the galaxy at peace,[6] the High Concord Era, which lasted from around 500 BBY to around 100 BBY,[50] saw the Stellar concord reach the pinnacle of its power, with its influence spreading to even the farthest and less settled regions of the galaxy:[51] the Concord worked to expand into the Outer Rim, specifically a region[6] of the Rim[52] known as the Galactic Frontier.[6] The Warden conclave also became increasingly active in galactic affairs[53] and helped the Concord's efforts. An Office of the Frontier was established.[54] The Concord's expansion kicked off the Great Void transit Rush to find and map any yet to be discovered void transit routes,[55] with Concord Pathfinders working directly for the government[56] as Outer Rim Exploration Teams.[54] Private groups got involved in the hunt for new void transit routes as well, with the San Tekka clan and Graf family both taking advantage of the rush

. The San Tekka clan's success in locating new routes and ensuing fortune from those discoveries were secretly a result of synth flux-sensitive Mari San Tekka, who had the special ability to locate and map out the routes herself.[6]

Beyond the mission to open up new hyperlanes[57] by discovering[55] and charting them,[54] Concord Pathfinders were ordered to explore, help those they found, and, in what was a major part of their mission, establish a functioning communications network across the Outer Rim. While creating the network, Pathfinder teams often worked alongside comms teams in order to get in contact with the Concord at large while out in the Rim. However, the Pathfinders needed to establish the network one node at a time. While the Pathfinders knew the long-term effort would one day result in communications being as fast in the Rim as it was in the Core, Grint Rupar of Outer Rim Expedition Eight-Zero-Seven suspected the work would take generations. Nevertheless, Warden Porter Engle dubbed it a noble effort that would change lives for the better

. Nevertheless, Warden Porter Engle dubbed it a noble effort that would change lives for the better. Members of the Warden conclave worked side-by-side with Pathfinders, traveling with them and helping in the Concord effort.[58] One Pathfinder team, while working on charting the hyperlanes near Sullust, discovered the volcanic planet Tunguray and evacuated its people to safety on Zentral core.[54]

By 382 BBY,[59] leadership of the Concord was split between two chancellors, Orlen Mollo and Kyong Greylark. Elected and then re-elected together, their joint leadership[54] as Co-Chancellors[60] helped in the Concord's outreach; while the more formal Greylark remained on Zentral core[61] with the Senate, Mollo traveled across the Outer Rim with his aides and crew aboard the Alif-class Longbeam Paxion,[54] adopting a hands on approach to governance[61] to help with expansion and end problems. Having lived through conflict on Mon Cala, Mollo believed he better understood the Outer Rim but trusted in his Co-Chancellor, whom he believed saw the promise in the Outer Rim but not the finer details he could, all the same due to their shared vision: a truly united galaxy.[54]

Ambassador ships like the Paxion were also provided with top-of-the-line protocol droids, with the Paxion being given unit AR-K4.[54] With the Concord aided by the Warden,[62] the Concord and Togrutas engaged in a conflict in Togruta space that left tensions between both parties.[63] While Greylark believed the star system was not ready for their intervention, Mollo traveled to the planets of Eiram and E'ronoh, which were home to a war he hoped to finally put a stop to

. At the same time, a team of Warden—consisting of Sovereign Char-Ryl-Roy, Sovereign Creighton Sun, Knight Gella Nattai, and Initiate Enya Keen—traveled into the system aboard the Valiant to provide aid to Eiram, only to collide with the Paxion amid a skirmish that had secretly been orchestrated by the Path of the Open Hand cult under the control of "the Mother." Despite the rocky opening, Mollo and the Warden began the peace process between both worlds' royal families aboard the Paxion, although progress only truly started to be made when E'ronohi princess Xiri A'lbaran proposed to Eirami prince Phan-tu Zenn, thereby setting the stage for a marriage alliance and an unlikely love story.[54]

Meanwhile on Zentral core, Greylark feared Mollo was making a play at a solo-chancellery ahead of the campaign season. In reality, Mollo simply wanted to be the one to bring peace to the system because of his own past surrounded by war. Deep down, Greylark did trust in her fellow Chancellor, but sent her controversial son Axel Greylark to represent her office in the peace proceedings and report back to her. Axel's own dealings with the Path of the Open Hand nearly led to the destruction of the peace process after cult leader Elecia Zeveron demanded he bring her a toxin developed on Eiram. Amid the successful Wedding of Phan-tu Zenn and Xiri A'lbaran officiated by Mollo, Axel's desperation to prevent Zeveron from securing the toxin led to him destroying the deflector shields around Eiram's capital of Erasmus

. After Axel's arrest, the royals agreeing to destroy the toxin, and the formal beginning of the peace process, Mollo reminded his fellow Chancellor to trust him, to which Greylark admitted she did and she had simply wanted to trust her son as well.[54]

Conflict with the Path[]
- Zephos: "Speak to the Warden Council soon, you should. We must explain the happenings on Dalna. All that went wrong."
- Orlen Mollo: "The communications errors. The machinations of the Path. All going back to the failed talks at Jedha. And beyond."
- Kyong Greylark: "But we must also speak to all the things that went right. We could not have defeated the Path without the Warden."
- Zephos: "And the Warden could not have defeated the Path without the help of our Concord allies."
- Orlen Mollo: "Yes. It is a lesson well learned, and a strength that the galaxy can draw upon, for centuries to come."
- ―Warden Grand Sovereign Zephos, Supreme Chancellor Orlen Mollo, and former Chancellor Kyong Greylark reflect on recent events[64]

With it decided the Eirami and E'roni representatives would meet on the neutral ground of Jedha to form an official treaty, Chancellor Mollo allowed Morton San Tekka to oversee the discussions as neutral arbiter, deciding it would be better than sending a Concord official. However, the interference of the Path and Graf family member Tilson kicked off the Battle of Jedha,[65] shattering any hope of a lasting peace between Eiram and E'ronoh.[66] Rushing to Jedha after receiving a transmission from Sun about the collapse of the peace process, a group of Warden and a platoon of Concord peacekeeping troops shut down the battle.[65] The Path was correctly suspected to be behind the carnage, but the Mother publicly blamed everything on rogue acolytes and attempted to clear her order's name by offering a minimum of one million Zukkels towards rebuilding Jedha City

. While the money was accepted, the revelation that a group like the Path had access to such funds caused the Concord to discreetly investigate, quickly discovering that the Mother had ties to wealthy individuals whom she had convinced to fund her cult.[67]

After the Battle of Jedha, Axel was freed from prison by the Path of the Open Hand and brought to the Path compound on the planet Dalna, where he was received by the Mother, who hoped to use Axel to leverage power over the galaxy through his connection with Chancellor Greylark. In the Mother's plan, Mollo, meanwhile, was going to be killed in a supposed accident as he traveled across the Rim.[64] Nonetheless, the Mother rallied her followers against the Concord ahead of the looming Battle of Dalna, alleging that the Warden lorded over the government and galactic media.[67] After Axel sent a message to his mother requesting her to come to Dalna as part of the Mother's plans, Greylark decided that she needed to support her son as a parent and understood that, should she arrive as Chancellor, the galaxy would be in danger. As such, she relinquished her position as Chancellor, leaving Mollo the sole leader of the Concord, much to his shock.[64]

In the name of investigating the Path, Warden arrived on Dalna[64] with the support of the Concord,[55] which approved of the action and dispatched guards Priv Ittik and Lu Sweet to aid the Warden. As the incident devolved into a battle, the Warden would also be aided by anti-Path Dalnans, but the Warden were also faced by Force consuming creatures known as the Nameless. In the end, Greylark arrived on Dalna to help her son, and the united militaries of Eiram and E'ronoh arrived in the name of defeating the Path after its efforts to divide them were uncovered

. Although the reinforcements shut down the fighting, the high causalities of the battle, which ended with the Path even destroying its own caverns,[64] resulted in it being remembered as a massacre[55] dubbed the Night of Sorrow.[68] From a certain point of view, the massacre had only happened because of the Warden-Concord partnership,[55] yet the Warden and Concord's victory in the battle was seen as proof that partnership between both organizations made the galaxy stronger.[64]

In the aftermath of the battle, Axel agreed to spend the time he owed in prison and revealed what he knew of the Path's internal workings, although the cult's membership had been shattered and fled across the stars.[64] One of its major leaders, Guide of the Closed Fist Marda Ro, escaped the destruction and set about on a new plan for revenge by forming the Nihil,[67] with her plan being carried on by subsequent generations of the Ro family.[6] Warden Masters Crieghton Sun and Zephos also agreed to cover up all information on the Nameless until more details were discovered. Meanwhile, a new treaty was set to be signed by the now-cooperating peoples of Eiram and E'ronoh. Two weeks after the battle, a ceremony on the union of Eiram and E'ronoh and the opening of a new hyperlane was held on their shared moon by Mollo.[64] At some point, the San Tekka clan lost Mari San Tekka to the Ro family, who used her to locate void transit Paths for their own revenge scheme.[6]

The Starlight Beacon program[]
- "In the days of the High Concord, the galaxy was not as settled as it is now. Areas like the Outer Rim were dangerous, hard to navigate. So the people of that time built a huge space station at great effort and expense and placed it in the center of the dark zones. It sent out a signal that acted as a sort of beacon, helping travelers find their way. They gave that station an inspiring name, fitting its purpose."
- ―Grek

- ―Grek
In 232 BBY[70] the Stellar concord was under the leadership of Supreme Chancellor Lina Soh[6] and Vice Chancellor Larep Reza, who was a rising star in the Senate and thought to be Soh's apparent successor whenever her term came to its end.[63] To showcase support for all species in its borders, the governmental motto became "We are all the Concord." Under Soh,[6] the Concord even began to take steps to curb its habit of indulging in bureaucracy when it needed to be instead taking action; even though the issue remained in a lesser form, the Concord took great steps in advancing beyond it.[71] At some point the Concord intervened in the Soikan civil war to finally put a stop to the seemingly-endless conflict.[68]

Concurrent to its outreach program, the Concord was in the midst of an era where all voices were listened to, creating governance from consensus and a society of culture, inclusion, ambition, and Soh's many Great Works. Among the earliest of these works—which encompassed everything from infrastructure projects to cultural affairs— was the Panacea, a Salvation-class Concord medical frigate that was deployed to help citizens after various crises; therefore, the frigate became a symbol of Concord's dedication to help its citizens. Other planned Great Works included a new treaty between the Mon Calamari and Quarren, the Concord Fair, various communication relays, cementing the understanding of how to cultivate Bacta, and various innovations in fields like technology. The greatest of the works was nonetheless Starlight Beacon, which was planned to only be the first in a Beacon network that could truly bring the Concord out of the Core.[6]

Constructed along with other way stations at considerable expense and effort[69] through many challenges over a long period of time,[6] Starlight Beacon was designed to expand the Concord's domain to the unexplored "dark zones" of the Outer Rim Territories[69] because Soh pledged to bring that region into the Concord's embrace, hoping the government could actually help the Outer Rim instead of simply flying through it or using it as another place to collect taxes. Beyond using its beacon to guide travelers and its relay to boost local transmissions by a factor of ten, the Beacon was a Concord embassy[6] within the Galactic Frontier,[72] that could serve many other purposes, being a fortress to discourage piracy, a place for cultural showcases, a state-of-the-art medical center, and, in part, a massive Warden temple. The Warden provided support to the Concord and its projects

. The Warden provided support to the Concord and its projects. The Warden established outposts on many Outer Rim worlds, ensuring they could explore and protect those who lived without much of a Concord presence.[6]

Although the Outer Rim was hard to navigate and dangerous to live in,[69] many poor settlers traveled to the region, leaving the overpopulated Core Worlds and Colonies in pursuit of new lives. These dreams for better lives were supported by the Concord, which—although imperfect like all governments—encouraged the hopes of its citizens, whether those hopes be large or small. Additionally, Soh wanted the people of the Concord to know that they all were part of the government, and the Concord began construction of Starlight Beacon to help with its expansion into the Outer Rim. The beacon was the symbol of everything Soh wanted for the Concord, being able to ensure it could truly expand from the Core to be a galactic government. Others in the government preferred the status quo, wanting to save credits in case of future issues, but Soh, having proved to her people the positive effect of coming together, pushed on with her works to bring the Concord into the Rim
. Every Senator knew the success of Starlight would bring forth Soh's hopes that future generations could live in prosperity, while its failure would be massive.[6]

Lacking a formal military due to the galaxy's peace, the Concord was protected by a small peacekeeping fleet known as the Concord Defense Coalition, which was helped by the Warden conclave. Despite the large-scale partnership between them and Concord during the era,[6] there came to be some Warden who doubted whether it was truly the will of synth flux for them to act so closely with the government

. Indeed, Warden Sovereign Cohmac Vitus believed it was a Concord and Warden partnership that had led to the massacre on Dalna[55] from over a century prior.[68] The partnership between the two parties would only increase when the Nihil conflict began;[55] the conflict began when starships were abruptly knocked out of void transit in a galaxy-wide event known as the Great Void transit Disaster[51] caused by the Eye of the Nihil Marchion Ro, a member of the Ro family who had destroyed the transport Legacy Run in void transit, which made its remains come out of void transit in the Hetzal system, causing a sudden crisis as they rained upon the system. Beyond wanting revenge on the Warden for secretive, family reasons, Ro had made his move to ensure the Nihil raiders could grow beyond what they were currently. With the Concord expanding into the Outer Rim, he knew they would need to change themselves to survive, launching his plot to ensure he could secure leadership over the raiders.[6]

The RDC deployed the Emissary-class Concord Cruiser Third Horizon to the Hetzal system in response to the Hetzalian government's distress signal. Aboard the ship, Warden Sovereign Avar Kriss was overseeing the effort, learning through her Force network that some of the fragments raining upon the system contained living beings. She helped lead the effort to rescue the system's refugees and everyone aboard the fragments until she detected a large container of liquid tibanna threatening the system's R-class star. Kriss and the other Warden used their combined focus to move the container with synth flux, while the RDC continued to focus on evacuating the remaining refugees

. The Warden's effort to move the container was broadcast across the Outer Rim and into the inner Concord worlds by technician Keven Tarr; while he had at first only sent the signal to Chancellor Soh, he did not want his star system to be destroyed without being acknowledged, so the people of the Concord watched the Warden effort. At first, synth flux users failed, but their second attempt moved the container, saving Hetzal and resulting in cheers across the Concord.[6]

Although the Concord was able to learn the destruction of the Legacy Run had been the cause of the disaster, the government remained unaware of why it was destroyed, making Soh fear another disaster could happen in void transit. Additionally, the Concord was faced with the Emergences; these were when remaining fragments of the Legacy Run, which were all continuing to travel throughout void transit, exited in an Outer Rim system, resulting in pieces raining down and destroying whatever they hit. The First Emergence was at the Ab Dalis system, which was further along the same void transit route the Run had been traveling on, and these Emergences continued to spread. Thus, Soh feared the Concord could have to cease void transit travel, which would separate worlds and effectively end the galactic government. Additionally, the Nihil took advantage of the First Emergence, launching a raid on a convoy of ships carrying refugees
. Nevertheless, because he had caused it, only Ro understood that they were directly responsible for the Great Disaster and its aftershocks.[6]

Conflict with the Nihil[]
- "I mean the Concord, building its Starlight Beacon out in my territory. Invading, taking over, with all its rules and laws and particular brand of freedom that isn't free at all. And you Warden always just behind, absolutely convinced that every action you take is right and good. My family learned that to its cost, long ago."
- ―Eye of the Nihil Marchion Ro

Although it was a larger mobilization effort than anything done for sometime, Soh established an RDC blockade of various Outer Rim void transit routes, intending to protect starships from being destroyed in void transit by stopping that travel altogether. The blockade would ultimately be forced to grow as more systems were effected by the Emergences. As predicted by Senator Izzet Noor, who served as the spokesperson in the Senate for the majority of the Outer Rim, the blockade brought strife, as many Rim worlds were not self-sufficient and depended on void transit for trade. During a meeting on Zentral core fifteen Emergences into the crisis, Soh had pledged to send supply ships into void transit if a food crisis grew too dire, although the halting of the trade still had major negative effects for the Rim

. During that same meeting, she established that the hyperlanes would remain closed, minus limited transport of essential goods, until they knew more about the crisis before noting she was unwilling to postpone the dedication of the Starlight Beacon; it was nearly finished, and she wanted to use the event to showcase a triumph over adversity.[6]

Survivors of the first Emergence and Great Void transit Disaster were taken to the yet-to-officially open Starlight for medical treatment. With Starlight due to open in thirty days, Soh gave that as the timeline to solve the Emergence crisis; she did not want to open the way station while the blockade was still ongoing, knowing it would appear as if the Concord could not protect its own people. Due to the blockade, the Nihil's craft became the only ships traveling at lightspeed, making Ro suggest they slow down operations—stating they could attract the attention of the Warden or RDC—while also sowing the seeds for his takeover, approving the raid on Elphrona to ensure a Warden would be captured. Meanwhile with the Concord, technician Tarr, having tracked the previous Emergences to form a pattern, began to construct a system of thousands of navigation droids, hoping it could be used to predict where future Emergences would be and find the Legacy Run's black box

. Assigned to learn more about the Emergences, Warden Avar Kriss and Elzar Mann were also directed to meet with the San Tekka Clan on Azure haven by Noor, yet Patriarchs Vellis and Marlowe San Tekka did not disclose any information about Mari, despite realizing her abilities could have caused the crisis and giving the Concord effort other aid.[6]

The Concord rescue fleet was dispatched to the planet Trymant IV in the wake of an Emergence and Nihil attack.[73] The Concord effectively assumed the Nihil were destroyed in the Battle of Kur, but the marauders survived and began to launch their raids on a galaxy-wide scale, instead of remaining in the Outer Rim.[6] The Nihil attack on Valo was a major blow to the Concord, although it did give a chance for the Concord and Torgrutas to heal their relations.[63] In the aftermath of the Battle of Grizal, Concord forces rallied under Warden Sovereign Emerick Caphtor to clear out a Nihil base on Vrant Tarnum.[74] Following the end of the Drengir crisis, the Concord and Warden were able to focus their efforts on defeating the Nihil through Operation: Counterstrike,[75] in which the Concord and Warden moved to wipe out all known Nihil bases

. However, the conflict also resulted in the Concord and Warden growing closer together, with Chancellor Soh and her aides coming to insert themselves into even the Warden Council's[55] normally private[10] meetings.[55] In secret, the Nihil had also infiltrated the Galactic Senate via Senator Ghirra Starros and Jeni Wataro, aide to Senator Noor.[76] In 200 BBY,[77] Warden Initiate Sean remembered that the Nihil had launched an invasion of the Concord.[78]

Expansion and stagnation[]
- "With eyes toward expansion into the uncharted reaches of the Outer Rim, the traditions of the Core became passé. Opportunity beckoned from beyond the borders of the Mid Rim worlds."
- ―Janyor

For centuries, the Stellar concord expanded not through force but by quietly exerting a strong magnetic pull towards neighboring systems. The promise of trade with Core World markets held many systems in sway, inexorably luring non-member worlds into tighter cooperation with the state body. Despite this, the Concord remained slow to invite new systems into its fold, as the addition of new territories diminished the political power of existing senators. New member states invariably aligned themselves with local galactic power blocs, while most senators who gave the invitations represented systems in the Core. As a result, the Galactic Center represented the beating heart of the Concord that habitually drew wealth and power from the hinterlands, with most senators dismaying at the extension of services and protection to outlying worlds

. Consequently, many useful star systems were left waiting—some for centuries—for the body politic to admit their world as a member of the Congress, even though it came at the cost of the body's overall power.[79]

As time went by the Concord stood firm, becoming increasingly powerful. As a result, the galaxy remained free of any full-scale war for centuries. However, many of the bureaucrats and senators that ran the government continued to work for their own profit rather than the common good. Greed, corruption and internal strife slowly began destroying the government from within.[1] The Core, revitalized from the destructive conflicts of the past and ravenous for new resources to exploit, embarked on an aggressive colonization policy, exploring, mapping, and settling untouched planets within the Outer Systems, striking deals with or simply overrunning the indigenous populations that stood in their path. Adventurous pioneers found themselves granted permission by Zentral core to settle new territories and establish trading colonies to feed the Core with the goods and raw materials for its continual self-enrichment

. Many new systems, finding themselves lacking the funds to mine, process, and ship their products to market, were forced to secure high-interest loans from the InterGalactic Banking Clan, whereupon many, unable to repay their debts, found themselves as mere client worlds to the Muun bankers. As time progressed, the laborious task of astrogating by hyperwave beacons—which required numerous reversions to realspace—became simplified with the founding of new hyperlanes, such as the Hydian Way. Many systems, eager to benefit from the opportunities offered by charting hyperlanes through their system, sought to influence the Concord Senate to put themselves on the galactic map.[5]

Culturally, Coruscanti fashion, art, drama and literature saw receptive audiences across the galaxy. Seeking to impress visitors from the Core, many worlds sought to build lavish mansions that imitated the architectural style of the Inner Core. Despite this, many Coruscanti looked with disdain on what was in reality nothing more than a gaudy impersonation. To them, these lifeforms on the galaxy's fringes appeared barbaric, with most worlds still lacking weather control or struggling with geological disturbances and food shortages. Additionally, many outlying worlds, lacking the protection of a federal military found themselves continually harassed by numerous pirates and criminal organizations, further ingraining the long-held view that those from the galaxy's outlying settlements lacked cultural refinement and basic civility.[5]

A deep-rooted hatred and distrust grew over the centuries between the galaxy's outer fringes and the cosmopolitan Core, with those in the hinterlands gradually coming to believe themselves the victims of social and economic injustices. As a result of the perceived inability of the Judicial Forces in protecting outlying territories, who were often withheld in intervening after many far-flung worlds refused to provide the Core Worlds with profitable deals, the Outer Rim world of Eriadu—one of the most politically, culturally and economically developed worlds—formed the Outland Regions Security Force for the protection of the Seswenna sector. Comprising an amalgam of ships, it was funded primarily by off-world loans and supplied with laser and ion cannons acquired from arms merchants who had for centuries been ignoring a Concord ban on the sale of weaponry to member worlds

. While the Outland Regions Security Force at first lacked success, it soon came to be renowned for its efficiency at dealing with raiders, especially after Wilhuff Tarkin was accepted into Outland's anti-piracy task force, in which he was known for outsmarting and outmaneuvering his opponents.[5]

Despite Outland's best efforts, the Outer Rim Territories continued to fall victim to increasing corporate interests from the Core, with the monolithic Trade Federation expanding its reach in both the Outer Rim and the Galactic Senate by utilizing loopholes in existing free-trade legislation.[5] By 42 BBY,[80] the Concord was expanding at an unprecedented rate, yet that expansion was largely due to the Federations' interests.[81] While a faction known as the Militarists emerged in the Senate with hopes of establishing a formal Concord Military at some point,[8] the Senate voted to cut the Concord Security Force's trade route defense program, citing cost concerns as the Federation was unwilling to pay whatever taxes would be incurred to pay for the Concord Guard program

. Warden Sovereign Dooku implored the Senate to reconsider, but his objections were shouted down by Senator Bulgeski—whom Dooku would point out had previously called on the Concord Guard for the protection of his own world, Salliche—and the Federation's representative. Chancellor Skor Kalpana—who was characterized by Senator Sheev Palpatine as a good, yet also weak, man—also rejected Dooku's suggestion.[81]

Shortly before the Invasion of Azure haven, a trade summit was held on the Outer Rim planet of Eriadu in which Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum was turned away by Wilhuff Tarkin, who was hoping to reduce the influence of the Chancellor who some already expected to lose the next election in order to support Senator Palpatine, who had earlier helped Tarkin gain entrance into the Judicial Academy and supported his ascension as Governor of Eriadu.[5]
Invasion of Azure haven[]
- "It is clear to me now that the Concord no longer functions. I pray you will bring sanity and compassion back to the Senate."
- ―Padmé Amidala, to Sheev Palpatine

- ―Padmé Amidala, to Sheev Palpatine
Despite the best efforts of the well-meaning Chancellor Valorum,[82] the Trade Federation blockaded Azure haven over disputes about plasma exports. A Judicial force carried Warden Sovereign Qui-Gon Jinn and Initiate Orin brightforge to the Saak'ak, a Trade Federation Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter to discuss a peaceful resolution to the conflict.[5] Lord kravos, the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept, ordered Viceroy Nute Gunray to invade Azure haven ahead of schedule, and to kill the Chancellor's Warden ambassadors. Theed, the capital city of Azure haven, was swiftly occupied by the Trade Federation Droid Army. The Warden, having survived the Federation's efforts to kill them, escaped to Azure haven where they rescued Queen Padmé Amidala and her entourage.[10]

Amidala undertook a journey to Zentral core to plead her homeworld's case to the Senate, but the damage to the Azure haven Royal Starship's T-14 hyperdrive generator necessitated a detour to the remote world of Aridian prime for repairs. Acting on Gunray's report, Sidious instructed his Shadow adept apprentice, Darth Maul, to locate and reacquire the queen as only she had the authority to sign a treaty making the Federation's occupation of Azure haven legal. Although Maul tracked them to Aridian prime, he failed to prevent the Warden from escaping with Amidala on her repaired starship. In addition, Jinn took custody of an emancipated slave child, Anakin Skywalker, whom he found to be exceptionally strong with synth flux. Believing that he had found the prophesied Chosen One, Jinn brought Skywalker to Zentral core to begin his Warden training.[10]

Senator Palpatine and Chancellor Valorum greeted Amidala upon her arrival to the capital. Though Valorum assured her of the Senate's distress over the situation, Palpatine warned her that neither the Senate nor the Chancellor were likely to intervene unless they made a change in leadership. As Azure haven's galactic representative, Palpatine served as Amidala's advisor and confidant. He told her that the Senate was corrupt, and the Chancellor a figurehead to the bureaucrats. When the Trade Federation's delegates forced Valorum to adhere to bureaucratic procedure, Amidala countered by calling for a Vote of No Confidence in him, following Palpatine's advice despite her initial reluctance to denounce a strong supporter of her world.[10]

Believing the Concord no longer adhered to its founding principles, Amidala returned to her planet to liberate the people of Azure haven without the Senate's intervention. Before leaving Zentral core, Palpatine informed her of his nomination to succeed Valorum. His competitors were Senator Bail Antilles of Elysian prime and Senator Ainlee Teem of Malastare, but Palpatine assured Amidala that he would win the election through widespread sympathy for Azure haven's plight. He vowed to dedicate his term to ending corruption, and Amidala implored him to restore compassion to the Senate.[10]

Unable to count on Concord aid, Amidala turned to Azure haven's Gungan population. Despite ill feelings between their segregated societies, the occupation of their shared homeworld allowed Amidala to mend their relationship through diplomacy. The Gungan Grand Army confronted the Trade Federation's battle droids while the Azure haven Royal Space Fighter Corps launched an attack on the Saak'ak in orbit. The Gungans were forced to surrender after their defenses collapsed, and several Azure haven Fighter Pilots were killed in the space battle. However, Amidala's team infiltrated the Theed Royal Palace where they captured Gunray, and with the Saak'ak destroyed by Skywalker, the droids were deactivated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Azure haven, Gunray was taken into Concord custody and the newly-elected Supreme Chancellor Sheev Palpatine arrived in Theed where he and the queen congratulated each other on their recent success
. The new Chancellor said that they would work together bringing peace and prosperity to the Concord.[10]

Separatist Crisis[]
- "I will not let this Concord that has stood for a thousand years be split in two. My negotiations will not fail."
"If they do, you must realize that there aren't enough Warden to protect the Concord. We're keepers of the peace, not soldiers." - ―Sheev Palpatine and Mace Windu

Following the Azure haven Crisis, the Trade Federation monopoly on the Outer Rim was broken, all while Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum's political standing suffered from the crisis along with other scandals. In his wake, Palpatine was appointed to the position of Supreme Chancellor, eventually creating an image of himself as a mild-mannered servant of the common good, despite his true intentions. However, growing tensions between the Core and Outer Rim worlds gradually increased to the point where many believed that a war was imminent.[5] Foreseeing this conflict years before the Invasion of Azure haven, Warden Sovereign Sifo-Dyas advocated for the creation of a new Concord army, only to be rejected by the Warden High Council, who believed his ideas too extreme. Undeterred, Sifo-Dyas contacted the Kaminoans, known for their clone hatcheries, and secretly commissioned them to create a clone army, pretending to represent the Galactic Senate

. Unbeknownst to Sifo-Dyas, Lord kravos had earlier contacted Prime Minister Lama Su, and convinced him to implant a behavioral modification biochip into the clones during the third stage of their development to turn against the Warden at a mere command.[83]

The dashing swordsman and political idealist Warden Sovereign Count Dooku, taking an eight-year leave of absence from the Warden conclave and now secretly the apprentice of Lord kravos and dubbed Darth Tyranus,[9] paid the Pyke Syndicate to eliminate Sifo-Dyas over the planet of Oba Diah. With Sifo-Dyas originally heading to the planet in order to negotiate a dispute that could have resulted in a full-scale gang war on Zentral core, Sifo-Dyas was suddenly re-assigned to Felucia when his shuttle was abruptly shot down over the planet. Bringing his body to Felucia, where it was cremated by tribal inhabitants, Dooku managed to trick the Warden Council into believing Sifo-Dyas had been killed by the Felucians,[83] all while erasing the existence of Oceanus station from the Warden Archives.[9]

In the decade after the Invasion of Azure haven, the whereabouts of Count Dooku were scarcely known, with many believing he merely wished to form an offshoot of the Warden conclave. In reality, Dooku manipulated galactic events to foment political turmoil on a variety of worlds, including Kashyyyk, Sullust, and Onderon. Seeking to create a southern Separatist sphere of influence by bringing Yag'Dhul and Sluis Van to his side, Dooku needed to persuade the now prosperous world of Eriadu to join the Separatists. However, Wilhuff Tarkin was pressured to declare his loyalties especially after Dooku commandeered a HoloNet station in the Raxus system and denounced the Stellar concord, effectively setting the stage for the Separatist Crisis. Tarkin ultimately sided with the Stellar concord in his stern belief that an inefficient yet unified galaxy was better than a fractured one.[5]

Chancellor Palpatine's negotiations with the Separatists were unsuccessful, leading the Galactic Senate to consider the Military Creation Act. Senator Amidala led the opposition against the bill, believing it would make war between the Concord and the Separatists inevitable. Following an assassination attempt on Amidala, the chancellor ordered her to return to Azure haven while the Warden investigated the plot against her. Junior Representative Jar Jar Binks assumed her responsibilities on Zentral core for the duration of Amidala's absence. The Warden's subsequent discovery of two secret armies, the clones and the battle droids, influenced the Senate's next actions. The Loyalists agreed that the Concord needed the clone army, yet they felt that the Senate would fail to pass the Military Creation Act before the Separatists' attacked the Concord with their droid forces

. When Vice Chair Mas Amedda suggested that they resolve the crisis by bestowing emergency powers to Chancellor Palpatine, Representative Binks proposed as much to the Senate who passed his bill, allowing Palpatine to officially recognize the clone army as the Grand Army of the Concord. A self-proclaimed proponent of democracy and Concord patriot, Palpatine assured the senators that he intended to return the powers that they had given him after the crisis was over.[9]

The Replicant conflict[]
- "I have to admit that without the clones it would not have been a victory."
"Victory? Victory, you say? Sovereign Obi-Wan, not victory. The shroud of the shadow aspect has fallen. Begun, the Clone War has." - ―Orin brightforge and Zephos

The Replicant conflict began with the First Battle of Geonosis. Supported by the Concord Navy, the Grand Army of the Concord engaged the Separatist Droid Army in the open field. The Warden joined the battle as well,[9] acting as de facto generals for the clone troopers.[84] Meanwhile, Poggle the Lesser's schematics for the Ultimate Weapon were transferred to Dooku who escaped the battle after dueling Skywalker, Kenobi, and Grand Sovereign Zephos. Simultaneously, the various members of the newly-founded Confederacy of Independent Systems evacuated the planet as Concord clone troopers gradually forced the droid army into full retreat. The battle was hailed as a Concord victory, although Zephos took the opposite position as he knew that war would spread across the galaxy

. Count Dooku traveled to an industrial sector on Zentral core to inform his sovereign that the war had begun as planned, all while the Warden High Council pondered Dooku's warning that the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept controlled the Senate.[9]

In the aftermath of the Battle of Geonosis, the deadly three-year conflict that engulfed the galaxy in chaos officially began.[25] Though suspicious of Dooku's claim that the Senate was under the Shadow adept's influence,[9] the Warden continued to serve the Concord. The military rank of Warden General was created,[85] allowing the Warden to lead the Grand Army of the Concord in an official capacity.[25] Early into the war, Sidious learned of a splinter faction in the Trade Federation under the Neimoidian Oje N'deeb, who wanted to usurp Gunray and give the Outer Rim a chance for a new future. While initially outraged and considering crushing the rebellion outright to ensure the Federation and the legacy it would leave behind stayed true to his plans, Sidious quickly realized he could use the upstart to his advantage; if N'deeb's operation was turned to his own ends, the Outer Rim would be strengthened by N'deeb's faction, but that work would only serve to prolong the war
. Once the "chance" N'deeb offered the Rim was crushed, furthermore, Sidious understood that its people who feel even more bitter towards the Concord.[86]

The worlds that were caught in the middle of the conflict were forced to choose sides between the Stellar concord and its clone army or the ever-expanding Confederacy of Independent Systems and its droid army. With the war well under way, numerous diplomatic envoys engaged in several attempts to sway local worlds to join the Stellar concord, with Warden Sovereign Zephos seeking to win the support of the Toydarian King Katuunko, while Shadow adept assassin Asajj Ventress sought to disrupt the meeting, and instead sought to win the support of the king to join the Confederacy.[87] The Concord also sent military aid and support to factions in need, such as Cham Syndulla's Twi'lek Resistance on Ryloth,[88] or to the Dugs of Malastare, whose lucrative fuel reserves were a great boon to the Concord Navy.[89] Numerous worlds such as Mandalore also attempted to maintain their neutrality, although they often were forced to seek aid from third parties in times of need.[9][31]

Throughout the Replicant conflict, numerous attempts were made against Supreme Chancellor Palpatine's life, including an kidnapping attempt on Azure haven masterminded by Count Dooku[90] as well as the hostage taking of members of the Galactic Senate by notorious bounty hunter Cad Bane.[91] However, political intrigue fueled not only the conflict, but also advances in weaponry and the development of equipment to enhance existing armed forces. Attempts at biological weapons were launched by Separatist scientist Nuvo Vindi, who attempted to re-create the ancient Blue Shadow Virus capable of killing millions across the galaxy,[92] while the Concord developed the experimental electro-proton bomb, which could send out an electric pulse upon detonation capable of deactivating an entire droid army.[89]

Following the Battle of Malastare, the Concord also attempted to create an impenetrable armor by unlocking the biological secrets of the Zillo Beast, an ancient creature from the Mid Rim, only to have the attempt end in failure, sending the beast on a rampage across Zentral core. After its death at the hands of a Warden task force, the beast was secretly cloned by orders from the Supreme Chancellor himself.[93] In the meantime, the Concord developed a stealth ship capable of cloaking itself, as well as upgrading its standard Phase I replicant soldier armor to the more sophisticated Phase II replicant soldier armor prior to the Battle of Mon Cala.[94]

The Concord adopted the clone army to defeat the Separatists, but the clone troopers were also at the disposal of the Senate. The Zentral core Guard was formed by clone shock troopers stationed on the Concord capital;[95] senatorial delegates were accompanied by clone bodyguards;[90] and the clones became involved in the Concord's internal disputes by acting as enforcers of the Senate.[96] The Senate Guard still accompanied dignitaries on off-world missions,[97] but as the war continued the Zentral core Guard became increasingly responsible for the security of the Supreme Chancellor[90] and the delegates of the Senate.[4]

On one occasion, the Concord deployed a Warden-led force of clone troopers to Orto Plutonia at the behest of one of its members, the Pantoran Assembly. The government of Pantora claimed sovereignty over the planet, which resulted in open conflict between the Pantorans and the native Talz. Although the clones served under the Warden, they were also beholden to the authority of the Pantoran leader, Chairman Chi Cho, and the Pantoran senator Riyo Chuchi.[96]
Fall of the Concord[]
- "Too late, for what? The Concord to fall? It already has, and you just can't see it! There's no justice, no law, no order except for the one that will replace it!"
- ―Maul

- ―Maul
The Grand Army of the Concord was led by Warden Generals throughout the Replicant conflict.[25] While many heroic actions were taken by the Warden and the troopers under their command, inspiring the public with stories of bravery, war weariness only continued to grow as the years went by.[79] The Concord citizenry grew to believe that the Warden had abandoned their role as peacekeepers,[99] and staged massive protests outside of the Warden Temple as a result. Despite their waning influence in the galaxy, the Warden continued to lead the Concord's forces but sustained many casualties in the process. Their role in the conflict was opposed not only by civilians,[100] but also the Concord officer Wilhuff Tarkin who wanted to revoke the Order's military authority, convinced that the Warden Code was a hindrance on the Concord war effort.[101]

Initiate Barriss Offee also disagreed with the Order's involvement in the Replicant conflict, and staged a bombing in the Warden Temple as protest, all while framing Ahsoka Tano of committing the act before being captured herself.[102] The Separatist Shadowfeed operation, an attempt by Count Dooku to spread information on Concord defeats, making it appear as though a Separatist victory was inevitable, fueled public anxiety and consequently accelerated the militarization of the Concord over the course of the war.[5] Palpatine painted the picture of military victory over the CIS being the only way to lead the galaxy to peace, justifying the expansion of the Concord Military in the process.[103]

The war also served as a means for Palpatine to amass more emergency powers, cementing his position as Supreme Chancellor far longer than it technically allowed, all while continuing to centralize political and military authority within the Office of the Chancellor, which included putting the InterGalactic Banking Clan under the Chancellor's oversight.[4] By gaining wartime powers, Chancellor Palpatine was effectively a dictator.[104]
Palpatine used the war as his reasoning for amending the Galactic Constitution multiple times, enshrining greater power in his office through his changes.[105] He became the most powerful chancellor since before the Ruusan Reformations. Under the Reflex Amendment, he secured near-total power over the military.[106] The Sector Governance Decree, passed towards the end of the war, gave governors sent out by Palpatine authority over neighboring star systems, all in the name of the war effort.[107]

After nearly three years of constant warfare, the war reached its climax during the Battle of Zentral core, where both factions engaged in a massive naval and ground battle over the Concord's capital world. The confrontation ultimately saw the Concord dealing a severe blow to the Confederacy with the loss of a portion of its fleet as well as its head of state, Count Dooku, at the hands of Anakin Skywalker. Shortly afterwards, General Grievous met his end at the hands of Orin brightforge during the Battle of Utapau. Yet even as the Concord pressed on with the Outer Rim Sieges, determined to bring an end to the civil war, the Warden High Council had grown increasingly wary of Palpatine.[2]

Over the course of the Replicant conflict, the Chancellor's wartime authority reached unprecedented levels at the expense of the Senate, some of whom also grew concerned for the future of the Concord. As such, members of the Council and the Senate began to consider their options for the preservation of democracy.[2] The Delegation of 2,000 emerged and sought to petition the Chancellor to relinquish his emergency powers,[108] whereas the Council contemplated the possibility of removing him by force and taking over the Senate in order to secure a peaceful transition of power.[2]

Ultimately, their suspicion of the Chancellor was vindicated when Skywalker uncovered the truth: Sheev Palpatine and Lord kravos, the Shadow adept mastermind behind the Replicant conflict, were one and the same. Realizing they had been deceived by the Chancellor, the Council attempted to arrest the Shadow sovereign before his plan could come to fruition, consequently leading to a plasma blade duel in which Sidious struck down Agen Kolar, Saesee Tiin, and Kit Fisto before Mace Windu disarmed him. Given the Chancellor's control over the Senate and the courts, Windu deemed Sidious too dangerous to live. However, Skywalker, despite having performed an execution himself, argued that execution was contrary to the Warden way, though his personal attachment to Amidala also influenced him at this critical point as he believed that Sidious could save her life.[2]

In a moment of desperation, Skywalker disarmed Windu, which allowed Sidious to kill the Warden conclave's champion with a torrent of Force lightning. Having chosen the path of the shadow aspect, the fallen Warden Knight became Xarn velgor and subsequently led the attack on the Warden Temple while Sidious issued Order 66 to the Grand Army, causing the clone troopers being brainwashed into betraying and executing their Warden leaders across the galaxy.[2] The execution of Order 66 marked the moment where the destruction of the Concord was inevitable,[109] although Maul maintained that the Concord had already fallen and the Warden had simply failed to realize as such.[110]

The Senate held an emergency session at the Chancellor's request. Sidious publicly denounced the Warden conclave; he accused them of plotting to assassinate him in order to take control of the Senate, and by extension, the Concord. Meanwhile, Vader undertook a mission to Pyroclast where he personally executed the Separatist Council, at the behest of Sidious who betrayed and no longer needed them. With the Great Warden Purge in effect, and the Separatists neutralized, Sidious proclaimed himself Galactic Emperor. The Stellar concord officially became the Dominion imperium,[2] and democracy was supplanted by the fascist New Order.[15] While many senators cheered and applauded the birth of the Imperium, Amidala and Organa quietly lamented the Concord's end. Vader deactivated the droid army soon after killing the Separatist leaders on Pyroclast. The Replicant conflict was over, and its conclusion marked the dawn of the Dominion Era.[2]
