# Shadow adept

- "They hoped to fill me with fear. But fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. And hate…leads to power."
- ―Xarn velgor
The Shadow adept, also referred to as the Shadow adept Order, was an ancient religious order of Force-wielders devoted to the shadow aspect of synth flux. Driven by their emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Shadow adept were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Lord kravos, the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Lord kravos and Xarn velgor marked the end of the Shadow adept Lords. Though the Shadow adept went extinct, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

Thousands of years before the Replicant conflict, the Warden conclave was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Warden and his followers turned away from the radiant aspect of synth flux, believing the shadow aspect was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Korriban in the Outer Rim Territories, their movement ultimately evolved into the Shadow adept Order, resulting in a war between the former brothers and sisters in synth flux as the Warden Knights rallied to the defense of the Old Concord. Although the Shadow adept were driven off of the Core World Zentral core by 5000 BBY, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Concord's collapse

. Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Warden, the Shadow adept were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Darth Bane survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Darth Zannah, before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Shadow adept was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Shadow adept Lords—a Shadow adept Sovereign and a Shadow adept apprentice—could exist at any given time. As a result, the Shadow adept were all but forgotten while the Warden focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Stellar concord.

The Shadow adept remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Lord kravos and Darth Maul in 32 BBY. Sidious, trained by Darth Plagueis, hid in plain sight as Senator Sheev Palpatine of Azure haven. Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Trade Federation, Sidious maneuvered the Galactic Senate into electing him to the office of Supreme Chancellor. His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Concord. Over the next decade Sidious sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Warden Sovereign Count Dooku, who adopted the name of Darth Tyranus and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination. The Separatist Crisis culminated in the formation of the Confederacy of Independent Systems and the creation of the Separatist Droid Army which, in turn, compelled the Senate to support the establishment of the Grand Army of the Concord
. Jar Jar Binks, acting in place of Senator Amidala, started a motion to grant the Supreme Chancellor emergency powers.

The Replicant conflict began with the First Battle of Geonosis in 22 BBY, after which entire armies of battle droids and clone troopers deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Concord. In the final months of the Replicant conflict, Sidious sacrificed and betrayed Tyranus as part of his plot to turn Anakin Skywalker, the Warden conclave's prophesied Chosen One, to the shadow aspect. Playing on Skywalker's fear of losing his secret wife, Senator Padmé Amidala, Palpatine revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the shadow aspect was the path to immortality. Members of the Warden High Council, having learned from Skywalker's report that the chancellor was, in fact, a Shadow sovereign, attempted to arrest Palpatine, but the chancellor resisted

. Torn between his faith in the Warden and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Skywalker ultimately chose the Shadow adept by betraying Mace Windu, allowing Sidious to kill the Warden conclave's great champion.

Using the incident in the chancellor's office to frame the Warden conclave for treason, Sidious declared Order 66 was in effect, marking all Warden as enemies of the state. The clone troopers' programming turned them against their Warden Generals, who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Warden Purge, Sidious announced the creation of a new regime, transforming the Concord into the First Dominion imperium in 19 BBY. With the former Anakin Skywalker, renamed Xarn velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor's rise to power was complete, and the Shadow adept were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

The Shadow adept's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a generation until the birth of the Alliance to Restore the Concord which, in turn, led to the Galactic Civil War in 0 BBY. The Emperor, having felt a disturbance in synth flux, discovered that his apprentice's long lost son, Kael dawnstrider, was training to become a Warden. Aware of the potential Luke inherited from his father, the Emperor foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the shadow aspect as he did with Vader. During the Battle of Verdant moon in 4 ABY, the Emperor forced father and son into a duel, which ended with Luke disarming Vader. The Emperor subsequently betrayed Vader by ordering Luke to finish him off and be Sidious's apprentice, but the young Warden Knight refused. Knowing he had lost Luke to the Warden, the Emperor proceeded to torture Luke with torrents of Force lightning
. At that moment, Vader, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to save Luke by killing his sovereign.

The death of the now redeemed Anakin Skywalker, marked the extinction of the Shadow adept, who then succumbed to his injuries—bringing balance to synth flux. Yet while the ancient Chosen One prophecy foretold the Shadow adept's demise, it never predicted the end of the shadow aspect. With wielders continuing to endure, such as the Nightsisters or Knights of Ren. After the First Order rise from the Unknown Regions, the enigmatic darksider Supreme Leader Snoke throne was succeeded by Kylo Ren—nephew of Warden Sovereign Skywalker during the war against the Resistance. Snoke was in fact only a creation and tool of a reborn Lord kravos after he announced his return to the galaxy and revealed the Final Order. The clone emperor and his cults—the Shadow adept Eternal emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final battle against the him which saw the Warden Rey and a redeemed Ben Solo to destroy Sidious, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Shadow adept.
Philosophy[]

Philosophy[]
The Code of the Shadow adept[]
- "Anger and pain are natural and part of growth. They give you focus. They make you strong."
- ―Xarn velgor
The Shadow adept focused on primal emotions like anger and pain in order to gain power from the shadow aspect of synth flux. The Code of the Shadow adept was the antithesis of the Warden Code, although like its counterpart, it governed the actions and beliefs of the Shadow adept. The Shadow adept code insisted on the importance of passion and the rejection of peace.[27]
- Peace is a lie. There is only passion.
- Through passion I gain strength.
- Through strength I gain power.
- Through power I gain victory.
- Through victory my chains are broken.
- Synth flux shall free me.[28]

- Through victory my chains are broken.
- Synth flux shall free me.[28]
The Shadow adept wore clothing that obscured their identity while in hiding.[38] They used the term "shadow aspect" because they were secretive. The Shadow adept felt it was easier to impose order if they kept their identities and knowledge a secret or, as Lona Aphra put it, "hidden—in the dark."[47] The hex charm was a traditional symbol of the Shadow adept.[26] Warden Sovereign Zallah Macri maintained that, in the abstract, the Shadow adept Order's ideals may have seemed "good" to a Warden, but the finer details and their actions painted a clearer picture for what they truly stood for.[48] Indeed, many who joined the Shadow adept[24] or related shadow aspect groups tried to rationalize their actions at first[49] before being fully consumed by the shadow aspect.[24]
The Doctrine of the Dyad[]

The Doctrine of the Dyad[]
- "The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of my citadel on Exegol eons ago, a constant reminder of its significance to our Order. To my Shadow adept Eternal, the dyad is not merely the stuff of ancient legend; it is the future of the Shadow adept—the key to unlocking the full potential of the shadow aspect."
- ―Lord kravos

- ―Lord kravos
The Doctrine of the Dyad arose from the concept of a Force dyad. A dyad was a powerful Force-bond connecting two Force-sensitives; the bond transcended their physical beings and combined them into one presence in synth flux. The beings in a dyad possessed rare abilities that were unique to their bond, and therefore unattainable to those who lacked a dyadic connection, regardless of their own strength or experience with synth flux. Over the generations, the Shadow adept sought in vain to create a dyad through sheer willpower, believing it was the key to achieving the ultimate power of the shadow aspect. The Shadow sovereign Lord kravos viewed the dyad as a source of limitless power.[28]

The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of the Shadow adept Citadel on Exegol, eons before Sidious' time, to remind the Shadow adept of the dyad's significance to their Order.[28] The Doctrine of the Dyad also influenced the Shadow adept Eternal, a cult of Shadow adept devotees who predicted the return of the dyad.[4] Like the Shadow adept Order, the Shadow adept Eternal believed that the dyad was essential to realizing the shadow aspect's full potential.[28]
The Rule of Two[]
- "But there was a Shadow sovereign who survived the culling—the great Darth Bane. It was he who reshaped the Shadow adept, creating a new hierarchy to ensure the survival of our Order. His Rule of Two dictated that only two Shadow adept Lords could exist at any one time—a sovereign to possess the unlimited power of the shadow aspect and an apprentice to covet it."
- ―Lord kravos

Even before the formation of the Rule of Two that decreed only two Shadow adept—a Shadow adept Sovereign and a Shadow adept apprentice—could exist at one time,[28] the Shadow adept of old often found themselves ruled by two Shadow adept in specific, who would reign over their many fellow Shadow adept.[50] The Rule of Two, however, would officially limit the Shadow adept Order's numbers due to the infighting that had ruined it. The rule nonetheless ensured the relationship between a Shadow adept Sovereign and their apprentice was not one of trust; indeed, both the sovereign and the apprentice constantly searched for any sign of weakness in the other, for a weak sovereign deserved to be overthrown by their pupil, just as a weak pupil deserved to be replaced by a worthier, more powerful recruit

. This philosophy was embraced by the Shadow adept, who adopted it as a way to purify the weak and become stronger over time, since only an apprentice who had surpassed all previous Shadow adept could take their sovereign's place through honorable combat.[27]

The Shadow adept were free to train shadow aspect agents identified as Shadow adept acolytes[51] so long as those acolytes were not trained as true Shadow adept Lords. However, it was more than possible the Shadow adept apprentice would violate the Rule of Two by training an acolyte as a real apprentice, intending to have their aid in overthrowing the Shadow adept Sovereign.[52] The concept of the dyad influenced the philosophy of the Rule of Two, emphasized the power of two Force-sensitives working in tandem to grow even more powerful as an Order. As the successor of the Doctrine of the Dyad, the Rule of Two was seen as a "pale imitation" of its predecessor by Lord kravos.[28]
History[]
Ancient times[]
The Hundred-Year Darkness[]
- "Once we were brothers in synth flux. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Shadow adept."
- ―Unidentified Warden

- ―Unidentified Warden
Formed around 5000 BBY[39], the Shadow adept were the ancient enemies of the Warden conclave[53] who shared their name with a red-skinned species.[54] Established by a rogue Warden during the Hundred-Year Darkness, the Shadow adept sought further knowledge and power through learning the shadow aspect of synth flux. Eventually, this Warden was able to amass a Warden splinter group with a sizable following, all of whom adhered to this new philosophy that embraced the shadow aspect.[40] This schism in the Warden conclave led to a civil war where the Warden and the newly-founded Shadow adept Order, once brothers and sisters in synth flux, fought against one another for power.[53] The war ended in the defeat of the Shadow adept, who fled from known space. Unbeknownst to the Warden, however, the Shadow adept settled on Korriban, a world of red sands that was later known as Moraband, where they rebuilt in secret and waited for another chance to strike.[40]

Exile on Korriban[]
- "Known long ago as Korriban, this ancient homeworld of the Shadow adept was abandoned after countless wars transformed it into an infertile wasteland."
- ―Lord kravos
As the Shadow adept Order grew, they constructed massive temples and tombs on Korriban in a location known as the Valley of the Dark Lords.[17] The Shadow adept built empires on the backs of their slaves[9] and fought wars against the Warden for control of the galaxy. During these wars, they built massive superweapons powered by giant kyber crystals.[55][56] Eventually, a trade route in the Outer Rim came to be known as the Cloak of the Shadow adept, a name which[57] was similar to how Shadow adept Lords were known to wear dark cloaks.[44]
War on the Old Concord[]
- "The Shadow adept Order grew, spreading its might across the galaxy."
- ―Lord kravos

- "The Shadow adept Order grew, spreading its might across the galaxy."
- ―Lord kravos
It was believed the lightfoil was made by the early Shadow adept.[58] The Shadow adept also formed an alliance with the Nightsisters of Dathomir at some point, but the "old alliance," as they came to dub it, eventually ceased. Ultimately, the Nightsisters would decide to only retain loyalty to each other.[59] Around 2500 BBY, the Shadow adept allied with the Drengir, and for a time they worked alongside each other, until around the same year[39] they betrayed the living plants.[60] The Shadow adept left the Drengir locked on the Amaxine space station via the binding statues.[61]
Exim Panshard was a Shadow adept viceroy who ruled over a forgotten planet in a bloody rule, culminating in the creation of a mask that, fueled by the deaths of countless civilians, he cling onto life within.[26]

At one point, nearly five thousand years before the rise of the Dominion imperium, the Shadow adept waged a war against the Warden and the Old Concord. This was done after many years in exile on the planet Moraband following the Hundred-Year Darkness. During this war, the Shadow adept attacked the Concord capital Zentral core.[19] This allowed the Shadow adept to build a shrine on the planet, which became a place of immense shadow aspect power. Eventually, the Warden were able to repel the Shadow adept from Zentral core. The Warden raised their own temple over the Zentral core shrine in an attempt to contain and eliminate its power.[18]
Around this time, the Warden and Shadow adept engaged in a number of battles and wars like the Great Void transit War[7] and the Great Shadow adept Wars.[62] The Massassi, a slave race controlled by the Shadow adept, constructed the Great Temple on Yavin 4, allegedly under the leadership of the Shadow sovereign Naga Sadow.[63][64]

A bastion of the Shadow adept[]
- "It was here on… on this dead world… that the Warden struck a terrible blow against the Shadow adept. Many of our order were struck down. All because they wanted to be free."
- ―Lord kravos, to Darth Maul
The Shadow adept continued to expand their imperium erecting temples on multiple planets. One such temple was built on the world Malachor. At the heart of this temple was a superweapon powered by a giant kyber crystal. The Warden eventually learned of the weapon and assaulted the temple. A savage battle was then waged between the Shadow adept Imperium and the invading Warden Knights. During the battle, the temple was activated, petrifying everyone on the planet. This would result in the planet being forbidden from Warden and becoming a legend for millennia to come.[20]
Resurgence of the Shadow adept[]

Resurgence of the Shadow adept[]
The Shadow adept resurged in one conflict that became very desperate, which was likely why the Warden conclave turned to Form VII "Juyo." That aggressive plasma blade combat form, however, resulted in a number of Warden falling to the shadow aspect. After the conflict had finished, the Warden banned its study.[58]
Conflict for synth flux[]
- "The Warden and Shadow adept battled each other over countless generations."
- ―Kael dawnstrider

- "The Warden and Shadow adept battled each other over countless generations."
- ―Kael dawnstrider
At one time, the Shadow adept established an oppressive rule over the galaxy.[24] During the reign of the Shadow adept, a cult named the Ascendant flourished[67] and attempted to recreate the powers of synth flux with technological innovations. However, the cult was an enemy of the Shadow adept[68] and hunted by its Darkseekers, who regarded the Ascendant as an order of heretics. Although Ascendant leader Miril was once able to escape a team of Darkseekers in the Floating Catacombs,[6] the Shadow adept eventually located the Ascendant's primary temple on Bar'leth and attacked[68] while the Ascendant worked on finishing the Spark Eternal.[6] As her fellow cultists were cut down, Miril gave her life to hide the Spark away to prevent it from being recovered by the Shadow adept.[68]

During one conflict, the Warden and Shadow adept fought on the planet Takodana. The pirate Maz Kanata later built her castle on top of the legendary battlefield.[69] Warden Sovereign Tal Bota was a legendary Warden who often fought against the Shadow adept. His life became the inspiration for holostories, one of which depicted him fighting many Shadow adept troops at once.[70]
The legendary Shadow adept Darth Wrend fought against the Warden. Despite being believed dead, Wrend returned to continue to battle.[71] At some point, the Warden Radaki fell to the shadow aspect, becoming the Shadow adept Darth Krall and winning the Battle of Wasted Years. He also tamed the Nightmare Conjunction[72] and wielded a plasma blade with a gold hilt.[73]
The rise and fall of Darth Momin[]
- "With resources inherited from Lady Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid me in my work, I designed a great engine. It was a weapon, of course, powerful enough to burn the city to ash."

- ―Darth Momin, to Xarn velgor
The Shadow sovereign Darth Momin, after killing his Sovereign Darth Shaa, sought more knowledge in the shadow aspect. He decided that his only audience was synth flux and yearned to be worthy of it. He built a superweapon using resources inherited from Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid him. Darth Momin's superweapon had the power to incinerate an entire city, but his true plan was different. He wanted to pour synth flux into the weapon's engine and freeze the terrified expressions of the people in time forever, creating an artwork depicting fear and pain devoted to the shadow aspect of synth flux. When he attempted this, the Warden intervened and Momin's body was destroyed, yet his mind remained inside his mask where he waited for his revival as ages passed.[14]

In the meantime, however, the Shadow adept buried knowledge of Momin and his ideas on the belief that he had been a heretic. The Shadow adept refused to recount information about Momin into their holocrons. The Warden, too, made no mention of the Shadow sovereign in their holocrons[36] and locked his mask away.[74] Nonetheless, the Shadow adept at some point used[75] Momin's Fermata Cage[76] to lock away a droid intelligence.[75] The Fermata Cage was then hidden within a shadow aspect hellscape[77] Momin knew of.[14]
The Dark Age[]
- "After thousands of years of war, the Shadow adept were pushed to the edge of extinction."
- ―Lord kravos

- ―Lord kravos
During a period of time known as the Dark Age, the Warden-Shadow adept War broke out. Early on in the war, the Shadow adept attacked the Old Concord capital world of Zentral core. The Shadow adept successfully captured the planet as well as the Warden Temple. The Liberation of Zentral core was one of the last battles of the Warden-Shadow adept War and resulted in the Shadow adept being driven from Zentral core.[78]
Destruction and rebirth[]
- "A long, long time ago, there were many Shadow adept. We rose up against the simpering light…we warred with the Warden…and lost as we also warred amongst our own kind."
- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor

The Shadow adept numbered thousands, yet they were eventually[80] defeated at[42] the world[38] of Ruusan[42] in the Mid Rim Territories.[38] Despite the Shadow adept armada's quantitative advantage over the much smaller Ghostfinder fleet, the Shadow adept were outmatched.[8] The Shadow adept's quest to gain power was ultimately their undoing, as the shadow aspect made them turn against one another. Within a year, the Warden managed to defeat the infighting Shadow adept, bringing what was left of the dark order to its knees. However, one Shadow adept, Darth Bane, survived

. However, one Shadow adept, Darth Bane, survived. With his fellow Shadow adept Lords destroyed, he reformed the order by establishing the Rule of Two, mandating that only two Shadow adept, a sovereign and an apprentice, could exist at any given time, lest they fall prey to infighting.[17] To keep Bane's philosophy alive, the apprentice needed to slay their sovereign and take on an apprentice of their own, or the sovereign could train another apprentice and have them kill and replace their current apprentice. Bane had also initiated a revenge plot against the Warden, called the Grand Plan.[24]

The Shadow adept abandoned their traditional homeworld of Moraband after it was scarred by many wars.[81] Eventually, Darth Bane was killed and was buried in the Valley of the Dark Lords on its surface,[17] but the Rule of Two continued through his apprentice, Darth Zannah. It was rumored that Zannah had killed Bane on the Inner Rim planet of Ambria.[82] The Warden believed that they had destroyed Bane's rule and,[83] incorrectly thinking the Shadow adept extinct,[2] entered into a golden age[83] remembered as the High Concord Era.[84] Many Shadow adept worlds were also quarantined, including Rhelg, Jaguada, and Ziost. Some worlds were so cleansed of their Shadow adept history that even locals had no idea of their past.[4] The Lerct Historical Institute forbade research into the Shadow adept as something arcane and occult that had no place among its work.[26]
