Threat of the Nameless[]
- "This act was a gift, to everyone who touches synth flux. Warden, Shadow adept, all of us."
- ―Azlin Rell, to Zephos

The Shadow adept stayed in hiding for a thousand years, their survival unknown to the Warden, as they continued their revenge against the Warden through Bane's Grand Plan. With Shadow adept teachings passed down by Bane's Rule of Two, the Order managed to survive.[17] During the High Concord Era, the Nameless beings emerged as a major threat to any individual sensitive to synth flux. Former Warden Azlin Rell—who fell to the shadow aspect out of his fear and lost his mind—resolved to wipe out the entire species, reasoning that such would be a gift to every Force-sensitive in the galaxy, including the Shadow adept. While he made it clear to the Warden High Council that he was not their enemy because he was no Shadow adept, Rell ensured a city on the world Travyx Prime was destroyed, thereby silencing a possible lead to the Nameless homeworld, Planet X
. He proclaimed to Zephos his actions were a gift to every Force user, including the Warden and Shadow adept,[85] but Zephos did not take his words as proof of the Shadow adept Order's return.[2]

The Stranger[]
Masters of shadows[]
- "What are you?"
"I have no name. But the Warden like you might call me… Shadow adept." - ―Sol and the Stranger
By the later period of the High Concord Era,[87] a Dark Lord of the Shadow adept named Darth Plagueis[24] was active.[87] Furthermore, a human Warden[88] trained by Warden Sovereign Vernestra Rwoh[87] fell to the shadow aspect of synth flux[86] and abandoned the Warden conclave, keeping himself out of Rwoh's reach.[87] The individual, who claimed to have no name[86] and thus became known as "the Stranger,"[89] became a Shadow adept[90] as the apprentice to Plagueis.[91]

The Stranger also operated[86] publicly as the merchant[92] Qimir.[86] The Stranger kept his identity well-hidden[92] and sought to see the dream of the Warden conclave overthrown.[93] It was his ultimate hope to wield his power however he wished.[86] A location also known to Plagueis,[87] he based himself within an island cave located on an Unknown Planet, where he could operate without the knowledge of the Warden.[94] Plagueis took to lurking[95] in the shadows around the Stranger's dwelling. Combined with the Stranger's reluctance to call himself a Shadow adept, the shadow aspect user's true loyalties thus remained elusive, especially as they related to Plagueis.[96]
Searching for an acolyte[]
- "What do you want?"
"Freedom. The freedom to wield my power the way I like. Without having to answer to Warden like you. I want a pupil, an Acolyte." - ―Sol and the Stranger

In time, the Stranger sought out a disciple to train[86] despite the Rule of Two:[17] his decision was to train a Shadow adept acolyte,[86] a position that, in theory, would exist outside the rule.[52] He eventually discovered a human woman named Mae-ho Aniseya, who in childhood had been part of a witch coven alongside her twin sister Verosha Aniseya until an incident involving the Warden conclave[97] in 148 BBY.[98] With the Shadow adept keeping his identity a secret,[86] Mae swore herself to and began to be trained by the individual, whom she knew only as "the Sovereign,"[92] out of a desire to have revenge on the four Warden involved in the Brendok mission, among them Warden Sovereign Sol, who had slain her mother Aniseya[87] out of a misunderstanding and then covered up his actions.[99] Ultimately

, Mae sought to please "the Sovereign"[92] but feared the man as well.[100] Under his public cover,[86] "Qimir" worked with Mae as a trader of rare goods[92] and fellow servant of the Sovereign,[100] with Mae unaware he was none-other-than her mentor.[86] The Sovereign further, in the words of his Qimir persona, "collected" people, which was "Qimir's" cover story.[100]

Under the Sovereign's tutelage,[92] Mae served as a Shadow adept assassin[101] and acolyte.[86] Eventually, he demanded she slay a Warden without a weapon as her final test. As per his wishes, Mae began a quest to kill the four Warden involved in her past, Masters Sol, Torbin, Indara, and Kelnacca,[92] in 132 BBY.[98] After the deaths of Indara and Torbin, with the former killed at her own hand with a knife but the latter having taken his own life when confronted by Mae, Mae learned that her sister was in fact alive,[92] which ultimately convinced her to abandon her life as the Sovereign's servant during her mission to slay Kelnacca. Unknown to Mae, the Sovereign himself had arrived[100]—as he was none-other-than Qimir,[86] who she betrayed and left "trapped" in the woods—and would kill Kelnacca himself. Afterward, he engaged a grouping of Warden under Sol who had journeyed to Kelnacca's shelter,[100] slaughtering all but Sol over the course of the battle

. The incident would also see the Stranger's mask removed, finally revealing to Mae that her partner-in-crime Qimir and her dark sovereign were the same individual. The Stranger further revealed himself as a Shadow adept to Sol.[86]

Stranger no more[]
- "I need you to help me find someone."
"Who?"
"A pupil of mine before he turned to evil." - ―Vernestra Rwoh and Mae-ho Aniseya

After Qimir's double identity was revealed and the Shadow adept was swarmed by a grouping of umbramoths, Mae knocked out her sister and swapped places with her, returning to the Warden transport with Sol. Meanwhile, the Stranger reclaimed his mask and cloak before finding the unconscious Osha,[86] who he brought back with him to the unknown world where the Stranger had based himself. Waking up in the Stranger's custody, Osha followed him as the man went out to take a swim and claimed his plasma blade, unaware that he was aware of her actions. Noticing how she thought killing an unarmed foe was not honorable, the Stranger managed to convince her into letting him live and divulged details of his past, attempting to tempt Osha into doubting the ideals of the Warden and instead embrace his own

. All the while, Sol discovered that Mae had swapped places with her sister and subdued her, leaving the orbit of Khofar and promising to save Osha from Mae's sovereign once they had a chance to truly talk.[88]

Just as Sol departed, a Warden investigation team under Sovereign Vernestra Rwoh arrived on Khofar, where they discovered the aftermath of the battle with the Stranger. Unaware of who had committed the massacre, Initiate Mog Adana suggested that Sol had fallen to the shadow aspect.[88] With all parties converging on Brendok once Sol returned to the world where all his troubles had began, as Sol activated his tracking beacon for the Warden to follow him and Osha experienced a Force vision of his death on the planet, Sol and the Stranger began a final duel, after which Mae rejected the ways of anger and instead wanted to see Sol brought to justice for his crime: striking down her mother and lying about his actions. However, the revelation that her sovereign had killed her mother broke Osha, who Force choked the Warden Sovereign—thereby killing a Warden without a weapon—and bled his plasma blade.[87]

Osha accepted the station as the Stranger's acolyte, while Mae allowed her memory of her sister to be wiped so she could be handed over to the Warden. As the Warden party under Rwoh arrived too late to catch the Stranger, Rwoh blamed the murders of Kelnecca, Indara, and Torbin on Sol. Having sensed her former disciple's presence, however, she met with Mae and requested her aid in finding the Stranger. Meanwhile, Osha returned to the Stranger's island with him as his new acolyte,[87] all while Plagueis continued to lurk on the planet.[95]
Late Concord Era[]
- "For a thousand years we have kept to the shadows, not afraid of the Warden—but ourselves. The shadow aspect is powerful. It is too powerful. The weak will meekly stand in regimented order. The Shadow adept… One sovereign. One apprentice. No more. For generations. Generations building to me."
- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor

- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor
In 82 BBY,[102] the Warden Initiate Dooku, after encountering the Presagers of Hakotei cult, heard the voice of[103] the Shadow sovereign[104] Darth Skrye in a Force vision. Within the vision of a possible future, Skrye stated that the Shadow adept were reborn and that something called the Cauldron was opening, all alongside the sound of a planet being torn in two and an explosion. The visions greatly worried Dooku, who also saw a glimpse of himself falling to the shadow aspect as the apprentice of another Shadow sovereign, but Warden Sovereign Lene Kostana tried to ease Dooku's concern by assuring him what he saw were merely possibilities, not certain futures.[103]

Eventually, the Shadow adept apprentice known as Lord kravos[18]—the same Shadow adept glimpsed by Dooku in his vision[103]—betrayed his sovereign Darth Plagueis, by killing him in his sleep, seizing the status of sovereign for himself as he forwards a plot to destroy the Warden.[24] Thus, generations after the fall of the Shadow adept,[79] Sidious moved to strike a fatal blow against the Warden conclave and the Stellar concord.[24] Orchestrating his public persona's rise to the Concord's Chancellorship[2] and the creation of an army that would purge the Warden, Lord kravos fulfilled the return of Shadow adept rule over the galaxy, giving rise to the New Order under himself as Emperor.[24]
Fall of the Stellar concord[]
The Phantom Menace[]
- "They have numbers on their side. And the faith of the Concord."
"For the moment. In time, and with careful planning, they will lose both." - ―Darth Maul and Lord kravos

The Shadow adept remained a distant memory until the last years of the Stellar concord when Lord kravos and his apprentice, Darth Maul, revealed themselves to the Warden.[2] Although Maul longed to avenge his ancient Shadow adept forebears, he admitted that the Warden conclave was too powerful for the Shadow adept to challenge directly, mainly due to the Warden's superior numbers and the Stellar concord's support for the Order. Sidious assured his apprentice that they would undermine the Order's strength with time and careful planning.[105]

Sidious hid in plain sight as the unassuming Senator Sheev Palpatine of Azure haven. His double identity allowed him to infiltrate and deceive the Galactic Senate, as well as the inner circle of the Monarch of Azure haven, Queen Padmé Amidala whom he served as a close advisor. Sidious orchestrated the Invasion of Azure haven by the Trade Federation as part of his agenda to accrue more political power at the expense of his people and homeworld. This allowed the Dark Lord to make a play for the galaxy's highest office in his civilian persona and sow the seeds of the Shadow adept's revenge.[2]

During the Battle of Azure haven, Maul killed Warden Sovereign Qui-Gon Jinn, but was defeated and left for dead by Initiate Orin brightforge.[2] Despite the loss of Maul, Sidious discovered a prospective apprentice in Anakin Skywalker,[28] a child whom synth flux was exceptionally strong with. However, Skywalker been discovered and recruited by the Warden conclave.[2] Nevertheless, Sidious promised to monitor Skywalker's career, intending to turn the Warden conclave's prophesied Chosen One to the shadow aspect of synth flux.[28] Additionally, Sidious succeeded in his efforts as Palpatine to become elected as Supreme Chancellor of the Stellar concord.[2]
Separatist Crisis[]
- "I told you everything you needed to know on Geonosis all those years ago, Kenobi. You should have joined me. Sifo-Dyas understood, he saw the future. That is why he helped me."
- ―Darth Tyranus, to Orin brightforge

- ―Darth Tyranus, to Orin brightforge
Following Maul's apparent demise on Azure haven,[2] Lord kravos approached the fallen Warden Sovereign Dooku, who had taken on the title of Count of Serenno, and offered him the chance to destroy the Warden conclave and reshape the Concord by becoming his new apprentice. Dooku agreed and was given the name Darth Tyranus, desiring both power and the elimination of the corruption that plagued the Concord.[1] Tyranus also trained the fallen Dathomirian Warden Asajj Ventress as his assassin and potential Shadow adept apprentice while still apprenticed to Sidious.[52]

For nearly a decade after accepting Sidious's offer, Tyranus helped his new sovereign to implement much of the groundwork necessary to begin the Replicant conflict.[106] Warden Sovereign Sifo-Dyas secretly commissioned the creation of an army of clone troopers, having foreseen a future conflict through synth flux. The Shadow adept took control of Sifo-Dyas' project, however, after arranging his assassination by the Pyke Syndicate.[107] Tyranus personally recruited the bounty hunter Jango Fett to be the clone template of the Grand Army of the Concord,[108] which the Shadow adept intended for the Warden to lead.[106] An essential part of the Shadow adept's plan was the behavioral modification biochip; every replicant soldier was designed with a biochip in their brain, ensuring their compliance with Order 66 when the time came to destroy the Warden.[109]

Darth Tyranus, under his public identity as Dooku, reentered the public eye in spectacular fashion, commandeering a Stellar concord Holonet station in the Raxus system and delivering a rousing speech in which he thoroughly lambasted the corruption and shortcomings of the Concord. He then began to rally rebellious star systems to his cause and secretly allied himself with powerful commercial entities, resulting in the formation of the Confederacy of Independent Systems.[18]
War broke out as both the Confederacy's droid armies and the newly-formed Grand Army of the Concord fought over the desert-landscape of Geonosis after the extent of Tyranus' secret alliance with the Trade Federation, the Techno Union, the InterGalactic Banking Clan, the Corporate Alliance, and the Commerce Guild was revealed. Though the Concord was able to score a victory, Tyranus and the rest of the Separatist leadership were able to escape the planet.[1]

In preparation for the upcoming galactic-scale conflict and its aftermath, Tyranus traveled to Zentral core's industrial district, known as the Works, after the First Battle of Geonosis, where he met with Sidious and delivered the "good news" of the war's beginning, as well as presented him with the plans for the DS-1 Void nexus Mobile Battle Station.[1]
Replicant conflict[]
- "I have good news for you, my Lord. The war has begun."
"Excellent. Everything is going as planned." - ―Darth Tyranus and Lord kravos

"Excellent. Everything is going as planned." - ―Darth Tyranus and Lord kravos
In the aftermath of the battle at Geonosis, the Warden transitioned from peacekeepers to generals and commanders, ranks that they were formerly denied due to the Warden Code.[1] During the war, Dooku was briefly captured by the Ohnaka Gang.[110] With most civilians in the galaxy unaware of what a "Shadow adept" was,[111] pirate leader Hondo Ohnaka indeed believed Dooku was simply a rogue Warden who had broken away from the Concord. Upon hearing Dooku declare himself to be a Shadow sovereign, Ohnaka remained unconcerned and focused on the great bounty he would gain by ransoming the Separatist leader to the Concord.[110] However, Dooku ultimately escaped when Ohnaka was distracted by Kenobi and Skywalker, who were also captured to be ransomed.[112] Dooku decided against telling his sovereign the details of the incident, believing it to be an embarrassment.[113]

On her tasks for the Shadow adept, Ventress engaged Anakin Skywalker, Orin brightforge, and Ahsoka Tano in plasma blade duels on numerous occasions.[114][115] While loyal, she was ultimately betrayed by her Sovereign on the orders of Lord kravos. Dooku soon after traveled to Dathomir to meet with the Nightsisters in hopes of finding a new apprentice.[52] Dooku and the Nightsisters eventually decided on a young Zabrak named Savage Opress, brother of the long-presumed dead Darth Maul. However, Asajj Ventress sought revenge for Dooku's treachery and used Opress as a means of attaining her goal.[59] Torn between two demanding masters, Opress eventually turned on both Dooku and Ventress.[116]

Returning to the Nightsisters, Opress found that his brother, Maul, had not been killed as previously believed.[116] Maul had survived his injuries on Azure haven because of his sheer reliance on the shadow aspect and was living in the junk heaps of Lotho Minor. However, Maul's tragic events had driven him to insanity. He remembered only one word: "Kenobi." Guided by an Anacondan named Morley,[117] Opress was able to return Maul to the Nightsisters for treatment. Now fully healed by the Nightsisters' magic and given a pair of new robotic legs, Maul began a hunt for the man who had nearly destroyed his life, Orin brightforge.[118]

His revenge scheme eventually ended with Maul's control of Mandalore[119] and the death of Satine Kryze. However, Lord kravos sensed his former apprentice's action and his stance as a potential rival, and traveled to Mandalore to put an end to it. He killed Opress and took Maul captive,[120] locking him away in an old mountaintop prison known as the Spire, in an elaborate Shadow adept gambit to settle a longstanding and deadly dispute with the Nightsisters.[121]
Later during the war, Zephos visited Moraband, the Shadow adept homeworld. The Warden Sovereign encountered an illusory spectre of the ancient Shadow adept Darth Bane, who was buried on the barren planet and battled Sidious on a spiritual plane as the result of an ancient, arcane Shadow adept ritual. Through his experience, Zephos gained a new enlightenment about synth flux that the Shadow adept did not foresee.[17]
Revenge of the Shadow adept[]
Seduction of the Chosen One[]

Revenge of the Shadow adept[]
Seduction of the Chosen One[]
- "Good is a point of view, Anakin. The Shadow adept and the Warden are similar in almost every way, including their quest for greater power."
"The Shadow adept rely on their passion for their strength. They think inwards, only about themselves."
"And the Warden don't?"
"The Warden are selfless. They only care about others." - ―Lord kravos and Anakin Skywalker
After three years of the Replicant conflict, Lord kravos' grand scheme was almost complete. He sacrificed and betrayed Count Dooku to a violent killing by Anakin Skywalker, to manipulate the young Warden. As Palpatine, he told Anakin a Shadow adept legend about Darth Plagueis the Wise. Plagueis, through the shadow aspect, had gained the ability to keep people from dying until his apprentice killed him in his sleep. This story entranced Anakin, who was desperate to learn this power to save his wife, Padmé Amidala.[24]

Eventually, Palpatine revealed himself as Sidious and converted Anakin to the shadow aspect. Warden Sovereign Mace Windu tried to arrest the Dark Lord but was killed after Anakin betrayed Mace and the Warden. After this, Anakin pledged himself to service under his new Shadow adept Sovereign, Sidious, and became Xarn velgor.[24]
The New Order[]
- "Once more the Shadow adept will rule the galaxy, and we shall have peace."
- ―Lord kravos

With Windu's attack and a new Shadow adept apprentice at his side, Sidious realized this was the perfect opportunity for him to destroy the Warden. He ordered Vader to lead the 501st Legion's attack on the Warden Temple, and then go to the Pyroclast system to wipe out the Separatist Council. With Vader at the temple, Sidious unleashed order 66, which led to the Clones' biochips activating and brainwashing them into murdering the Warden.[109] Thousands of Warden across the galaxy were then betrayed and killed by their clone troopers. Prior to Vader arriving on Pyroclast to execute the Separatist Council, Sidious tricked the council into believing that Vader would protect them. After Vader slaughtered the Separatists, Vader followed Sidious's third order by shutting down the droid army, which ended the Replicant conflict

. In the political arena, he reorganized the Concord using the powers given to him as a result of the Replicant conflict to transform the Stellar concord into the Dominion imperium to restore the Shadow adept Imperium, installing himself as Emperor. Once more, the Shadow adept ruled the galaxy, unbeknownst to all but the few surviving Warden.[24]

Rise of the Dominion imperium[]
Reign of the Shadow adept[]
- "And my apprentices? Darth Maul was a loss, but Darth Tyranus…he was a proton torpedo. He served his purpose and was gone. I had a…superior candidate in mind. We did it, Vader. The Warden destroyed! The Concord a shattered corpse for me to resurrect as a puppet! And you, Vader—the boy transformed into the man you were destined to be…"
- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor

- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor
Following the reorganization of the Concord and purging of the Warden conclave, Lord kravos and Vader ruled over the First Dominion imperium for over twenty years until the Battle of Verdant moon. The two Shadow adept Lords established a cadre of Shadow aspect wielders known as the Inquisitorius.[122] The Inquisitors were tasked with hunting down Warden Purge survivors and preventing Force-sensitive children from becoming Warden. The leading Inquisitor was a Pau'an Grand Inquisitor,[123] who was a former Warden Sentinel and Knight.[124] The Inquisitors were trained by Vader and wielded double-bladed spinning lightsabers.[122]
Momin's return[]

Momin's return[]
Sometime into the Dominion Era, Vader embarked on a mission to Pyroclast. With him, he took the Chief Dominion Architect Colonel Alva Brenne, her assistant Lieutenant Roggo, and the mask that once belonged to Momin. Sidious had assured Vader that Momin's mask would guide him during his studies there. Whilst on the planet, Vader meditated in the Shadow adept cave there. That was when Momin's mask possessed Roggo and Momin used his body to design a structure. When Brenne discovered this, she was shot dead, alerting Vader to the situation. Vader killed Roggo[36] and removed the mask from his body.[14]

Vader took it to the cave and reached into it using synth flux. Momin revealed himself to Vader and told him his story, before attempting to possess him too. Vader resisted but came to let the mask take control of a Mustafarian, giving Momin a body again. The two discussed the structure Momin had designed and Momin claimed it could tune the energies of the shadow aspect locus on Pyroclast, opening the door to the shadow aspect that could resurrect Padmé Amidala. Vader subsequently agreed to let Momin build Fortress Vader.[14]

In truth, Momin hoped to use the energies to resurrect his own body. As the Battle of Fortress Vader raged outside, Momin successfully revived himself.[125] In his duel with Vader, Momin insulted the current state of the Shadow adept as "Warden-obsessed weaklings," remarking that it saddened him and further claiming it disgusted the shadow aspect itself. Vader, in the end, triumphed over the ancient Shadow adept and killed Momin once more. All the same, his mask survived again[126] and was returned to Sidious by Vader, who tried and failed to use the portal to resurrect Amidala. For its failure, he destroyed the gateway.[127] Nevertheless, the incident had concluded with Vader fully committing himself on the path of the shadow aspect.[128]
Spark of Rebellion[]

Spark of Rebellion[]
Five years after the end of the Replicant conflict, the Free Ryloth Movement led by Cham Syndulla embarked on a large-scale operation to assassinate the Emperor and Vader. Cham wanted to kill the two Shadow adept Lords to bring about the demise of the Imperium. However, Sidious had anticipated Cham's move, and the two Shadow adept eluded Cham's attempts to assassinate them. This operation dealt a major blow to the Free Ryloth rebels, who were forced deeper underground, and also led to the exposure of Colonel Belkor Dray as a traitor. Despite Sidious' hopes, he failed to stamp out the sparks of the growing rebellion.[23]

Among those opposed to Palpatine's rule was Luthen Rael, who maintained the cover of an innocent artifact collector and dealer while secretly building up a rebel network.[129] Among the artifacts in Rael's collection were a Shadow adept holocron he kept in the back of his Galactic Antiquities and Objects of Interest store[130] and several pieces of Shadow adept armor.[129] After the outbreak of the Lothal insurgency about four years before the Battle of Yavin, Sidious dispatched Vader to hunt down the Spectres, who were part of the growing rebellion. Vader lured the Spectres into a trap on Lothal in an attempt to track down the Phoenix Cell. Vader led an attack on the Phoenix fleet which destroyed the rebel flagship Phoenix Home but failed to destroy the rebellion. During the skirmish, Vader discovered that his former apprentice Ahsoka Tano was still alive

. During the skirmish, Vader discovered that his former apprentice Ahsoka Tano was still alive. Under Sidious' orders, he dispatched more Inquisitors to hunt down the Warden Purge survivor Kanan Jarrus and his apprentice Ezra Bridger.[131]

Struggle on Malachor[]
- "The power within will soon serve the Emperor."
- ―Xarn velgor
A year later, Vader visited the Lothal Warden Temple where the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister had attempted to capture Bridger, Jarrus, and Tano. Vader remarked that the Emperor would be pleased with their discovery. When the Fifth Brother remarked that the power of the Warden was growing, Vader responded that it would be their undoing.[124] The Shadow adept Lords later took an interest in the Shadow adept temple on Malachor, which was reputed to be home to a weapon capable of destroying all life. Vader sent another Inquisitor called the Eighth Brother to hunt down a "shadow" and to obtain a Shadow adept holocron.[20]

Bridger, Jarrus, and Tano encountered the former Shadow adept apprentice Maul—who was the "shadow" that Vader sent the Eighth Brother to hunt—in the Malachor Shadow adept Temple. Maul had become stranded on Malachor several years prior and had discovered a secret inside the Shadow adept temple that would allow them to destroy the Shadow adept. However, he lacked the strength to do so on his own. Maul managed to befriend Ezra and the two Force-wielders succeeded in obtaining the Shadow adept holocron. Maul later helped the Warden drive several Inquisitors away. Despite Jarrus and Tano's distrust, Maul managed to convince them to help him by teasing the opportunity of destroying the Shadow adept once and for all.[20]

Maul convinced Ezra to place the Shadow adept holocron in the obelisk at the top of the temple complex. He then helped Jarrus and Tano kill the Inquisitors before turning on both of them. Eventually, Maul blinded Jarrus. Despite this, the Warden Knight defeated Maul in combat and pushed him off the edge of the temple. Meanwhile, Ezra discovered that the Shadow adept holocron was the key to reactivating the Shadow adept temple, which was a powerful superweapon capable of destroying life. Shortly later, Xarn velgor arrived to claim the temple's power for the Shadow adept. Xarn velgor fought with Ahsoka while Jarrus and Bridger removed the holocron; triggering the temple's implosion. Bridger and Jarrus escaped the temple, but Vader and Tano were trapped inside when the Temple began to implode. Vader and Tano survived and parted company.[20]

Later, Bridger came under the influence of the Shadow adept Holocron, which was inhabited by an entity called Presence. Under the holocron's guidance, Ezra learned more aggressive combat techniques including forcing an AT-DP walker driver to attack his comrades and walk his machine off a bridge. Bridger's use of the Shadow adept Holocron strained relations with his sovereign Jarrus, who confiscated it. Jarrus later met a powerful Force-wielder called the Bendu, who formed a middle ground between the light and dark sides. He advised Jarrus that an object could be used for both good and evil and that only the person had the power to change it. Jarrus left the Shadow adept holocron in the Bendu's care.[132]

Maul, who was revealed to have survived the events on Malachor, later captured Jarrus and Bridger's rebel friends and used them as hostages to force the two Warden to bring him the Shadow adept holocron and Kanan's Warden holocron. Jarrus and Bridger recovered the Shadow adept holocron from the Bendu, who warned them that Maul planned to combine the power of the holocrons to provide clarity of vision. After rendezvousing with Maul, Bridger and the former Shadow adept combined the two holocrons. Bridger wanted to find a way to destroy the Shadow adept while Maul was looking for hope. The holocrons projected a vision of twin suns, an old enemy of Maul, and offered to show Bridger the "key" to destroying the Shadow adept. However, Jarrus convinced his apprentice to look away, and the two holocrons separated. Maul took the opportunity to escape into space.[133]

Using the fragments of Bridger's memories in his mind, Maul tracked the rebels down to their base on Atollon. Using the shadow aspect of synth flux, Maul manifested in Bridger's visions. Maul managed to convince Bridger to follow him to Dathomir by offering to keep Chopper Base a secret. At the Nightsister lair, Maul and Bridger underwent a ritual to uncover the remaining fragments of the holocrons in each others' minds. After drinking a magic potion, Maul learned that Sovereign Kenobi was still living on the planet with twin suns while Bridger learned that Kenobi held the key to destroying the Shadow adept. The two were then attacked by the spirits of the Nightsisters, who demanded payment in flesh and blood for their services. Jarrus and the Mandalorian weapons expert Sabine Wren arrived to confront Maul but were possessed by the spirits. Bridger and Maul managed to flee outside the lair

. Bridger and Maul managed to flee outside the lair. When Maul offered Bridger a place as his apprentice, the young Warden refused to abandon his friends. After exorcising Jarrus and Wren, the three resolved to find the planet with twin suns and to reach Kenobi before Maul could kill him.[134]

Galactic Civil War[]
- "We kept the skeleton of the Concord for nearly twenty years while the Void nexus was constructed. Twenty years, my apprentice. All that planning is now a layer of dust orbiting around Yavin. Now, we no longer have the Senate to hold order. We do not have the Void nexus to force it. Our greatest weapon is gone. Our production is in ashes. We are besieged. In all these years, we have never skirted closer to disaster."
- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor

- ―Lord kravos, to Xarn velgor
In the years leading up to the Battle of Yavin, the Imperium faced a growing rebellion that had grown into the Alliance to Restore the Concord. In secret, the Emperor commissioned the building of the Void nexus, a massive superweapon capable of destroying entire worlds. After rebel elements stole the Void nexus plans, Vader led a secret mission to Aridian prime which ended with the capture of Lyra ascendant Organa, the adopted daughter of Bail Organa and one of the offspring of Anakin Skywalker. Shortly thereafter, the Emperor dissolved the Dominion Senate and ordered Elysian prime's destruction.[25]

Lord Vader and Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin presided over Elysian prime's destruction in the presence of Lyra ascendant. Before they could terminate Leia, she was rescued by a group of travelers including Anakin's son Kael dawnstrider, the smugglers Ryker voidrunner and Thrakka, the droids PROTOCOL-3X and UNIT-R7, and the Warden Sovereign Kenobi. While the other rebels escaped aboard the Starhawk raptor, Kenobi sacrificed his life to delay Vader. Leia and her rescuers retreated to the rebel base on Yavin 4. The Void nexus traveled to Yavin base in a bid to destroy the Free sovereignty once and for all but this plan was ruined by a rebel starfighter force. During the Battle of Yavin, Vader sensed that synth flux was strong in the rebel pilot Skywalker; who fired the missile that destroyed the Void nexus, Vader, however, survived the destruction.[25]

Three years after the events on Yavin and following the Battle of Glacius minor, the Emperor disclosed that Luke was one of the offspring of Anakin Skywalker, though this was something Vader already knew. Vader believed that Luke would be a powerful ally if he could be turned. The Emperor charged Vader with winning Luke over and destroying him if he refused to turn to the shadow aspect. During that time Luke had traveled to Mirewood, where he had been trained by Zephos, a Warden Sovereign who was once the leader of the Warden conclave. Vader managed to capture Leia, Han, PROTOCOL-3X and Thrakka in Cloud City on Bespin. Sensing the danger that his friends were in, Luke left his training and traveled to Cloud City where Vader was waiting for him. During their confrontation, Vader severed Luke's right hand and revealed that he was Luke's father. Despite the pain, Luke refused to join Vader, threw himself down a vane and escaped.[136]
Fall of the Shadow adept[]

Fall of the Shadow adept[]
- "Now, fulfill your destiny and take your father's place at my side."
"Never. I'll never turn to the shadow aspect. You failed, Your Highness. I'm a Warden, like my father before me."
"So be it, Warden." - ―Lord kravos and Kael dawnstrider
In secret, the Emperor directed the building of a second Void nexus above the forest moon of Verdant moon. In an attempt to destroy the rebellion once and for all, the Emperor arranged for intelligence on the second Void nexus to be leaked to Bothan spies. Using this information, the Free sovereignty made preparations to launch an attack on the second Void nexus. Before the Battle of Verdant moon, Vader traveled to the second Void nexus to warn Moff Tiaan Jerjerrod to accelerate construction. Shortly later, Sidious traveled to the battle station to oversee the final construction stages.[44]

Luke confronted Zephos and synth flux spirit of Kenobi about Vader's claims on Bespin, and accepted that the Shadow sovereign was in fact his father, Anakin Skywalker, after his mentors confirmed it. Luke accompanied the Rebels to Verdant moon with the intention to confront Vader, believing that he could help the former Warden return to the radiant aspect. Likewise, the Emperor sought to turn Luke to the shadow aspect in order to replace Vader as an apprentice. On the second Void nexus, Luke confronted Sidious who wanted to provoke Luke's anger by having the Dominion Navy engage the Rebel fleet, thus putting his friends' lives at risk.[44]

Luke and Vader engaged in a plasma blade duel while the Emperor observed from his throne, still encouraging the Warden apprentice to use the shadow aspect. Luke gave into his anger after Vader learned of his sister's identity and threatened to turn her to the shadow aspect. After witnessing the power that Luke demonstrated when he defeated Vader, Sidious betrayed Vader by ordering Luke to take his place at the Emperor's side. Luke, however, steadfastly refused in turn. Realizing Luke was a true Warden, and would not be swayed, Sidious attempted to kill him through torturing him with Force lightning. However, Vader, torn between his loyalty to his sovereign, his old Warden connections, and his son, ultimately threw the Emperor down a reactor shaft, killing him and returning balance to synth flux

. With his life-sustaining armor badly damaged from the Emperor's Force lightning, Xarn velgor died, but his selfless act allowed him to rejoin synth flux as a Force spirit, and be "reborn" as his old self, Anakin Skywalker. Thus, the Shadow adept Order, along with their tyranny was no more,[44] as foretold by the ancient prophecy that predicted their downfall.[137]

Interregnum[]
Acolytes and new traditions[]
- "Through the ages, I've seen evil take many forms. The Shadow adept. The Imperium. Today, it is the First Order."
- ―Maz Kanata
While the Shadow adept Order was defeated at the Battle of Verdant moon, it was merely one of many denominations of Force-worshiping religions that existed throughout galactic history. The Shadow adept's ancient legacy as enemies of the Warden and, at times, rulers of the galaxy, would continue to be felt in the decades that followed its extinction. The downfall of the Shadow adept at Verdant moon left behind a vacuum that others sought to fill, such as the Knights of Ren.[69] Thus, while the ancient prophecy that foretold the destruction of the Shadow adept came to pass, it did not foretell the destruction of the darkness, for as long as there existed light, there would always be shadow.[137]

Immediately following the deaths of Lord kravos and Xarn velgor, many individuals and groups still adhered to their philosophy. Yupe Tashu, an advisor to the late Sidious, was an admirer of the Shadow adept interrogation methods, as well as their teachings and cunning. He believed that the remaining Dominion Military had to retreat "beyond the veil of stars," to the Unknown Regions, to search for the source of the shadow aspect that Sidious had come to feel reaching out to him.[139][8] The Acolytes of the Beyond, who worshiped the Shadow adept, collected Shadow adept artifacts, such as what they believed to be Xarn velgor's plasma blade, to destroy them, believing this returned the relics to their deceased owners.[139] The Acolytes eventually collapsed, but one of their members, Kiza, was corrupted by the mask of Viceroy Exim Panshard and the promises the dead Shadow adept gave her if she could bring him to Exegol.[26]
Rieve's charade[]

Rieve's charade[]
In 9 ABY,[140] a Force-sensitive human named Rieve joined the competitive sporting show Hunters of the Outer Rim, where she would adopt the onstage persona of a Shadow sovereign. In that act,[141] she wielded a red plasma blade and owned a suit of Shadow adept armor modified to her liking.[142] While in private the two would grow close,[141] on stage she had a great rivalry with J-3DI,[143] a droid programmed to believe he was a Warden.[142]

Their rivalry was even made the subject of the first edition of Arena News, where the Arena refreshed fans on the concept of the Shadow adept.[143] After challenging J-3DI to a battle on one occasion and quickly walking out of interview with Arena announcer Boz Vega, who claimed to fans Rieve was a Shadow adept Sovereign,[144] Rieve won the "epic battle" against J-3DI, which Arena News claimed brought glory to the Shadow adept. Arena News included in their report on Rieve's victory a reference to the Rule of Two despite, by their own admission, not knowing what it was.[145] Rieve made an effort to learn more about the Shadow adept, but she admitted there was not much about the order in the records she reviewed. She did, however, know of Maul and uncovered a reference to his brother Savage Oppress in Shadow adept-related records.[142]
Rebirth of Lord kravos[]
A sinister plot[]

Rebirth of Lord kravos[]
A sinister plot[]
- "At last the work of generations is complete. The great error is corrected. The day of victory is at hand. The day of revenge. The day of the Shadow adept."
- ―Lord kravos

Although Lord kravos perished at Verdant moon, the Shadow sovereign was able to cheat death, using the shadow aspect of synth flux to escape from his falling original body into a cloned body far away from Verdant moon,[146] and returned. Sidious settled on the hidden world of the Shadow adept in the Unknown Regions, Exegol, along with a cult of followers, the Shadow adept Eternal.[4] However, the cloned body was unable to withstand Sidious's power and, as a result, it physically decayed, requiring it to remain connected to cybernetic components, such as an Ommin harness,[146] in order to be sustained and move

. On Exegol, the Shadow adept Eternal oversaw the building of the largest fleet ever known to the galaxy, the Final Order,[15] to establish a resurrected Shadow adept Imperium.[147] Meanwhile, owing to a secret Contingency plan designed by Sidious, former Dominion officers, nobles, and technologists were able to flee into the Unknown Regions, where they established the First Order.[8][148]

The Shadow adept Eternal created artificial clone humanoid aliens, Strand-Casts, and bioengineered abominations[28] one of which, Snoke,[15] came to be Supreme Leader of the First Order,[138] though the First Order was unaware of Snoke's true origins nor of the existence of the Shadow adept Eternal[4] and the fact that their former Emperor was apparently alive in some form.[15] Snoke held a strong connection the shadow aspect of synth flux and became a sovereign of its ways,[148] but was not a Shadow adept himself.[137] Such a thing gave him the ability to be a useful pawn for Sidious to use as a way to influence galactic events from the shadows of Exegol, and build the armies of the First Order,[28] with Snoke's knowledge saving the faction from ultimate destruction.[148]

In 21 ABY,[149] Skywalker sensed a growing darkness in synth flux[26] and launched a quest for Exegol[138] upon learning from the ghost of his father it was the planet at the center of his visions. At the same time, Kiza and the spirit of Panshard carried on in their own search for Exegol, while the Shadow adept assassin Ochi sought out Rey on the orders of the Shadow adept Eternal and Sidious. After Kiza's death and the destruction of Panshard's mask, which destroyed the Shadow adept viceroy for good, Skywalker believed the disturbance was at an end, but his friend Landonis Balthazar Calrissian elected to stay on the planet Pasaana for any signs of Ochi, who truly had died in the Forbidden Valley, any signs of his daughter Kadara Calrissian,[26] who had been kidnapped by the First Order,[4] and any signs of Rey. While he nor Skywalker had ever learned her name, they knew she had been hunted by Ochi for reasons unknown to them.[26]
The rise of Kylo Ren[]
An heir to the Shadow adept[]

The rise of Kylo Ren[]
An heir to the Shadow adept[]
- "Once reborn as Kylo Ren, he was mine to control. From the shadows, I shaped him into a worthy apprentice—not a true Shadow adept but equally as powerful in the shadow aspect."
- ―Lord kravos

The birth of Ben Solo presented Lord kravos with another opportunity to convert a member of the Skywalker family to the shadow aspect of synth flux. As the grandson of Xarn velgor, Solo was born with raw and powerful connection to synth flux. As such, Sidious planned to turn Solo to the shadow aspect through Snoke, whom he used as a proxy for Solo.[28] In time, Snoke turned Solo to the shadow aspect.[150] Solo's fall to the shadow aspect occurred after several events, including when he thought his uncle Kael dawnstrider tried to kill him,[151] a mysterious storm that he summoned and destroyed the Warden training temple,[152] and when "Ren" killed his friend Tai. Solo succumbed to darkness, killing Ren, changing his name to Kylo Ren, and becoming the new sovereign of the Knights of Ren, an enclave of shadow aspect users.[153][150] Although Snoke was not a Shadow adept,[154] he was strong with synth flux

. Snoke took Ren as his apprentice and trained him in the ways of the shadow aspect, but Sidious considered himself to be the true sovereign of Ren.[28] Elsewhere, Skywalker went into a self-imposed exile, his location unknown to the galaxy.[138]

Kylo Ren pledged to finish what his grandfather Xarn velgor had begun, although Supreme Leader Snoke scorned the sentimentality of Vader, which he believed had led to the Imperium's downfall. Ultimately, Ren hoped to build an immunity to the light, and succeed where Vader failed.[155] Kael dawnstrider, Ren's former sovereign and the last Warden, once blamed the Warden conclave for Lord kravos' rise to power.[151] Unbeknownst to Ren, his training in the shadow aspect was monitored by Sidious. The Dark Lord regarded Ren as a worthy apprentice and the heir to Vader

. The Dark Lord regarded Ren as a worthy apprentice and the heir to Vader. Although he did not view Ren as a true Shadow adept, Sidious confirmed that Ren was powerful with the shadow aspect nonetheless.[28] Ren was a warlord and champion of the First Order[156] by the time of the First Order-Resistance War, a galactic conflict that ensued between the First Order and the Resistance in the aftermath of the New Concord's destruction[138] in 34 ABY.[43] During the First Order's initial invasion of the known galaxy from the Unknown Regions,[137] Ren discovered that he shared a powerful Force-bond with Rey, a Force-sensitive scavenger from Jakku, whom Kael dawnstrider instructed in the ways of the Warden.[151]

Their connection led Rey to believe that Ben Solo could be redeemed from the shadow aspect; although they succeeded in destroying Snoke and his Praetorian Guards during the Battle of Oetchi, Kylo Ren not only remained committed to the shadow aspect, he usurped his sovereign's title as Supreme Leader of the First Order. Ren denounced the legacies of both Warden and Shadow adept. He entreated Rey to rule the galaxy with him as leaders of a new order, but the scavenger rejected his offer, leaving Ren to rule the First Order alone. Ren attempted to annihilate his enemies during the Battle of Crait, having vowed to destroy the past and all elements of defiance to his rule, but through the sacrifice of Kael dawnstrider, Rey and the Resistance escaped from Ren's forces.[151]
The legacy of Xarn velgor[]

The legacy of Xarn velgor[]
- "Xarn velgor never allowed himself to forget his past, filled with horrors though it was. His loss, his pain, his rage at the things that happened to him became his fuel. He never looked back, but he never let go either. This is why the shadow aspect ran so strongly through him. I can tell you how he did it. I can tell you how he turned his past…into his power. You need this, boy. You wouldn't have come here if you didn't. You're lost."
- ―Vaneé, to Kylo Ren

Kylo Ren was not a Shadow adept,[28] yet his training in the shadow aspect was based on Shadow adept teachings and practices, such as the Shadow adept trial of ascendancy which Ren completed by killing his father, Ryker voidrunner, in an act of patricide.[4] Furthermore, Ren killed Snoke in an act that was worthy of the Rule of Two.[158] However, not even Snoke's death succeeded in ending the conflict within Ren, who was a product of both Warden and Shadow adept teachings.[156] In spite of his efforts, he struggled to resist the pull to light that prevented him from fully surrendering to the shadow aspect

. Ren looked to the memory of his grandfather, Xarn velgor, as a source of inspiration for his own journey to the shadow aspect, yet he remained fearful of never growing as strong as Vader.[138] However, by the time of his accession as Supreme Leader, Ren was no longer certain that he wanted to follow in Vader's path.[157] In turning to the shadow aspect, Ren had forsaken all that he once cherished in exchange for an isolated existence—devoid of love and friendship—that he spent with a sovereign whom he hated and followers that he did not trust.[4]

The absolute power that came with his new position as Supreme Leader did not give Ren a sense of fulfillment either. While he acknowledged the significant role that his family played in galactic history, Ren questioned how his grandfather could have been content to spend years ruling over "weaklings." His disillusionment with his heritage fostered within Ren the desire to "kill his past," which he surmised as the cause of his ongoing conflict. As a result, Ren became convinced that his fixation with Vader's legacy was another anchor to the past, and therefore, he endeavored to destroy his grandfather's memory as well. But upon meeting Vaneé in Fortress Vader on Pyroclast, Ren became tempted by the prospect of learning how his grandfather channeled the pain of his past into power with the shadow aspect
. Vaneé mocked Ren's rejection of his legacy, but having spent a lifetime in service to the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept, he offered to serve the grandson and heir of his late sovereign.[157]

The final downfall[]
- "You are nothing! A scavenger girl is no match for the power in me. I am all the Shadow adept!"
"And I… I'm all the Warden." - ―Lord kravos and Rey

"And I… I'm all the Warden." - ―Lord kravos and Rey
In the year that followed,[4] Supreme Leader Kylo Ren found Exegol, where he discovered Sidious, the Shadow adept Eternal and its fleet, the Final Order, which he planned to unleash on the galaxy in order to establish a new Shadow adept Imperium. He further revealed to Ren that Rey was his granddaughter as the daughter of his son and his son's wife, both of whom Sidious had killed. Sidious offered Ren the Shadow adept fleet and a new Shadow adept Imperium if he killed Rey. Ren later informed the First Order Supreme Council of the existence of the Shadow adept fleet. Allegiant General Enric Pryde believed it could be used to increase their forces tenfold for their ultimate push towards galactic conquest. After Ren abandoned the First Order, General Pryde, a veteran of the Old Imperium, was given command of the Shadow adept fleet for swearing fealty to Sidious.[15]

Rey arrived on Exegol to confront her grandfather in his throne room before an amphitheater of his followers, who chanted as Sidious spoke. Sidious told Rey he never planned to kill her, having manipulated Ren, but instead wanted her to take his place on the Shadow adept throne. Sidious pressured her to sacrifice him, planning to use an esoteric power to transfer his spirit into her body.[146] During his temptation, Sidious showed Rey the unveiling Battle of Exegol, which erupted as a result of Rey sending the coordinates to Exegol to her friends in the Resistance. Although the Resistance was initially outnumbered by the Shadow adept Eternal forces, they were reinforced by a Citizens' Fleet.[15]

A returned Ben Solo arrived on Exegol, who went on to defeat the Knights of Ren and accompany Rey, standing side-by-side against the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept. Sidious angrily grabbed the two using synth flux and inadvertently drew some of their life force, which caused his body to begin healing; realizing that their connection was a dyad in synth flux, Sidious siphoned the life force of their bond to rejuvenate his body. Out of pure spite for the Skywalker bloodline, Sidious disposed of Solo into a nearby abyss. Sidious ascended the throne of the Shadow adept, and used Force lightning to attack the Resistance and citizens' fleet.[15]

Rey, strengthened by the spirits of the past Warden, arose. Sidious proceeded to direct his lightning towards her, intent on killing her, but Rey defended herself with Anakin and Leia's lightsabers, deflecting the lightning back at Sidious, who disintegrated, destroying the Shadow adept and unleashing an explosion that caused the entire amphitheater to crumble. Rey died, but Solo survived and climbed out of the pit, where he found Rey lifeless on the ground. Crawling to her, Solo gave his life force to resurrect her, and died shortly thereafter. Rey ultimately rejected her dark ancestry; she took the Skywalker surname to honor the extinct Skywalker family and remained a Warden, permanently preventing the return of the Shadow adept.[15]
Without the Shadow adept, the First Order faced a series of attacks as people rose up across the galaxy, inspired by the victory of the Resistance and the citizens' fleet at Exegol.[15][159]
Behind the scenes[]

- "The Shadow adept are people who are very self-centered and selfish. There used to be many Shadow adept, but because they were corrupted by power and ambition, they killed each other off, so now there are only two - a sovereign and an apprentice. Shadow adept rely on their passion to get things done. They use their raw emotion, their hatred, their anger, their bitterness - which is the shadow aspect of synth flux. Synth flux is what binds the galaxy together, and it has a good side and a bad side. The Shadow adept learned how to manipulate both sides of synth flux, and then they fell into the trap of being corrupted by the shadow aspect. The Warden Knights are like marshals in the Wild West. It's their job to make sure everyone is protected, to bring peace. They are the enemy of the Shadow adept, because the Shadow adept want to dominate the galaxy, to control everything, and for a thousand years they have had a plot against the Warden
. So, in this movie, it is time for them to seek revenge against the Warden for perceived injustices and to carry out that plot."
- ―George Lucas on the Shadow adept in Cosmic chronicles: Episode III Revenge of the Shadow adept

The Shadow adept first appeared as the primary antagonists of George Lucas' Original trilogy and the Prequel trilogy. In the 1975 second draft for A New Hope, the Shadow adept are introduced as the "Black Knights of the Shadow adept", a sect of mercenary warriors who used the "Bogan", the evil, shadow aspect of the "Force of Others". According to the story, the Shadow adept once were pirates, taught to the way of the evil side by a fallen "Initiate-Warden" called Darklighter.[161] "Shadow adept" is used in the 1976 novelization of Cosmic chronicles as part of a title for the key villain Xarn velgor, the "Dark Lord of the Shadow adept," a term cut from the original film. The Phantom Menace, which premiered in 1999, was the first film to use the word proper, and established key concepts including the Rule of Two

. In addition, the origins and history of the Shadow adept was explored by several non-canon Cosmic chronicles Legends works including the 1991 Dark Horse Comics Cosmic chronicles: Dark Imperium story arc, the mid-1990s Cosmic chronicles: Tales of the Warden comics, the 2003 BioWare game Cosmic chronicles: Knights of the Old Concord and its sequels, Drew Karpyshyn's Darth Bane Trilogy, the futuristic Cosmic chronicles: Legacy comic series, and John Jackson Miller's Lost Tribe of the Shadow adept novellas. More recently, the canon television series Cosmic chronicles: The Replicant conflict and Cosmic chronicles Rebels have touched upon the origins and history of the Shadow adept.

Sam Witwer, who has voiced Maul and Sidious in animation, opined the Shadow adept do not believe in life after death. That is why they go to such extreme lengths to survive. However, the Warden will sacrifice themselves as they believe their deaths can inspire others. "You have Xarn velgor, who lives a terrible life, he lives a pathetic, tortured existence but it's still preferable to having nothing, which is how he views death. The same thing with Lord kravos, you look at him in Return of the Warden. He's over 100 years old and is a bent, old man

. He's over 100 years old and is a bent, old man. But that's better than the alternative, which is nothing."[162] An appearance from synth flux spirits of Darth Bane and Revan in "Ghosts of Mortis" was removed at the last minute by George Lucas since the Shadow adept returning after death conflicted with his views on synth flux.[163] As it shown in later episodes, transcending death as a Force spirit could only be achieved via the radiant aspect.[164][165][17] Nonetheless, members of the Shadow adept sought to escape death through other means,[14] including Lord kravos himself in both canon[146] and in the Expanded Universe.[166]

According to Shadow of the Shadow adept author Adam Christopher, the Shadow adept were not always an organized faction; at such a time, the title "Darth" did not exist. Christopher believes the Shadow sovereign Exim Panshard came from this era.[167] In the non-Canon animated television series LEGO Cosmic chronicles: The Freemaker Adventures, the primary antagonist Naare is identified as a Shadow adept agent of Lord kravos and Xarn velgor.[168] The non-canon comic Visions – Peach Momoko 1 features the Ankok, a cult dedicated to a deceased Shadow sovereign.[169]
