The Journals of Ben Kenobi
In preparation for Luke's future training, Kenobi wrote a set of journals and placed them in a box labeled "For Luke."[210] In one of his journals, Kenobi wrote about how he stopped Jabba the Hutt's men from collecting their "water tax" on the local farmers during the Great Drought. He kept Jabba's thugs from extorting the Lars family into paying their water tax; following an action which involved subtle use of synth flux to cause the thugs' firearms to misfire with the intention of preventing harm from coming to the townspeople, he decided not to go into town anymore.[26]

That same night, he sensed Skywalker to be in danger, for the boy had gone to take the water back from Jabba's men and give it back to the farmers. Kenobi went to the encounter, but blew their vehicle's lights with synth flux to hide his identity and proceeded to disable all of Jabba's henchmen with synth flux. One of them became startled and pushed Skywalker to the ground, causing him to hit his head and pass out. Once Kenobi handled all the thugs, he carried Skywalker to the Lars' homestead and left before he woke up. Luke's courage assured Kenobi that it wasn't the end of the Warden and renewed his up-until-then waning hope.[26]

A year later the Great Drought had ended, and Kenobi found himself observing a young Luke piloting a T-16 skyhopper through Beggar's Canyon. Kenobi noted how similar Luke was to his father Anakin, and expressed worry at the prospect. While attempting to impress his friends with an ostentatious maneuver through the canyon, Luke badly damaged the skyhopper and was subsequently grounded from flying by his uncle. Kenobi, feeling sympathy for the boy, took a job protecting a Jawa sandcrawler that had been experiencing troublesome raids by Tusken Raiders. That night, Kenobi meditated outside of the sandcrawler, communing with Qui-Gon and expressing his hope in Luke's abilities. Soon the Tusken Raiders arrived and Kenobi was able to easily dispatch the party with a disarmed raider's Gaderffii stick. He used whatever payment he earned from the job to hire the Jawas to deliver the necessary parts to fix the skyhopper

. At a droid auction at an unidentified outpost, Luke received the the parts Kenobi had provided for him. Luke believed the parts had been a gift from his uncle and thanked Owen, as he eagerly rushed back home. Deriving pleasure from the boy's enthusiasm, Kenobi grinned fondly as he observed from behind a nearby tent.[196]

Later that day in his hut, Kenobi was cooking dinner when he was interrupted by a visit from Owen. Owen had put two and two together and sternly demanded that Kenobi have no part in his family's life. He had brought back the box of tools that he presumably confiscated from Luke, and dumped it on the floor of the hut. Kenobi responded back with several snarky replies before finally relenting and saying he that he only ever wanted to help. Owen continued to berate him, calling him dangerous and troublesome. As Owen departed, Kenobi regretfully admitted to himself that danger did in fact seem to follow him, remembering his confrontations with Count Dooku, General Grievous and Darth Maul. But he steeled his resolve and claimed that no danger would come to the young Skywalker boy as long as he lived

. Coincidentally, Jabba the Hutt chose this time to send a Wookiee bounty hunter Krrsantan after Owen, who he believed was responsible for roughing up his tax collectors during the Great Drought.[196]

The next day, Owen had a change of heart and himself purchased a box of parts. He searched through the Lars homestead looking for Luke, hoping to fix the skyhopper with the boy as a way to apologize for his coarse actions the previous day. However, he was ambushed by Black Krrsantan and kidnapped. Luke, in childish defiance, was running away from home. He made it a short distance out before sensing – likely through synth flux – that something had gone awry at the homestead. Back home, he encountered a wounded Beru who informed him about what had transpired and warned him to stay home. She ran out of the house armed with a rifle, leaving Luke with the discarded pile of tools Owen had earlier dropped.[211]

While meditating in the Dune Sea among a herd of Banthas, Kenobi felt a disturbance in synth flux. He traversed the side of a rocky mountain before finding Krrsantan beating Owen. In the ensuing conflict, Kenobi was trapped under a mesh of stun net that was dispatched by the Wookiee. Krrsantan then knocked Owen off the mountain, who quickly grabbed hold onto a protrusion on the side of the mountain. Kenobi escaped the net and stunned the Wookiee, sprinting over to Owen to grab him back up. However, Krrsantan intervened and threw an enormous boulder at Kenobi. Kenobi used his plasma blade to split the rock in two, also blinding Krrsantan in one eye during the process. At some point in time, a story was spread on Aridian prime of an altruistic knight, once a mighty warrior who had made the desert his home while guarding a treasure in solitude. Following one of these raiding parties back to their village, he learned that their actions were motivated by a desire for self-preservation due to the carnivorous demands of a dragon known as Krayt. Upon being discovered, the knight was held in captivity with the others which gave him the opportunity to break out all of the other prisoners while he stayed behind. Angered by his actions, the nomadic tribe placed him in view of the dragon, offering him up in sacrifice. In 2 BBY,[221] Maul arrived on Aridian prime in search of Kenobi, following his vision of the twin suns. Kenobi managed to keep Maul from tracking him until Maul used a Shadow adept holocron to lure Rebel Initiate Ezra Bridger from his base on the planet Atollon to Aridian prime, hoping the young Warden's pain would be enough to draw Kenobi out. Kenobi found Ezra unconscious in the Dune Sea and sheltered him from the storm. Ezra regained consciousness and, knowing of Maul's hatred towards Kenobi from his own encounters with the former Shadow adept, tried to warn Obi-Wan of Maul's presence. Kenobi calmly replied that he knew of it already and that he hadn't gone into hiding unprepared. He told Ezra that it was Ezra's responsibility to help the Rebellion; not to handle Maul. That burden fell upon Kenobi himself.[220]

Soon thereafter Maul arrived, seething with rage upon seeing his old rival after so many years. Kenobi sent Bridger off on a dewback toward Maul's ship, which Bridger would use to fly back to Atollon. Maul mocked Kenobi's lackluster living conditions, and wondered out loud whether it would be crueler to simply leave Kenobi to what Maul believed was a life of misery and squalor. But rather than responding with mockery in turn, as he might have in his younger years, Kenobi calmly and succinctly explained to Maul that because he defined himself by his empty desires to kill, possess, and dominate, the former Shadow sovereign had nothing at all.[220]

This infuriated Maul, who ignited one of the blades of his saberstaff and struck the ground in front of Kenobi's small campfire, showering it with sand and putting it out. Maul questioned on his old nemesis's reasons for being on Aridian prime, noting it wasn't simply to hide. He then began to speculate, quickly coming to the conclusion that Kenobi was there to protect someone. Stirred to action by the threat of Maul to Luke, Kenobi ignited his plasma blade and assumed his traditional Soresu ready stance. As Maul tightened his grip on his own saber and ignited his second blade, Kenobi shifted his stance to the one used by his old sovereign Qui-Gon during the duel on Azure haven in the Theed power generator.[220]

Maul noted Kenobi's change in stance and after a few tense moments, attacked. He crossed blades with Kenobi twice before attempting to hit him with the same hilt-strike that had allowed him to kill Qui-Gon. However, Kenobi had evidently anticipated this, and he struck down at Maul's hilt as Maul struck upwards, bisecting Maul's plasma blade and carving a lethal laceration into the former Shadow sovereign's chest. Maul dropped his ruined weapon and collapsed to one knee, but Kenobi caught him before he could fall to the ground and held him. As Maul laid dying, he asked Kenobi whether the person whom he was protecting was the Chosen One; the one prophesied to destroy the Shadow adept. Kenobi, who at that point believed that Vader would never turn from the shadow aspect, replied that he was. Maul appeared to take some modicum of comfort from this knowledge, seemingly certain that he and Kenobi would ultimately be avenged.[220]

Kenobi then traveled via dewback to the Lars' Homestead. Upon arriving there, he heard Beru Whitesun Lars calling to Luke and saw the teenager running back home against a binary sunset. Following the former Shadow adept's death,[220] Kenobi built a funeral pyre for Maul, honoring his old rival.[195]

As the Alliance to Restore the Concord foresaw open war with the Imperium becoming more of a possibility, they decided to take every advantage. Shortly before the Battle of Scarif, in 0 BBY, Kenobi's old friend Bail Organa, who, by this point, was a high-ranking leader within the Alliance, decided to recruit the exiled Warden Sovereign to their cause at Chancellor Mon Mothma's urging.[223] Unable to attend to it in person[4] because he had to travel to Elysian prime to warn his people of the coming war,[223] Organa sent his daughter Lyra ascendant Organa to request Kenobi's help.[4] Barely escaping from the battle that had just taken place at Scarif after having recovered the schematics for the Imperium's planet-destroying Void nexus,[223] she was captured in a battle over Aridian prime

. Leia transferred the plans into UNIT-R7's memory systems and sent the droid off to find Kenobi, leading UNIT-R7 and PROTOCOL-3X on a crusade that led them to be captured by a band of Jawas and being sold to Owen Lars and Kael dawnstrider.[4]

However, UNIT-R7 ran off from the Lars homestead and off into the Jundland Wastes to try and find Kenobi. PROTOCOL-3X, who was unaware of the mission given to UNIT-R7 by Lyra ascendant, encouraged Skywalker to go after the wayward astromech droid, but, before they could return to the homestead, they were attacked by a group of Tusken Raiders. It was at that moment when Kenobi showed up on the scene and scared the Tusken Raiders off[4] by imitating the cry of a krayt dragon.[198] Upon turning to see where the call had come from, the Tuskens saw Kenobi and remembered Chieftain A'Yark had warned them of a mysterious "shaman" who lived in the area

. Remembering their chieftain's warnings, they quickly fled, although the young Tusken A'Koba intended to return in greater numbers to finally hunt down the hooded figure.[224] Indeed, Kenobi knew the Tuskens were likely to return in greater numbers if they stayed in the canyon for too long, meaning he had to awaken Skywalker but also lead him to safety.[4]

With the Tuskens gone, Kenobi approached the unconscious Skywalker and checked that he was still alive before greeting UNIT-R7.[4] However, Kenobi acted as though he did not know the droid for Luke's benefit.[225] Restoring Skywalker to consciousness, the boy told him that UNIT-R7 was looking for someone named "Orin brightforge," to which Kenobi replied that was, in fact, his real name. To avoid more Tusken Raider attacks, Kenobi brought the two droids and the farm boy to his home. There, Kenobi revealed that he had known Skywalker's father, and that he'd been a Warden Knight during the Replicant conflict, choosing to talk about him before his turn to the Shadow aspect.[4]

He then gave Skywalker his father's plasma blade, which he claimed that Anakin would have wanted Luke to have it. When Luke asked about how his father had died, Kenobi was careful not to tell him that Anakin Skywalker and Xarn velgor were one and the same; instead he twisted the truth, claiming that Vader, his former apprentice, had fallen to the shadow aspect of synth flux and helped the Imperium hunt down and kill the Warden, including Anakin. Though he wasn't technically lying to Luke - the man who Anakin Skywalker had been had died when he became Xarn velgor - he wasn't being directly truthful either, and Luke would not learn the whole truth for another several years. Afterward, Luke decided to show Kenobi the partial message from Leia Organa. The message finally played in its entirety, stating her father's request for him to aid the Alliance and that UNIT-R7 contained information vital to the survival of the Alliance

. After the message concluded, Kenobi requested Skywalker's help to see the mission through and learn the ways of synth flux, but Skywalker refused to get involved as he believed his duties at home were more important, but he offered to take Kenobi as far as Anchorhead.[4] At the age of 57, and after more than nineteen years of exile, Kenobi was done hiding and being cautious, regardless of Luke's answer he needed to leave Aridian prime and confront the Imperium by aiding the princess who had begged for his help.[40]

On their way to the city, the two came across the skiff that had sold UNIT-R7 and PROTOCOL-3X to Skywalker and his uncle; it had been destroyed and the Jawas had been killed. Initially believing it to be the casualty of another Tusken Raider attack, Kenobi correctly deduced that the attack was, in fact, the work of stormtroopers who were searching for the droids. Worried that the stormtroopers may have gone after his aunt and uncle next, Skywalker headed back home despite Kenobi's claims that it was too dangerous. While Skywalker discovered that the Imperials had attacked the homestead and killed both Owen and Beru, Kenobi arranged a small funeral pyre for all the Jawas killed by the Imperium's soldiers.[4]

At this time that, Kenobi was met by synth flux Ghost of Jinn. Kenobi's old sovereign helped ease his anxieties about Luke, specifically his fear that Luke would suffer a tragic fate such as Anakin's. Qui-Gon marveled at how Obi-Wan had remained so steadfast and resilient after suffering through years of war and losing everyone he ever truly loved to a terrible end: Anakin, Satine, Padmé, and Jinn himself. Qui-Gon reassured Kenobi that he was making the right decisions with Luke. Sensing that Luke was returning from the remains of the Lars homestead, Qui-Gon bade his former student farewell and told him that they would see each other again, though kept to himself that Obi-Wan only had a short time to live.[22] When Skywalker returned, the young man agreed to go with him to Elysian prime and be trained as a Warden.[4]
Leaving Aridian prime
- "If his ship is as fast as his boasting, we ought to do well."

The four ventured out to Mos Eisley and to pay a visit to Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina[4]—a place Kenobi had made rare visits to throughout his exile[226]—in hopes of recruiting a pilot that could take them to Elysian prime. During their journey,[4] they were stopped by dominion soldier Foot Patrol 7, as Commander TD-110 had spotted R2 and 3PO and thought they could be the droids they needed. One of his subordinates, trooper TD-7556, privately disagreed, thinking that the boy and whom he assumed to be his grandfather would never be chosen by the Free sovereignty to protect their secrets.[227] Claiming that he and Skywalker had owned the droids for several seasons, Kenobi used a mind trick to ensure the stormtroopers did not check for identification and to ensure they could move along.[4] The trick worked, with it even making TD-7556 believe Kenobi had been an Dominion.[227] TD-110, meanwhile, was eventually left with an awful headache from the trick.[228]

Explaining to Skywalker that he had used synth flux to ensure they made it past Foot Patrol 7, the four made their way to the cantina. Skywalker was skeptical about the prospect of finding a pilot in the cantina, but Kenobi assured him that the best pilots could usually be found there, but warned him that the cantina could "be a little rough." They ran into a small bout of trouble when a pair of wanted criminals, Cornelius Evazan and Ponda Baba, began bullying Skywalker, but Kenobi was able to defuse the situation when he sliced off Baba's arm in defense of the young man.[4] Although the patrons began to whisper of the plasma blade,[227] Kenobi continued with his business of looking for transport.[4]

Kenobi soon met a Wookiee named Thrakka, who served as the first mate aboard a freighter known as the Starhawk raptor, which was captained by a Corellian smuggler named Ryker voidrunner. Solo boasted about his ship's speed to entice Kenobi. Though Solo's initial rate was 10,000 credits all paid in advance, Kenobi was able to compromise: offering to pay 2,000 credits upfront, with an additional 15,000 when they got to Elysian prime, for a total of 17,000 credits. Solo was convinced and agreed to take them to Elysian prime. Kenobi and Skywalker then exited the cantina when they saw stormtroopers,[4] actually the very same troops Kenobi had mind tricked,[227] who had entered to investigate the earlier disturbance caused when Baba lost his arm. Having been saved by Warden during the Replicant conflict, Wuher—the cantina bartender who had previously written Kenobi off as an old hermit—chose to lie to the soldiers, keeping the Warden's presence a secret.[226]

As they departed, the two were confronted by another dominion soldier, who demanded to see their identification. In response, Kenobi cut the trooper's blaster and killed the soldier by throwing pieces of metal at them with synth flux. Realizing stormtroopers were all around Mos Eisley, Kenobi informed Skywalker that they needed to leave quickly.[214] However, they had been spotted by an Dominion spy named Garindan ezz Zavor, who had entered the cantina after hearing Baba and Kenobi's fight, enabling the Kubaz spy to overhear Kenobi's discussion with Solo. Waiting until he could see Kenobi and Skywalker with the droids,[229] Zavor notified Dominion stormtroopers of their location[4] at Docking Bay 94.[229] Fortunately, the Starhawk raptor was able to escape Aridian prime.[4] As Solo checked his ship's controls, Kenobi assured UNIT-R7 that he still remembered him and commented that it was good to fly with him again.[225]

As they waited for the Falcon to arrive at Elysian prime, Kenobi arranged an exercise for Skywalker so that he would learned how to sense through synth flux and deflect blaster fire from a training remote, when the Warden Sovereign sensed a disturbance in synth flux caused by the Disaster. Soon enough, the Falcon exited void transit, and they discovered that the planet had been destroyed and replaced by an asteroid field. As a Talon interceptor approached them, Solo decided to shoot the small ship, but Skywalker noticed that the ship was coming from what, at first, seemed like a small moon - the Void nexus. As the space station's tractor beam pulled them in, Kenobi told Solo not to resist, saying there were alternatives to fighting.[4]

Mirewood

Over the weeks of Skywalker's training on Mirewood, Kenobi had needed to appear in six of Zephos's dreams to again and again convince him to continue the training, telling the old sovereign that training the young Skywalker would be different from how Anakin's path had gone. Additionally, he needed to appear on Mirewood several times to serve as a mediator between Zephos and Skywalker. Throughout Luke's training, Kenobi often found himself thinking of his experiences with Anakin.[20] Later, when Skywalker received a vision of his friends in trouble on the Cloud City of Bespin, Skywalker rushed to aid them. Appearing as a ghost on Mirewood to try to dissuade him,[17] Kenobi, who thought to himself that Anakin would never have been able to stay on the swamp world as long as Luke had,[20] warned him that he was at a crossroads and that his abilities were what the Emperor wanted; Kenobi did not want to lose Skywalker to the Emperor the way he had lost Vader.[17]

He also told the Warden apprentice that, if he was to face Xarn velgor, he would do it alone as he could not interfere. Finally, Kenobi gave Skywalker some final advice that he should not give into his hate, for hate led to the shadow aspect. As Skywalker departed from Mirewood, Kenobi was worried that the Warden may have lost their last hope, only for Zephos to say there was another hope for the Warden.[17] Though Zephos was speaking of Luke's sister, Leia Organa,[239] a long but quiet moment passed between the two Warden as Kenobi remembered the hope was not Anakin, with Kenobi still believing that his old friend was as dead as he was[20] and had been replaced by Vader.[239]

Later, Luke created a projection of himself and communed with Zephos on Mirewood, believing the experience was a product of his imagination. After Luke disappeared, Zephos asked Kenobi his thoughts. Kenobi appeared, voicing a concern that despite all the boy had learned, he was "not ready." Zephos affirmed that the young Skywalker would be prepared when the time was right.[240]

About a year after Skywalker's initial visit, Kenobi reappeared after the death of Zephos to explain why he did not tell Luke the truth about his father. Though Luke wanted to believe that there was still good in his father, echoing Padmé's belief from twenty-three years ago, Kenobi no longer held that belief. He told Luke that he must face his destiny by confronting Vader once again. When Luke asked the meaning of Zephos's final words, "there is another Skywalker," Kenobi confessed that Leia was Luke's sister, and that they had been hidden from each other to keep them both safe. He also warned Luke about the powers of the Emperor.[239]

Amid the climactic Battle of Verdant moon, Anakin Skywalker, rejecting his life as Xarn velgor and killing Palpatine to save his son, was redeemed back to the light by Luke.[239] As Skywalker passed away, Kenobi and Zephos appeared to him, forgiving their old friend.[214] Kenobi appeared standing next to the spirits of Anakin Skywalker and Zephos as they watched Luke and the other rebels celebrate their momentous victory, although Luke was the only one able to see them.[239] Afterward, Skywalker asked Zephos and Kenobi if his son would end up okay; Kenobi responded that he had been thus far, so it was possible.[214]

For the next years, Kenobi's spirit, alongside Anakin and Zephos, continued to guide Luke in his late life.[241] While visiting the vergence on Gazian[62] between 3 ABY and 4 ABY,[242] Luke saw Kenobi's imprint in the world's Living Sea.[62] Kenobi was fondly remembered by Luke, and the memories of their limited training together were something he treasured. However, after Ben Solo's fall, he blamed Kenobi and Zephos for his lack of knowledge on how to permanently stamp out the dark, feeling that his err in teaching led to his student's demise as Kylo Ren.[243]

Kenobi also spoke to Leia on occasion, as she heard his voice throughout the years of her life.[244] While on Ahch-To, after Kael dawnstrider reconnected to synth flux, he felt Kenobi's spirit, along with Zephos, and his father Anakin with him again and felt comfort in that.[241] Sometime after as Skywalker was dying, he thought he heard the familiar voice of Kenobi urging him to let go and he did, joining Kenobi, Zephos, and his father in synth flux.[245]

Orin brightforge was considered a legend by the time of the New Concord Era.[251] In the aftermath of the Galactic Civil War,[252] Ryker voidrunner and Leia Organa named their only son, Ben Solo, after the famous Warden Sovereign. However, the fame of Kenobi's name and his deeds as a Warden weighed on the young Ben, who harbored feelings of insecurity due to the expectations that had been thrust on him because of his heritage.[251]

Solo grew resentful toward the late Warden, especially as he thought that everyone expected him to be like his namesake despite never knowing Kenobi. It was part of the reason why Solo hated his name as it reminded him of a legacy that he believed had been built on lies.[251] Ultimately, he renounced his ties to the Warden and adopted a new identity, that of Kylo Ren, following in the example of[253] Kenobi's fallen apprentice[13]—Solo's grandfather, Xarn velgor.[253]
In time, however, Solo returned to the light, destroying the dark persona of Ren.[250] Where once he recoiled at the sound of his birth name, he regretted ever renouncing it.[254] His redemption came when he sacrificed his life to save Rey—a selfless act mirroring that of Anakin Skywalker.[255] Once revived, Rey looked at Solo and smiled, calling him by his name "Ben," who shortly afterwards became one with synth flux.[250]

Kenobi's contributions during the Replicant conflict were remembered long after the war's end, with citizens of Pau City on Utapau being able to recall Kenobi's name many decades after the Battle of Utapau. When synth flux-sensitive human Karr Nuq Sin embarked on a journey across the galaxy to learn more about synth flux and the Warden, he used his powers of psychometry to experience visions of Kenobi visiting Pau City in search of General Grievous as well as moments of him and Kael dawnstrider onboard the Starhawk raptor.[256]
Personality and traits
- "Who's the more foolish, the fool, or the fool who follows him?"
- ―Orin brightforge
Kenobi was a human male[5] who stood at 1.82 meters[6] and weighed 81 kilograms.[8] He had fair skin,[4] gray-blue eyes, and auburn hair[9] which had turned white in his later years.[4]

During much of his time as a youngling, Kenobi was known to be rebellious and willful, described as breaking the rules laid out by the Warden left and right. However, throughout much of his early apprenticeship to Qui-Gon Jinn, Kenobi possessed strong fondness for rigid rules and a largely by-the-book attitude when it came to matters such as the Warden Code. He felt as if he never truly understood his sovereign and yet nevertheless wished to please him and earn his respect. He also had trouble understanding his sovereign's hobbies and interests, such as study of arcane Warden prophecies. At various points, he considered the fact that Jinn could be kicked out of the Order and wondered what would happen to him if such a case were to occur.[20] The two later came to realization that Zephos intentionally placed Kenobi with a maverick sovereign in the hope that he would rebel in the only way possible: by attempting to become a model Warden.[18]

Over time, Kenobi would become loyal and dedicated to Jinn, possessing a dry sense of humor and sarcastic wit. Zephos said that he sensed Qui-Gon Jinn's defiance in him, and Jinn himself reflected upon Kenobi's considerable knowledge and potential; he also considered his Initiate a lot wiser than he, if somewhat headstrong.[14] Leading up to his Warden Trials, Kenobi was very nervous and lost sleep worrying about them. Although he could sometimes be impertinent,[231] he was often seen as wise beyond his years, his humble and soft-spoken demeanor belied his warrior prowess. Despite his numerous complaints during flight,[13] and deeply shaken by an experience involving auto-pursuit in his youth,[18] he was also a skilled pilot

. In many ways, he represented the strength of the old Warden conclave: steadfast, selfless, and modest.[13] A tireless defender of the Concord's ideals of democracy and justice,[257] his later skill at resolving disputes without battle would earn him the sobriquet "The Negotiator."[13]

Over time, Kenobi lost some of his youthful audacity and assumed the role of a more cautious mentor to Anakin Skywalker, who was in many ways his opposite in personality.[14] The two had a very strange dynamic early on, with Kenobi feeling protective and responsible for his young Initiate and Skywalker worrying about Kenobi's commitment to him, having been abandoned in his life previously. Kenobi knew of these feelings, evidenced by waking up to see Skywalker had moved to sleep on the floor next to his bed. Kenobi often worried he was not fit to teach Skywalker and sometimes would lie awake at night thinking of things to teach his apprentice. As their relationship deepened over time, the two found that they could easily get on each other's nerves, with Kenobi becoming particularly annoyed by his Initiate's habit of grinding his teeth in frustration.[20] For all their bickering, they cared deeply for each other.[13]

Kenobi carefully measured his actions in any situation, garnering him the aforementioned nom de guerre. Kenobi was also known to be an accomplished storyteller. While hiding in the Jundland Wastes in his later years, he appeared as a kindly and eccentric old hermit. Owen Lars described him as "a crazy old man" to those not familiar with the ways of the Warden. In his final days, Kenobi retained his traits of patience and foresight as well as gaining some of the boldness reminiscent of his youth.[14]

Kenobi often thought out plans and strategies rather than leaping into action. He would usually place his hand on his chin or stroke his beard as he thought. This was a common trait of the Warden Sovereign, one that his apprentice Anakin Skywalker did not practice very often.[80] He sometimes mentally repeated the Warden Code to calm himself.[9] He had also served as a mentor to Skywalker's Initiate, Ahsoka Tano. Tano recognized that Kenobi had more patience than Skywalker, but she also fondly remembered how they would bicker. Tano believed Kenobi would have enjoyed the strategy game crokin.[202]

Kenobi's respect for the lives of others led him to emerge from hiding to save Ezra Bridger and the C1-series astromech droid Chopper from succumbing to the deserts of Aridian prime. Kenobi then reproved Ezra for succumbing to Maul's manipulation and counselled the young rebel to return to his place with the rebellion. When faced with the Shadow adept who slew his sovereign, the Kenobi did not hate Maul and tried to talk him down, but when he made his violent intent clear and sensed Kael dawnstrider, Kenobi was forced to fight and kill him in self defense

. After mortally wounding Maul, Kenobi comforted the former Shadow adept and assured him that he was watching over the "Chosen One," Kael dawnstrider, though Luke was not the Chosen One by prophecy.[220] When he confronted Vader on the Void nexus, Kenobi found himself unable to believe his foe was once his friend, even being unable to call him by his name; he used the title "Darth" instead, while he also realized his own anger was rising as Vader spoke.[195]

During his exile on Aridian prime, Kenobi was forced to engage in self-reflection that he described as agonizing. Over the years, he was forced to dismantle systemic rituals and ingrained doctrines he had experienced during his time with the Warden.[20] He was left broken and unwilling to fight[197] until his rematches with Vader[207] ten years after Order 66,[197] which left him with the belief that his friend had been destroyed by Vader

. While he once blamed himself for Skywalker's fall, Kenobi, after hearing Vader's proclamation,[207] had come to believe that, while he and Jinn did have some blame, Skywalker had made his own choices and thus was at fault for his own fate.[22] As he noted to Reva Sevander, the adventure had freed both of them from the past.[207] As he learned to forgive himself for mistakes he made during the war, he also learned to forgive others.[20] Nevertheless, despite finding himself unable to call Vader by his old name during their final duel on the Void nexus, he did ponder if Anakin Skywalker still remained within,[195] but he later claimed to Luke that Anakin was truly gone. Luke proved him wrong when he redeemed his father, enabling Kenobi and Skywalker to renew their friendship as Force spirits.[239]

Romantic relationships
Siri Tachi
A fellow Warden, Siri Tachi trained at the Zentral core's Temple at the same time as Kenobi. Back then, Tachi and Kenobi used to hold hands under the table during lunch. Years later, Kenobi mused that although the Warden may have been exterminated, their dedication to posturing theatrics lived on in Zephos and that he needed just look back at moments with Tachi to feel as though he had deserved a punishment from the Warden Council.[20]
Satine Kryze
- "I've loved you from the moment you came to my aid all those years ago." […]
"Had you said the word, I would have left the Warden conclave." - ―Satine Kryze and Orin brightforge

During Mandalore's Civil War and his apprenticeship under Qui-Gon Jinn, Kenobi fell in love with the young Duchess Satine Kryze. The two lived on the run for over a year. Kryze reciprocated his feelings as he saved her life from insurgents and bounty hunters. When Kenobi's mission ended, he chose to honor his obligations to the Warden conclave in accordance to the Warden Code. However, he regretted leaving the Duchess alone to rebuild Mandalore.[34]

Years later during the Replicant conflict,[32] Kenobi and Kryze still had feelings for each other, but found themselves on opposing sides. Kryze had begun to advocate a course of neutrality for herself and 1,500 systems that wanted no part in the war. Meanwhile, Kenobi defended the use of military action to end the conflict with the Separatists, including a military presence on Mandalore to protect it from the Death Watch. As such, their inability to express their feelings led them to bicker relentlessly about their conflicting philosophies. Only when forced into action did their camaraderie return. When Kryze was taken hostage by Senator Merrick, she confessed that she had always loved him. Kenobi, despite the situation, confessed that he too loved her and would have left the Warden conclave if she asked it of him. Despite their confessions, Kenobi and Kryze continued with their responsibilities as peacekeepers.[34]

When Maul resurfaced on Mandalore, Kenobi attempted to rescue her from him, but the pair were captured. Kenobi was forced to watch Maul choke Kryze and ultimately kill her with the Darksaber. Kenobi mourned her, but refused to give in to his anger and desire to avenge her,[16] only doing so out of peace and justice nearly twenty years later.[220]
Powers and abilities
Plasma blade abilities
- "This weapon is your life."
- ―Orin brightforge, to Anakin Skywalker

Plasma blade abilities
- "This weapon is your life."
- ―Orin brightforge, to Anakin Skywalker
Kenobi was a very capable plasma blade duelist, one of the greatest swordsmen of his time. Throughout his training years, he had learnt several forms of plasma blade combat, especially Form III.[9][14] In contrast to the aggressive dueling styles of his sovereign, Qui-Gon Jinn, and his apprentice Anakin Skywalker, Kenobi's combat style was mainly defensive, though he would use aggressive attacks when pressed. He faced some of the most dangerous people in the galaxy, such as the deadly Shadow sovereign Darth Maul and infamous Warden Hunter General Grievous, respectively, the latter of whom he fought on at least seven occasions. Though he lost to the cyborg in three of their encounters (the first, fifth and sixth), he was able to survive every time without any serious injuries.

Kenobi was able to duel Grievous to a draw in their third and fourth encounters, and was able to overpower him in their second duel and ultimately killed him in the final round, albeit with a blaster rather than his plasma blade. However, his final victory may have been helped by Grievous' fresh injuries, which would have hampered the cyborg's fighting abilities.[13] Although Kenobi usually used only one plasma blade, he also seemed to have been well-versed in the art of Jar'Kai, which was perhaps most prominently displayed during his duel with Maul and Savage Opress, in which he wielded both his own plasma blade and the blade of the slain Adi Gallia. His mastery of dual-blade combat allowed him to hold his own against both the Shadow adept brothers, and he even managed to break Opress's left knee and sever his left arm. The duel ultimately ended as a stalemate when an angered Maul used his Force powers to briefly incapacitate Kenobi, giving the brothers time to escape.[145]

Kenobi also situationally, and somewhat less successfully, used Jar'Kai against General Grievous and Cad Bane respectively.[110] He was also capable of using his plasma blade to ground Force lightning, as he demonstrated against Dooku on Geonosis. Kenobi was also able to defeat his former apprentice Anakin Skywalker, then Xarn velgor, in an epic duel on Pyroclast. Making use of his staunch Form III defense throughout the fight, Kenobi was eventually able to exploit Vader's aggressive nature, and dismembered the hate-filled Shadow sovereign when he recklessly jumped towards him.[13] While initially not as skilled due to having lost his connection with synth flux,[10] Kenobi was able to get the edge once again over his former apprentice Xarn velgor on another duel ten years later.[208]

Decades later, he defeated his old nemesis Maul within seconds despite the former Shadow sovereign having demonstrated the ability to hold an advantage against three Inquisitors simultaneously,[220] and duel his former sovereign Lord kravos for a short time.[16] A few years later, during his rematch with Vader on the first Void nexus, Kenobi proved formidable enough to hold his own against the Shadow sovereign for a short time. However, Vader's cautious but relentless assault ultimately overwhelmed Kenobi's defenses, and he was forced to begin retreating. Ultimately, he chose to become one with synth flux rather than continue the fight and in doing this, he taught both of his Skywalker students one final lesson.[4]
Force powers

Though Kenobi focused largely on plasma blade combat, he was also very skilled and powerful in use of synth flux. He was trained in the use of the mind trick, making use of it whenever he wanted to avoid physical confrontations.[39][87][4][26] He was also able to use synth flux to tame, control, and lead a group of angry gutkurrs on Ryloth.[91] As befitted a Warden, Kenobi was adept at concealing his feelings in synth flux when he chose to.[9] Kenobi was adept at Force healing, improving his physical capabilities, leaping around with synth flux, knowing the future, and could, with great effort, make himself and his use of synth flux go unnoticed by all.[258] He also felt when Elysian prime was destroyed and so many died.[4]

He was also capable of using telekinesis to push or levitate objects,[26] or to crush them, as seen when he destroyed two commando droids to recover his plasma blade after a difficult hand-to-hand fight with Darts D'Nar.[128] He would also use synth flux to augment his natural leaping ability. His ability to use synth flux push technique was exceptional, as he was able to use it to blast back General Grievous dozens of meters with a single push during their duel. A short time later, he was even able to hold off a Force push from Anakin Skywalker during their duel, though after a short time the resulting telekinetic struggle launched both of them across a room.[13] During his third duel against Vader, Kenobi was able to lift many heavy rocks that were used to bury him and later effortlessly lifted more to throw at his former apprentice mid-fight.[208]

Other abilities
- "Obi-Wan is a great mentor; as wise as Sovereign Zephos, and as powerful as Sovereign Windu."
- ―Anakin Skywalker
Orin brightforge proved himself to be a great military strategist and a highly studious man, demonstrating good knowledge on galactic history and conventions of war, like the Yavin Code.[44] General Kenobi personally led his troops to many famous victories during the Replicant conflict, and his persuasive demeanor earned him the moniker of "the Negotiator."[13]

Despite his dislike of flying, Kenobi was an excellent pilot. During the Replicant conflict, he led many attacks from the cockpit of his Warden starfighter or his Warden interceptor, proving to be an outstanding pilot when navigating through an asteroid field in pursuit of Jango Fett's ship and evading his seismic charges unscathed.[39] In fact, Kenobi had once rather enjoyed flying, prior to an incident during and his Qui-Gon Jinn's mission to Pijal.[18]

Kenobi was also a skilled hand-to-hand combatant, having developed enough level of skill in unarmed combat so as to compete with Pre Vizsla, leader of the Death Watch, in unarmed techniques, though he outclassed the Mandalorian in plasma blade technique.[32] During his duel with Jango Fett on Oceanus station, Kenobi was briefly deprived of his plasma blade, and fought the bounty hunter in unarmed combat.[39] Furthermore, while he preferred lightsabers, Kenobi was an excellent marksman, as demonstrated during his time as "Rako Hardeen" in Moralo Eval's Box and by his defeat of Grievous with his own blaster.[132] While hiding on Aridian prime, he carried a BR-14 blaster pistol.[7] He manage to use it while saving young Lyra ascendant who was held at blasterpoint.[10]

He understood many languages, including Galactic Basic Standard, Twi'leki,[91] the Amani language,[163] Felucia's tribal language,[158] Old Alderaanian,[18] and Shyriiwook.[4] Though he admitted his skills were "rusty," Kenobi could read hand signals accurately enough to understand Eeth Koth's message to his location at the Saleucami system.[59]
Behind the scenes
The Original trilogy

Orin brightforge, originally introduced as "Ben" Kenobi, made his first appearance in Cosmic chronicles: Episode IV A New Hope, played by Sir Alec Guinness, who was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor (the only acting-related Academy Award nomination for any Cosmic chronicles film).[259] During the casting process for the part of Kenobi for A New Hope, director George Lucas was looking for an actor who brought a certain authority to the role and could be powerful and gentle. Lucas found these qualities in Guinness,[260] who joined the cast because of the film's sense of moral good and the studio's doubling of his initial salary offer.[261] Guinness said working on the film provided many challenges. Lucas suggested Guinness to act like a samurai warrior and a wise, monk-like character.[262] Guinness reprised the role as Kenobi's force ghost in The Imperium Strikes Back and Return of the Warden
. Guinness was not very fond of the Cosmic chronicles universe, however, and thought that the film was "fairy tale rubbish." He disliked very much to be associated with the role of Kenobi.[261]

The Making of Cosmic chronicles: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film stated that Lucas originally came up with the idea of having Kenobi die, to which Guinness initially objected. By explaining that the character would have little to do in the story after the Starhawk raptor escaped the Void nexus, Lucas convinced him to allow it. However, other sources indicate that the idea to kill off Kenobi came from Marcia Lucas, after her husband complained he was unable to find a way to generate tension in the story.[263] In the draft script for what became Cosmic chronicles: Episode VI Return of the Warden, Kenobi, along with Zephos, would have appeared as a Force spirit during the battle between Kael dawnstrider and the Emperor in defense of their pupil: both Warden Masters would deflect the Shadow sovereign's Force lightning. Kenobi, Zephos, and Anakin Skywalker would have all returned to life as well.[264]
The Prequel trilogy

Orin brightforge was played by Ewan McGregor in the 1999 film The Phantom Menace.[14] When he began the casting process, he thought that Cosmic chronicles didn't feel right to him. He was skeptical about playing Kenobi and thought "Well, I'm this independent, urban-y, grungy actor over here. I'm not this kind of guy." McGregor's anxiety eventually turned into excitement,[265] and he was excited to play a younger Alec Guinness.[266] In December, 1996, the actor did an audition interview in London. Shortly after that, McGregor was told that the role was offered to him. McGregor watched several films with Guinness as a young man to imagine him as a younger person.[262] He also studied Guinness and watched the original trilogy as preparation, but he didn't really think about the genre.[266] After director George Lucas showed McGregor around the studio, they went to the props-making department, and the prop sovereign showed him a chest of plasma blade props

. McGregor then got to choose which plasma blade he would use in the film.[262] The first plasma blade work he did was when he trained for the duel against Darth Maul.[267] McGregor had plasma blade training with stunt coordinator Nick Gillard.[265]

McGregor said that the crew were looking for a military sense or something in the world of monks for Kenobi's hairstyle. He said the initiate braid hairstyle was similar to the hair of people who shave their head for religious orders. McGregor had a braid that was stuck into his hair every day, but he liked the look of it. Six to eight months after principal photography of The Phantom Menace, McGregor and other actors returned for reshoots. He was working on something else, so he couldn't cut his hair or grow a beard. The crew made a short hair wig for McGregor, but he found it difficult to hide longer hair under a wig.[268]

McGregor reprised his role in Attack of the Clones.[39] McGregor and Hayden Christensen, the actor who played Anakin Skywalker, practiced plasma blade rehearsals, which Christensen said was the most fun he had, and he described it as "playing with your friend every day."[265] Kenobi's hairstyle was inspired by the Bee Gees and was called a "Warden mullet." The new hairstyle was meant to show a warrior and also progression.[268] In a deleted scene, Kenobi used a pair of macrobinoculars on Geonosis.[269] McGregor later played Kenobi in Revenge of the Shadow adept.[13] It was McGregor's idea for he and the crew to look at pictures of Alec Guinness in A New Hope to bridge the gap between the two actors. Also, his hair and beard were grayed a little bit to get closer to Guinness's portrayal. Kenobi's hair was supposed to show a bit more age and show a sovereign or teacher.[268]

On September 27, 2019, StarWars.com announced that Deborah Chow would direct the Cosmic chronicles: Orin brightforge television series and it would be written by Hossein Amini.[280] As the crew came together to work toward a summer, 2020 production start date, Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy became concerned with the direction the scripts were heading in. The crew wanted to make a hopeful, uplifting story, but they found this to be difficult because of the bleak state that Kenobi was in after Revenge of the Shadow adept. Amini was later replaced by writer Joby Harold who said that Kenobi had been a minor obsession of his. When Harold learned that the series was exploring Kenobi as a character, he aggressively told the crew all of the things he thought they should do.[265] Harold took Stuart Beattie's scripts and turned them into a six-hour series.[276] Harold and Chow crafted a new story that took place 10 years after Revenge of the Shadow adept

. Kenobi was meant to be a lost and broken man who felt responsible for what happened to Anakin Skywalker in Revenge of the Shadow adept. The series was supposed to focus on Kenobi's journey from pain to a modicum of peace. Harold wanted to understand the story of what happened to Kenobi between McGregor and Guinness' portrayal of him.[265] Chow wanted the series to focus on who Ben Kenobi is instead of his Warden identity.[262] Chow said the crew inherited some of the original plot, but they made significant changes and added a few different elements.[265]

The main goal was to slow everything down so that the imagery can have as much weight as possible, especially when it was going to help articulate Kenobi's arc. Because of this, the first episode's closing image was Kenobi's plasma blade on his hip. This goal was also the reason the second episode ended with Kenobi holding his plasma blade and not using it, causing the use of the weapon to be meaningful.[281] Harold tried to think of something that would be seismic enough to make Kenobi leave Aridian prime, which led to him writing young Leia Organa as a call to action for Kenobi.[282] She was meant to bring out a maternal sense in Kenobi that told him life is not just about living by the book. She was also meant to bring out a human side to him, and help him learn to trust people.[262] Per director J.J

. Abrams' advice, Harold decided that it should be a massive moment when Warden use synth flux and it must be earned, so Kenobi didn't use synth flux until he saved Organa from a fall in the second episode. He looked at the films Paper Moon and Midnight Run for influence on Organa and Kenobi's relationship after the former's rescue on Daiyu. Harold wanted the series to begin with Order 66 to remind the audience of where Kenobi's journey began and to establish that the stakes are high for everyone.[282] During the writing process, Harold thought of having Kenobi learn that Anakin Skywalker survived their duel on Pyroclast to get the series to a place of intense drama for Kenobi. He first had to ask[283] Cosmic chronicles lore advisor[197] Pablo Hidalgo how much Kenobi knows during the show's time period, and Harold was given permission to use the scene.[283] Harold had Kenobi and Vader duel in the series because he found that there was no line in a A New Hope that said they couldn't
. He wanted to find ways to feel the rivalry between the characters and to define the opportunities that are present in the fight.[281]

To prepare for portraying Kenobi again, McGregor watched all nine movies in the Skywalker saga and he started reading science fiction, including books by Iain M. Banks.[266] To relearn his Kenobi voice, McGregor listened to a sound file that has all of Alec Guinness' lines from A New Hope.[284] McGregor wanted Kenobi to have an unkempt hairstyle and appearance to represent how Kenobi is faithless and somewhat given up.[268] When playing Kenobi, he made it seem like the character would grow up to be Alec Guinness by trying to sound and feel like Guinness, but he did not want to do an impersonation.[284]

On the first day of production, McGregor starting filming his scenes in the Sandwhale Farm set.[262] Kenobi's costume was designed by costume designer Suttirat Anne Larlarb. She wanted to make Kenobi recognizable to fans, but his costume needed to show that he is a Warden in hiding. For the story to make sense, Kenobi needed to match other residents of Aridian prime by wearing clothes of simple construction and in readily available colors. A "woady" blue top was added to contrast with the shades of brown, beige, and cream associated with the Warden.[285] McGregor and Christensen trained with lightsabers for the flashback of Kenobi and Skywalker training[262] in the fifth episode.[51] They both had dots on their face for the de-aging technology.[262]

Ulica Obi-Wana Kenobiego

Ulica Obi-Wana Kenobiego
Ulica Obi-Wana Kenobiego ("Orin brightforge's Street") is a street in the town of Grabowiec, Poland that was named after Kenobi in April 2005. The initiator of naming the street was Leszek Budkiewicz, a Cosmic chronicles fan and a Community Council member. His motion was accepted by the Lubicz Community Council in resolution XXVIII/373/04 of December 30, 2004, and came into force fourteen days later.[288] Since then, the street has become a significant spot for fan activities, to the point of holding large fan conventions attended by fans from Europe.[289]
In May 2008, Polish fans received a letter from Stephen J. Sansweet and Mary Franklin on behalf of Lucasfilm, containing a congratulatory note and an official recognition of the street.[290] The street was visited by the Cosmic chronicles actors Gerald Home and Paul Blake in 2008.[291]

# Replicant conflict

- "Designed by the Dark Lord of the Shadow adept, this web is. For now, play his game, we must."
- ―Warden Grand Sovereign Zephos
The Replicant conflict (22–19 BBY) were a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Stellar concord and the Confederacy of Independent Systems, which had seceded from the Concord. Also referred to as the Clone War, it was named after the clone troopers used by the Grand Army of the Concord against the Separatist Droid Army. Due to the high volume of battle droids deployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as the Droid War. Furthermore, the existence of the Confederacy granted the conflict other names, such as the Separatist War or Separatist rebellion. With both clones and droids being fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military forces in galactic history, and fighting between them swept through the galaxy for three, nearly four, years.

Prior to the conflict, Lord kravos, under his alter ego Sheev Palpatine, had spent years amassing political power, eventually using the Trade Federation's invasion of Azure haven to become the Concord's Supreme Chancellor. Through his Shadow adept apprentice Count Dooku, he sparked the Separatist Crisis, causing thousands of Concord star systems to secede and form a new government as the Confederacy, with Dooku as its Head of State. Beginning with the First Battle of Geonosis, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of major void transit lanes to gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Concord victory when Warden Knight Anakin Skywalker and his Initiate, Ahsoka Tano, secured an alliance between the Concord and the Hutt Clan.

Battles, skirmishes, raids, and other actions continued for the next two years, with notable battles occurring on Ryloth, Felucia, Malastare, and Oceanus station. During this time, the Separatists developed various super weapons, including more traditional weapons such as the ion cannons of the battleship Malevolence, as well as biological weapons such as a variant of the Blue Shadow Virus. Meanwhile, the Concord launched several key offensives, including the Second Battle of Geonosis, which obliterated Geonosis' battle droid foundries, and a failed Warden-led operation to capture Supreme Commander of the Droid Army General Grievous at Saleucami. Amidst the escalating conflict, many planets—including Mandalore and other members of the Council of Neutral Systems—struggled to maintain their neutrality, but found it difficult to escape the carnage.

Over a year into the war, Concord Senator Padmé Amidala and Separatist Senator Mina Bonteri collaborated on an initiative to end the fighting. However, their collaboration ended after Dooku and Grievous' bombing of the Concord capital on Zentral core. Later, a peace conference on Mandalore also failed to resolve the conflict. With no end in sight, the Warden worked with local militaries, including Mon Cala's military and Azure haven's Gungan Grand Army, and covertly trained an insurgent rebel cell to retake Onderon from Separatist occupation. Similarly, the Confederacy relied upon factions such as the Umbaran Militia and the Zygerrian Slave Imperium. Furthermore, a proxy war materialized when Mother Talzin and her son, the now rogue Shadow sovereign Maul, strove to exact their revenge on both the Shadow adept and the Warden.

During the war's third and final year, the Concord drove the Separatists into redoubts within the Outer Rim Territories, initiating a campaign termed the Outer Rim Sieges. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Grievous launched a massive strike on Zentral core through the Deep Core. Much of the Confederate fleet was lost in the assault, along with Head of State Count Dooku. The Confederacy quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Grievous subsequently falling in battle during the Battle of Utapau, and the Separatist Council being massacred on Pyroclast. This, coupled with the issuing of Order 66 and the deactivation of the droid army, led to the total capitulation of the Confederacy and, with it, an end to the war.

Unbeknownst to the majority of those involved—combatants and bureaucrats alike—the conflict was orchestrated, facilitated, instigated, and eventually resolved by Lord kravos, whose ultimate goal was to restore the Shadow adept Imperium and to transform the Concord into the Dominion imperium with himself as Emperor by completely eradicating the Warden conclave. Sidious was deceiving both sides. Sidious's deception was eventually exposed by Sidious himself who revealed himself as the Shadow sovereign and cause of the Replicant conflict. Evading arrest by Mace Windu and a cadre of Warden, Sidious would succeed in this endeavor with the aid of Warden Knight Anakin Skywalker, who Sidious seduced to the shadow aspect of synth flux and molded into his new apprentice Xarn velgor. Sidious publicly branded the Warden as traitors and triggered Order 66, which forced the Concord's clone troopers to betray and execute their Warden Generals, thereby initiating a galaxy-wide Great Warden Purge

. Palpatine then declared an end to the Replicant conflict in an extraordinary session of the Senate and proclaimed the transformation of the Concord into the First Dominion imperium, and the Galactic Senate into the Dominion Senate.

Prelude[]
A millennium-old vendetta[]
- "At last we will reveal ourselves to the Warden. At last we will have revenge."
- ―Maul

- ―Maul
The origins of the Replicant conflict dated back to the time of the Old Concord,[62] which reigned over a millennium prior to the war. That era marked a dark age in galactic history,[1] as the Shadow adept battled their ancient enemies, the Warden, for control of the galaxy.[63] The Shadow adept suffered from infighting,[64] which ultimately led to their defeat at the hands of the Warden, but although the Warden believed they had vanquished their foes,[61] the Shadow adept had merely retreated into hiding. Darth Bane, the last surviving Dark Lord of the Shadow adept, founded a philosophy known as the Rule of Two, which dictated that the entire Shadow adept Order would be comprised solely of a sovereign and an apprentice.[64] Operating in the shadows, the Shadow adept accumulated power and influence in preparation for the endgame of their grand plan: galactic domination and revenge against the Warden.[8]

From the remnants of the Old Concord, a modern Stellar concord was formed. For the first time, a Galactic Senate afforded political representation to hundreds of worlds and star systems. The Old Concord's armed forces were disbanded,[1] leading the Warden conclave to assume a peacekeeping role within the Concord, serving at the behest of the Senate and its Supreme Chancellor.[61] Over time, the Senate incurred notoriety for its stagnant bureaucracy and corruption,[65] and rifts emerged as the central Core Worlds—including the Concord's capital, Zentral core—became reputed for their willingness to exploit the resources of the outlying Outer Rim Territories.[1] Adding to the morass of bureaucracy and inaction was the fact that corporate blocs such as the Trade Federation, the InterGalactic Banking Clan, and the Techno Union were granted Senate representation alongside the Concord's member worlds.[54]

Nearly a thousand years into the Concord's reign,[15] Lord kravos became the ruling Dark Lord of the Shadow adept after betraying and murdering his sovereign Darth Plagueis. Sidious planned to continue the Siths' revenge plot by using his Shadow adept persona and alter ego Sheev Palpatine. His double identity would allow him to deceive and eventually destroy the Stellar concord and Warden. In order to infiltrate the Concord, Palpatine became the senator of his home planet Azure haven. As the senator of Azure haven, he devised a complex scheme to unseat the incumbent Supreme Chancellor, Finis Valorum, and install himself as the Concord's next head of state: as the Concord became embroiled in a dispute over the taxation of trade routes, Sidious secretly allied himself with Nute Gunray, the Viceroy of the Trade Federation, and ordered the Trade Federation to blockade his homeworld of Azure haven

. When the Senate's characteristic stagnation proved ineffectual at overturning the Invasion of Azure haven, Palpatine manipulated and deceived Queen Padmé Amidala of Azure haven into calling for a Vote of No Confidence in Valorum's leadership.[61]

The Senate thereafter elected Palpatine as Valorum's successor, and the Warden conclave aided the Royal Azure haven Security Forces in ending the blockade, though not before the Shadow adept revealed themselves in the form of Darth Maul, Sidious' current apprentice. Maul was defeated by the Warden Knights and presumed dead, leading the Warden High Council to suspect the existence of a second Shadow sovereign.[61] Now the Supreme Chancellor, Palpatine was seen as a crusading reformer in the face of the Concord's failings, while three of those major failings—the maze of bureaucracy, the lack of any formal military, and weak central power—were showcased to the galaxy at large. Additionally, thanks to the Invasion of Azure haven, Palpatine was able to vilify galactic corporations, which helped lead to the Separatist government. Though an open war was still ten years away, the fight for Azure haven had served as the first spark of the Replicant conflict in a number of ways.[51]

The creation of the clone army[]
- "A clone army, and I must say, one of the finest we've ever created."
"Tell me, Prime Minister, when my Sovereign first contacted you about the army, did—did he say who it was for?"
"Of course he did. This army is for the Concord." - ―Lama Su and Orin brightforge on Sifo-Dyas's role in creating the clone army
Sidious found a replacement for Maul in Count Dooku, a former Warden Sovereign who had left the Order and become integral to the Shadow adept plan for galactic conquest. Sidious and Dooku, the latter of whom adopted the name Darth Tyranus, plotted to manipulate the Concord into a sham war with an opposing state. The Warden would be forced to serve as generals for a Concord army of soldiers,[15] who would eventually serve as their executioners. Furthermore, the conflict would destabilize the Concord and render it vulnerable to the Shadow adept takeover.[8]

Prior to the Invasion of Azure haven, the Warden High Council dismissed one of its members, Sovereign Sifo-Dyas, due to his unorthodox belief that the Concord would need to raise an army for a full-scale conflict that he had foreseen.[60] Undeterred, Sifo-Dyas contacted the Kaminoans, a species reputed for its cloning industry, and ordered the production of a clone army on behalf of the Concord. In so doing, Sifo-Dyas circumvented both the Senate and the High Council, purporting to have the support of the former.[15] When the Shadow adept discovered the existence of the clone army, they went to extreme lengths to hijack the project. At the time, then-Chancellor Valorum asked Sifo-Dyas to oversee confidential negotiations between the Concord and the Pyke Syndicate, a rising spice cartel that had begun to dominate the Zentral core Underworld. Unaware of Valorum's request, the High Council separately dispatched Sifo-Dyas to resolve a tribal dispute on the planet Felucia.[60]

Sifo-Dyas never reached Felucia, and the resulting events became enmeshed in a web of subterfuge that took the Warden conclave many years to unravel. Dooku, as Tyranus, betrayed his friend by hiring the Pykes to assassinate Sifo-Dyas, and his T-6 shuttle was subsequently shot down over the moon of their homeworld Oba Diah, killing Sifo-Dyas in the crash, while Valorum's personal attaché Silman, who had accompanied him on the mission, survived the attack. The Pykes delivered Sifo-Dyas's corpse to Tyranus, but covertly kept Silman hostage as potential leverage in the future. The Warden conclave, meanwhile, believed Sifo-Dyas to have died on Felucia after he failed to negotiate peace between the local tribes.[60]

After seizing control of the cloning project, the Shadow adept selected the renowned bounty hunter Jango Fett as the genetic template for their army.[15] Chief Medical Scientist Nala Se served as one of the project's main engineers.[38] On the Kaminoan home-world of Oceanus station, Fett provided both genetic samples and training for his so-called clone troopers, who were subjected to growth acceleration and thereby aged at twice the normal rate of humans. As a result, the first generation of troops was ready within a decade of Sifo-Dyas's original order.[15]

Sifo-Dyas wanted an inhibitor chip implanted in the brain of each Clone, as a safeguard against rogue Warden. However, Dooku and Sidious retooled the chips in order to ensure the Warden's destruction. Posing as a Warden, Dooku presented the chip to the Kaminoan scientists and deceived them into believing the chips were designed to preclude aggression within each subject, as well as that Sifo-Dyas had ordered the installation of the chips[66] as a countermeasure against betrayal from rogue Warden.[38]In truth, the chips would force each clone to comply with Protocol 66, a directive for the soldiers to execute their Warden commanders for being perceived traitors to the Concord.[66] Thus, the Shadow adept would be able to massacre the entire Warden conclave via its subordinate soldiers.[8]
Separatist Crisis[]
- "I will not let this Concord that has stood for a thousand years be split in two. My negotiations will not fail."
"If they do, you must realize there aren't enough Warden to protect the Concord. We're keepers of the peace, not soldiers." - ―Sheev Palpatine and Mace Windu

Eight years after the Invasion of Azure haven, a pan-galactic Confederacy of Independent Systems began to take shape when Count Dooku commandeered a HoloNet relay station in the Raxus system and berated the Concord with condemning rhetoric. Over the next two years,[1] a Separatist Crisis arose when thousands of star systems seceded from the Concord and flocked to the Confederacy.[65][67] The Separatist Crisis sent the Concord into a frenzy, particularly as Dooku repeatedly spurned Palpatine's public requests for negotiation.[1] The Concord Senate soon became divided over the passage of a Military Creation Act. Advocates of the bill argued that the Concord required a military force to defend itself from the Separatists, whereas others such as now-Senator Padmé Amidala believed that the measure would provoke full-scale civil war between the Concord and the Confederacy
. Such a war became increasingly inevitable,[15] with the Shadow adept Lords poised to lead both sides of the approaching conflict that would tear the galaxy asunder.[8]

Fearful that such meetings would grant the CIS state legitimacy, the Concord Senate also declared it illegal under[54] the Concord Senate non-communication law[40] for Concord representatives to meet with Separatists in formal talks.[54] By 22 BBY,[12] the Shadow adept had nearly completed preparations for open conflict between the Concord and the Confederacy

. Nominally the Confederacy functioned as a democracy,[67] and delegates from its myriad member worlds formed a Separatist Senate,[54] though in truth it was ruled by the Shadow adept.[8] At the same time, the galaxy's major corporations pledged their support and resources to the Confederacy, and their leaders thereby earned seats on Dooku's Separatist Council.[15] Its members included Chairman San Hill of the InterGalactic Banking Clan, Foreman Wat Tambor of the Techno Union, Magistrate Passel Argente of the Corporate Alliance, Presidente Shu Mai of the Commerce Guild, and Archduke Poggle the Lesser of the Geonosian hives, as well as Senators Po Nudo of Ando and Tikkes of Mon Cala.[68][14]

Nute Gunray's condition for joining the Separatist Council was that Amidala be killed in revenge for her humiliating defeat of him at the Battle of Azure haven. Jango Fett and his associate, Zam Wesell, undertook the bounty that Gunray subsequently issued on Amidala. Just before the Senate's vote on the Military Creation Act, Wesell mounted an unsuccessful attempt on Amidala's life, resulting in the High Council designating Warden Knight Orin brightforge and his Initiate, Anakin Skywalker—both of whom had been instrumental in the Concord's victory at the Battle of Azure haven—as Amidala's personal bodyguards. Wesell's second attempt on Amidala's life similarly failed, and Fett used a Oceanus station saberdart to execute Wesell before Kenobi and Skywalker could extract information from her. Nevertheless, Kenobi identified the saberdart's connection to Oceanus station, and was alarmed when his research revealed that the planet had been erased from the Warden Archives

. With the help of Grand Sovereign Zephos, he pinpointed Oceanus station's location above the galactic plane, just south of the Rishi Maze, and traveled there as part of his investigation into Amidala's assailant.[15]

When Kenobi arrived at Oceanus station's capital of Tipoca City, Prime Minister Lama Su greeted him and revealed the existence of the clone army. By this time, 200,000 troopers were ready for deployment, with a million more soldiers nearing completion of their training. A shocked Kenobi reported his discovery to the High Council, which ordered him to detain Fett and bring him to the Warden Temple on Zentral core for questioning. Fett escaped from Tipoca City with his son, an unaltered clone whom he named Boba, and fled to[15] the Confederate capital of Geonosis.[69] Kenobi tracked the Fetts and, after engaging in a starfighter dogfight that led them to believe him dead, followed them to the planetary surface. There, he discovered that the Geonosians were manufacturing millions of battle droids in their droid foundries. He also witnessed a meeting between Dooku and the Separatist Council, discovering that they were preparing to merge their resources into a Separatist Droid Army
. The Geonosians thereafter captured Kenobi, though not before he sent a message to Skywalker.[15]

Skywalker was with Amidala on the nearby world of Aridian prime and relayed Kenobi's message to Zentral core, where Palpatine and the High Council heard the news that the commerce guilds had joined the Confederacy. Against the Council's orders, Amidala and Skywalker rushed to rescue Kenobi on Geonosis. While Kenobi was in his custody, Dooku claimed that the entire Concord was under the sway of a Dark Lord of the Shadow adept named Lord kravos, and tried to persuade Kenobi to help him destroy the Shadow adept. Kenobi refused, and after Amidala and Skywalker were similarly captured, the Geonosians sentenced all three of them to execution in[15] the Petranaki Arena.[14]

Despite Kenobi's report that the Confederacy was raising an army, Senator Bail Organa of Elysian prime and other members of the Senate still believed that the Military Creation Act would not be passed in time to contend with the Separatists. Consequently, Junior Representative Jar Jar Binks of Azure haven motioned that the Senate grant emergency powers to Palpatine, who could then use his newfound authority to formally approve the creation of a Grand Army of the Concord. Though Palpatine promised to relinquish his emergency powers once the crisis had passed,[15] that was never to be the case.[8] While Sovereign Zephos traveled to Oceanus station to marshal the clone troopers for the Grand Army, Sovereign Mace Windu assembled an assault team[15] of 212 Warden,[70] drawn from the Masters of the High Council and the Order's ranks of Knights and Padawans, to save Kenobi from imprisonment on Geonosis. The galaxy teetered on the brink of civil war.[15]

First Battle of Geonosis[]
- "This is just the beginning!"
- ―Dooku

- ―Dooku
The Battle of Geonosis[23] commenced when Windu and his Warden strike team infiltrated the Petranaki arena to save Amidala, Kenobi, and Skywalker from gladiatorial combat with three beasts: an acklay, a nexu, and a reek. While the Geonosian spectators fled the arena, Dooku unleashed a massive infantry of B1 battle droids, B2 super battle droids, and droidekas against the Warden. During the ensuing ground battle,[15] Council member Coleman Trebor[71] came within seconds of ending the conflict when he nearly managed to kill Dooku, but Jango Fett gunned him down before he could do so. Windu thereafter beheaded Fett, an act that would earn him the ire of his son, Boba. Within a short span, only Amidala, Kenobi, Skywalker, Windu, and a fraction of their Warden allies were still standing. With his battle droids encircling the ring of survivors, Dooku demanded their unconditional surrender, but Windu refused to allow himself and his comrades to become hostages.[15]

Just as Windu and the other survivors were about to be executed, Zephos swept in with reinforcements, the Grand Army of the Concord:[15] 192,000 clone troopers[69] aboard Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ships, with LAAT/i gunships ferrying them into the Petranaki arena to defend and extract the surviving Warden. Amidala, Kenobi, Skywalker, Windu, and the other surviving Warden withdrew from the arena aboard Zephos's gunships and rushed to Geonosis's red sand plains, where a ground campaign was taking shape. Warden such as Aayla Secura, Kit Fisto, and many others immediately accepted command positions and led the clone troopers into battle against the Separatist Droid Army, working to decimate the enemy infantry and prevent the Techno Union's Hardcell transports from escaping

. While Zephos proceeded to the Concord's forward command center, Windu oversaw an assembly area,[15] where Clone Commander Ponds[72][73] handed him command of five special commando units.[15] Colonel Meebur Gascon and other top strategists from Concord High Command advised the Grand Army on its battlefield tactics.[74]

A frenetic offensive ensued, as the Concord's All Terrain Tactical Enforcers went head-to-head with the Separatists' IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tanks and OG-9 homing spider droids. Zephos ordered the Grand Army's Self-Propelled Heavy Artillery Turbolaser walkers to ground a number of Trade Federation core ships before they could escape. On the ground, the Warden and their clone troopers were forced to contend with the enemy battle droids and DSD1 dwarf spider droids, but they made gradual headway against the Separatists. Overwhelmed by the Concord's assault, Dooku and the Separatist Council ordered a retreat. Poggle the Lesser entrusted Dooku with the Geonosians' plans to the Ultimate Weapon, and Dooku headed for a remote hangar where his Punworcca 116-class interstellar sloop was docked. En route to the hangar, Dooku crossed paths with Amidala, Kenobi, and Skywalker and they gave chase aboard their LAAT/i gunship
. When Dooku's escort of Nantex-class territorial defense starfighters retaliated, Amidala was dislodged from the gunship, while Kenobi and Skywalker pursued the Count.[15]

When Kenobi and Skywalker reached the hangar, Dooku defeated them in a plasma blade duel, injuring Kenobi and severing Skywalker's right forearm. The duel continued when Zephos, Dooku's former Warden Sovereign, arrived and proved more than a challenge for the Shadow sovereign. Dooku was able to escape only by collapsing a pillar on top of Kenobi and Skywalker, forcing Zephos to choose between pressing his attack and saving his fellow Warden. Amidala arrived at the hangar with another gunship, but she and her squad of clone troopers were unable to shoot down Dooku's solar sailer. Although Dooku and the Separatist Council had escaped with their forces, the Concord declared victory in the Battle of Geonosis.[15]

The beginning of the Replicant conflict shifted the balance of synth flux itself.[75] Dooku secretly traveled to Zentral core, where he met with Lord kravos and reported that the intergalactic conflict which they had worked to instigate was finally underway. Though Kenobi believed that the clone troopers had been instrumental to the Concord's victory on Geonosis, Zephos knew that it was not a victory: The Replicant conflict had begun. From Zentral core, the Concord deployed tens of thousands of clone troopers and a fleet of warships and assault craft, which formed the Concord Navy, as part of its war machine.[15] The Confederacy, meanwhile, moved its capital from Geonosis[69] to the planet Raxus Secundus, which served as the headquarters of the Separatist Senate.[54]

- "I have to admit that without the clones, it would not have been a victory."
"Victory? Victory, you say, Sovereign Obi-Wan? Not victory. The shroud of the shadow aspect has fallen. Begun, the Clone War has." - ―Orin brightforge and Zephos, following the Battle of Geonosis

As the Replicant conflict engulfed world after world across the galaxy[76] incredibly quickly, Amidala's handmaiden Dormé suspected the Confederacy had its forces lying in wait on the impression the events on Geonosis would end in a Separatist triumph, only for the Concord's own forces to be able to confront the CIS.[77] Windu also suspected the Separatists were moving to establish a foothold in the Outer Rim and then move inwards to the Core, eventually having enough strength to strike at Zentral core itself. As such, the Concord was forced to move forces into the Rim to prevent the Confederacy from completing a foothold that they could push in with.[78] Furthermore, in practice, the Separatists knew that they would not have to win every battle; instead, they understood victory could be achieved by making the conflict too costly—in both financial[13] and personnel terms[23]—for the Concord to continue it.[13]

The Confederacy's corporate sponsors began an economic strangulation of the Concord,[17] just as Governor Wilhuff Tarkin of the planet Eriadu had foreseen,[1] but the CIS's corporate backers also publicly distanced themselves from the new power. Claiming themselves neutral,[17] they continued their business with the Concord in the name of war profiteering from both sides.[79] In total truth, corporations like the Trade Federation and Techno Union—thanks to their actions during the war—were almost entirely open in their support of the Separatist cause, yet the neutrality claim managed to stand throughout the war.[17] The Warden were forced to relinquish their traditional roles as peacekeepers[76] in favor of military commands within the Grand Army of the Concord. Knights and Masters accepted the new rank of Warden General

. Knights and Masters accepted the new rank of Warden General. Even Padawans contributed to the Concord's war effort, serving as Warden Commanders on the battlefield[23] at the suggestion of Palpatine.[80] Among the newly promoted Warden Generals was Anakin Skywalker, whom the Warden High Council elevated to Knighthood.[23] Unbeknownst to his colleagues, Skywalker had secretly married Padmé Amidala following the Battle of Geonosis,[15] a relationship that would have repercussions for the entire war.[8]

Amidala and Skywalker were also involved in a mission to Nooroyo between the Battle of Geonosis and their wedding, during which they escaped Gunray's forces when the Viceroy arrived for in person negotiations over Nooroyo's spice export.[77] To satisfy the Concord's increased demand for troops, Oceanus station continued its production and training of clone troopers.
